articles.title: Some aspect has rectangular circuit exponent two
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, there is a real
$k \ge 0$ at which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model
over $F$ equals $2$. Hence the set of such $k$, viewed in $[0, \infty]$, whose supremum is the dual
matrix multiplication exponent, is nonempty.

articles.title: Upper bounds for the dual circuit exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $K \in [0, \infty]$.
If $k \le K$ for every real $k \ge 0$ at which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of
the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ equals $2$, then the dual matrix multiplication exponent
$\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\alpha(F) \le K$.

articles.title: Dual matrix multiplication exponent (arithmetic circuits)
articles.statement:
For a field $F$, the dual
matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F) \in [0, \infty]$ of the arithmetic-circuit model is the
supremum of all real $k \ge 0$ at which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the
arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ equals $2$.

articles.title: Exponents above the circuit exponent are admissible
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $k, w$ real
numbers with $w > 0$. If the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit
model over $F$ at aspect $k$ is less than $w$, then $w$ is an admissible exponent at aspect $k$
over $F$.

articles.title: Exponent two is admissible at aspect zero
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the exponent $2$ is an
admissible rectangular circuit exponent at aspect $0$ over $F$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there
are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic
circuit over $F$ computes the product of an $n \times \lceil n^0 \rceil$ matrix and a
$\lceil n^0 \rceil \times n$ matrix, that is of an $n \times 1$ matrix and a $1 \times n$ matrix,
with at most $C n^{2 + \varepsilon}$ gates.

The outer-product circuit, with $n^2$ gates, is such a circuit.

articles.title: Admissible rectangular circuit exponents
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $k, w$ real numbers. The
exponent $w$ is admissible at aspect $k$ over $F$ when $k \ge 0$, $w \ge 0$, and for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that for every
$n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ computes the product of an $n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$
matrix and an $\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix with at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ gates.

The circuit may depend on $n$ and $\varepsilon$, and it must be correct on every pair of matrices
with entries in $F$.

articles.title: Circuits that compute the matrix product
articles.statement:
A circuit $c$ over a field $F$ whose inputs are
the entries of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix computes matrix multiplication
when, for all matrices $A \in F^{m \times r}$ and $B \in F^{r \times n}$ and all $i < m$, $j < n$,
its output at $(i, j)$ on the entries of $A$ and $B$ equals $(AB)_{ij}$.

Correctness is required on actual values in $F$, not as an identity of formal polynomials.

articles.title: Aspects with circuit exponent two bound the dual exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $k \ge 0$
a real number. If the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model
over $F$ at aspect $k$ equals $2$, then $k \le \alpha(F)$, where $\alpha(F)$ is the dual matrix
multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model.

articles.title: Lower bounds for the rectangular circuit exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $k$ a real number
and $W \in [0, \infty]$. If $W \le w$ for every real $w$ that is an admissible exponent at aspect
$k$ over $F$, then $W$ is at most the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the
arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ at aspect $k$.

articles.title: Matrix arithmetic circuit
articles.statement:
For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, r, n \in \mathbb{N}$, a matrix
arithmetic circuit is an arithmetic circuit over $F$ whose inputs are indexed by the entries
$(i, k)$ of an $m \times r$ matrix together with the entries $(k, j)$ of an $r \times n$ matrix,
and whose outputs are indexed by the entries $(i, j)$ of an $m \times n$ matrix.

articles.title: Matrix input assignment
articles.statement:
For matrices $A \in F^{m \times r}$ and $B \in F^{r \times n}$,
the input assignment of $(A, B)$ is the function on the entry positions $(i, k)$ of an
$m \times r$ matrix together with the entry positions $(k, j)$ of an $r \times n$ matrix that
sends $(i, k)$ to $A_{ik}$ and $(k, j)$ to $B_{kj}$. It supplies the inputs of a matrix
arithmetic circuit.

articles.title: Admissible circuit exponents are upward closed
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $k, w, w'$ real
numbers with $w \le w'$. If $w$ is an admissible exponent at aspect $k$ over $F$, then so is
$w'$.

articles.title: The outer-product matrix circuit computes the matrix product
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and all
$m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit over $F$ computes the product of an
$m \times 1$ matrix and a $1 \times n$ matrix.

articles.title: Size of the outer-product matrix circuit
articles.statement:
For every type $F$ of scalars and all
$m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit over $F$ has exactly $mn$ gates.

articles.title: Outer-product matrix circuit
articles.statement:
For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the
outer-product matrix circuit is the matrix arithmetic circuit for an $m \times 1$ matrix times a
$1 \times n$ matrix with exactly $mn$ gates: for $i < m$ and $j < n$, the gate for $(i, j)$
multiplies the input at entry $(i, 0)$ of the first matrix by the input at entry $(0, j)$ of
the second, and the output at $(i, j)$ is that gate.

articles.title: Lower bound for matrix multiplication circuits
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $c$ be a
circuit over $F$ that computes the product of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix,
where $r \ge 1$. Then $c$ has at least $mn$ gates.

Distinct entries of the product require distinct gates, over every field.

articles.title: Outputs of a matrix multiplication circuit are gates
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $c$ be
a circuit over $F$ that computes the product of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix,
where $r \ge 1$. Then for all $i < m$ and $j < n$, the output of $c$ at $(i, j)$ is one of its
gates, not a constant or an input.

articles.title: A finite rectangular circuit exponent is attained
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $k \ge 0$ a real
number. If the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $\omega$ of the arithmetic-circuit model
over $F$ at aspect $k$ is finite, then $\omega$ is itself an admissible exponent at aspect $k$
over $F$.

articles.title: Upper bounds on the rectangular circuit exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $k \ge 0$ and
$w \ge 0$ be reals. The rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is at most $w$ if and
only if $w$ is an admissible rectangular circuit exponent for $F$ at aspect $k$: for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic
circuit over $F$ of size at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ computes the product of an
$n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$ matrix and a $\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix.

articles.title: Admissible exponents bound the rectangular circuit exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let
$k$ and $w$ be reals. If $w$ is an admissible rectangular circuit exponent for $F$ at aspect $k$,
then the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is at most $w$.

articles.title: The rectangular circuit exponent at aspect zero is two
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the
rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $0$ equals $2$.

The upper bound comes from the outer-product circuit, which multiplies an $n \times 1$ matrix by a
$1 \times n$ matrix with $n^2$ multiplications.

articles.title: Rectangular circuit exponent
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ and a real $k$, the rectangular circuit
exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the admissible rectangular circuit
exponents for $F$ at aspect $k$: the reals $w \ge 0$ such that $k \ge 0$ and, for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, there are $C > 0$ and $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic
circuit over $F$ of size at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ computes the product of an
$n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$ matrix and a $\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix. The infimum of the
empty family is $\infty$; in particular the exponent is $\infty$ when $k < 0$.

articles.title: The rounded inner dimension is positive
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every real
$k$, the rounded inner dimension $\lceil n^k \rceil$ is positive.

articles.title: The square circuit exponent is the aspect-one rectangular exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$,
the square matrix multiplication circuit exponent of $F$ equals the rectangular circuit exponent
of $F$ at aspect $1$.

articles.title: Upper bounds on the square matrix multiplication circuit exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field with
square matrix multiplication circuit exponent $\omega(F) \in [0, \infty]$, and let $w \ge 0$ be
real. Then $\omega(F) \le w$ if and only if $F$ has rectangular circuit exponent $w$ at aspect
$1$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such
that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ with at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$
gates computes the product of every pair of $n \times n$ matrices over $F$.

articles.title: The square matrix multiplication circuit exponent is attained
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field whose
square matrix multiplication circuit exponent $\omega(F)$ is finite. Then $F$ has rectangular
circuit exponent $\omega(F)$ at aspect $1$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$
and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ with
at most $C n^{\omega(F) + \varepsilon}$ gates computes the product of every pair of $n \times n$
matrices over $F$.

articles.title: Square matrix multiplication circuit exponent
articles.statement:
For a field $F$, the square matrix
multiplication circuit exponent of $F$ is the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $1$.
Since $\lceil n^1 \rceil = n$, it is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the reals $w \ge 0$ such that
for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some
arithmetic circuit over $F$ of size at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ computes the product of two
$n \times n$ matrices, and it is $\infty$ when there is no such $w$.

articles.title: The rectangular circuit exponent is at least two
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and every real $k$,
the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is at least $2$ (it may be $\infty$).

articles.title: The square circuit exponent is at least two
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the square matrix
multiplication circuit exponent of $F$ is at least $2$.

This trivial bound holds because a circuit computing the product of two $n \times n$ matrices has
a separate gate for each of the $n^2$ output entries.

articles.title: Admissible rectangular circuit exponents are at least two
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $k$
and $w$ be reals. If $w$ is an admissible rectangular circuit exponent for $F$ at aspect $k$, then
$w \ge 2$.

A circuit computing the product of an $n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$ matrix and a
$\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix with $n \ge 1$ has a separate gate for each of the $n^2$ output
entries, so it has at least $n^2$ gates.

articles.title: Arithmetic circuit
articles.statement:
An arithmetic circuit over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and
outputs indexed by $B$ consists of a size $s \in \mathbb{N}$, a gate $g_i$ for each $i < s$, and
an output operand for each $b \in B$. Each gate $g_i$ is an addition, subtraction or
multiplication of two operands, each a constant in $F$, an input $a \in A$ or an earlier gate
$g_j$ with $j < i$; an output operand is a constant in $F$, an input or any gate $g_j$ with
$j < s$.

Constants and inputs are free; each gate counts as one scalar operation.

articles.title: Arithmetic gate
articles.statement:
An arithmetic gate over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and $n$ prior
nodes is an addition, a subtraction or a multiplication of two arithmetic operands, each of
which is a constant in $F$, an input $a \in A$ or a reference to a node $i < n$.

articles.title: Arithmetic operand
articles.statement:
An arithmetic operand over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and $n$
nodes is a constant $x \in F$, an input $a \in A$, or a reference to a node $i < n$.

articles.title: Gate evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and multiplication, let $A$
be a type and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Given a value in $F$ for each input $a \in A$ and a value
in $F$ for each node $i < n$, write $v(x)$ for the value of an arithmetic operand $x$: a constant
evaluates to itself, an input $a$ to its assigned value and a reference to node $i$ to the value
given for node $i$. An arithmetic gate over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and $n$ prior nodes
that adds, subtracts or multiplies the operands $x$ and $y$ evaluates to $v(x) + v(y)$,
$v(x) - v(y)$ or $v(x) \cdot v(y)$ respectively.

articles.title: Circuit evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and multiplication and
let $c$ be an arithmetic circuit over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and outputs indexed by $B$.
Given a value in $F$ for each input $a \in A$, the value of $c$ at an output $b \in B$ is the value
of the output operand of $b$, where a constant $x$ has value $x$, an input has its assigned value
and a reference to gate $g_j$ has the value of $g_j$, each gate being evaluated from the values of
the gates before it.

articles.title: Value of a gate in a circuit
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and
multiplication and let $c$ be an arithmetic circuit over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$. Given a
value in $F$ for each input $a \in A$, the value of gate $g_i$ of $c$ is the value of the operation
of $g_i$ on its two operands, where a constant $x$ has value $x$, an input has its assigned value
and a reference to an earlier gate $g_j$ with $j < i$ takes the value of $g_j$, defined
recursively.

articles.title: Operand evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $F$ and $A$ be types and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Given a value in $F$
for each input $a \in A$ and a value in $F$ for each node $i < n$, an arithmetic operand over $F$
with inputs indexed by $A$ and $n$ nodes evaluates as follows: a constant $x$ evaluates to $x$, an
input $a$ to its assigned value, and a reference to node $i$ to the value given for node $i$.

articles.title: Extensionality for arithmetic circuits
articles.statement:
Two arithmetic circuits over $F$ with inputs
indexed by $A$ and outputs indexed by $B$ are equal if they have the same size, the same gate at
each position and the same output operand for each $b \in B$.

articles.title: Correctness of the outer-product circuit
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and
multiplication. For all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, $a \in F^m$, $b \in F^n$, $i < m$ and $j < n$, the
outer-product circuit over $F$ evaluated on the inputs $a$ and $b$ has value $a_i b_j$ at the
output $(i, j)$.

articles.title: Size of the outer-product circuit
articles.statement:
For every $F$ and all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the
outer-product circuit over $F$ for $m \times n$ outer products has exactly $mn$ gates.

articles.title: Outer-product circuit
articles.statement:
For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the
outer-product circuit has inputs $a_0, \dots, a_{m-1}$ and $b_0, \dots, b_{n-1}$, one output for
each pair $(i, j)$ with $i < m$ and $j < n$, and exactly $mn$ gates: the gate for $(i, j)$
multiplies $a_i$ by $b_j$, and the output at $(i, j)$ is that gate.

articles.title: Binary encoding of natural numbers
articles.statement:
The binary encoding of a natural number $n$ is the
list of its base-$2$ digits, least significant first, with the digit $1$ written as the Boolean
value true and the digit $0$ as false. The list has no trailing zero digit, so $0$ is encoded by
the empty list.

Unlike the unary encoding, this encoding of $n > 0$ has length $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$,
which is the size model of the bit-complexity bound $O(n \log n)$ for integer multiplication;
with the unary encoding that bound could not hold.

## Sources

- Lean variant; this replaces the upstream unary encoding `Computability.encodeNat`.

articles.title: Encoding of pairs
articles.statement:
Given encodings $e_A : A \to \Gamma_A^*$ and $e_B : B \to \Gamma_B^*$
of types $A$ and $B$ as lists over alphabets $\Gamma_A$ and $\Gamma_B$, and a new symbol $\bot$
in neither alphabet, a pair $(a, b)$ is encoded as a list over the alphabet
$(\Gamma_A \cup \{\bot\}) \times (\Gamma_B \cup \{\bot\})$ by zipping: its length is the larger of
the lengths of $e_A(a)$ and $e_B(b)$, and its $i$-th entry is the pair of the $i$-th entries of
$e_A(a)$ and $e_B(b)$, where an entry missing from the shorter list is replaced by $\bot$.

articles.title: Harvey–van der Hoeven: integer multiplication in time $O(n \log n)$
articles.statement:
There is a
multi-stack Turing machine with finite alphabets and a function $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
such that, for all natural numbers $x$ and $y$, the machine started on the encoding of the pair
$(x, y)$ (the binary encodings of $x$ and $y$, zipped) halts within $t(\ell)$ steps with the
binary encoding of $xy$, where $\ell$ is the length of the input, and $t(n) = O(n \log n)$ as
$n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- D. Harvey and J. van der Hoeven, `Integer multiplication in time O(n log n)`, Annals of Math, 193 (2) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_integer_multiplication` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Alman–Duan–Vassilevska Williams–Xu–Xu–Zhou upper bound for matrix multiplication
articles.statement:
For
every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent of $F$ in the arithmetic-circuit
model is at most $2.371339$.

## Sources

- C15a [ADVXXZ2024], bound `2.371339`.

articles.title: Alman–Vassilevska Williams 2020 bound on the square exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the
square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\omega(F) \le 2.3728596$.

## Sources

- C15a [AV2020], Alman--Vassilevska Williams bound `2.3728596`.

articles.title: Bini–Capovani–Romani–Lotti bound on the square exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the square
matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\omega(F) \le 3 \log_{12} 10$.

## Sources

- C15a [BCRL1979, B1980], the `3 log₁₂ 10` approximate-algorithm bound.

articles.title: The square exponent depends only on the characteristic
articles.statement:
If two fields $F$ and $K$ have
the same characteristic, then the square matrix multiplication exponents of $F$ and $K$ in the
arithmetic-circuit model are equal.

## Sources

- C15a additional comments and [S1981]: the exponent depends only on the field characteristic. This circuit-model transfer is not proved.

articles.title: The rectangular exponent depends only on the characteristic
articles.statement:
If two fields $F$ and $K$
have the same characteristic, then for every real $k \ge 0$ the rectangular matrix
multiplication exponents of $F$ and $K$ in the arithmetic-circuit model at aspect $k$ are
equal.

## Sources

- LG2012 Section 1, characteristic dependence; this circuit-model transfer is missing.

articles.title: Cohn–Kleinberg–Szegedy–Umans bound on the square exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the
square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\omega(F) \le 2.41$.

## Sources

- C15a [CKSU2005], group-theoretic bound `2.41`.

articles.title: Coppersmith's rectangular exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the rectangular matrix
multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model at aspect $0.172$ equals $2$: an
$n \times \lceil n^{0.172} \rceil$ matrix times an $\lceil n^{0.172} \rceil \times n$ matrix costs
$n^{2 + o(1)}$ arithmetic operations.

## Sources

- C15b/LGU2018 Section 1.1, Coppersmith's 1982 exponent equality.

articles.title: Coppersmith's 1997 bound on the dual exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the dual matrix
multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\alpha(F) > 0.29462$.

## Sources

- C15b/LG2012 abstract, the previous Coppersmith 1997 record is strict.

articles.title: Coppersmith–Winograd 1982 bound on the square exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the square
matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\omega(F) \le 2.495548$.

## Sources

- C15a [CW1982], Coppersmith--Winograd bound `2.495548`.

articles.title: Coppersmith–Winograd 1990 bound on the square exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the square
matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\omega(F) \le 2.375477$.

## Sources

- C15a [CW1990], Coppersmith--Winograd bound `2.375477`.

articles.title: Dual matrix multiplication exponent
articles.statement:
For a field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication
exponent of $F$ is the supremum, taken in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$, of the
set of real aspects $k \ge 0$ for which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of $F$ at
aspect $k$ equals $2$.

articles.title: Duan–Wu–Zhou bound on the square exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the square matrix
multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\omega(F) \le 2.371866$.

## Sources

- C15a [DWZ2022], Duan--Wu--Zhou bound `2.371866`.

articles.title: Dupont–Eisenberger et al. upper bound for matrix multiplication
articles.statement:
For every field $F$,
the square matrix multiplication exponent of $F$ in the arithmetic-circuit model is at most
$2.371177$.

## Sources

- C15a [DEKMRSZAWB2026], best catalogue bound `2.371177`.

articles.title: Value of a rank-one trilinear term
articles.statement:
For a rank-one trilinear term over a semigroup $F$
with factors $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$, its value at $a \in A$, $b \in B$,
$c \in C$ is the product $u(a)\,v(b)\,w(c)$.

articles.title: Rank exponents via the minimum tensor rank
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $w$ a real number. Then
$w$ is a matrix multiplication rank exponent over $F$ if and only if $w \ge 0$ and there are a real
$C > 0$ and a natural number $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the tensor rank of the
$n \times n$ matrix multiplication structure tensor over $F$ is at most $C n^w$.

articles.title: Exponent three for matrix multiplication rank
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the number $3$ is a
matrix multiplication rank exponent over $F$.

It is witnessed by the direct decomposition of the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor into
$n^3$ rank-one terms.

articles.title: Exponents above the matrix multiplication exponent admit rank bounds
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field,
let $\omega(F)$ be its matrix multiplication exponent and let $w > 0$ be real. If
$\omega(F) < w$, then there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the
$n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ has rank at most $C n^w$.

articles.title: Matrix multiplication rank exponent
articles.statement:
A real number $w$ is a matrix multiplication rank
exponent over a field $F$ when $w \ge 0$ and there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number
$N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication coefficient
tensor over $F$ is a sum of at most $C n^w$ rank-one trilinear terms.

articles.title: Rank exponents for rectangular matrix multiplication
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $k, w$ be
real. Then $w$ is a rank exponent for rectangular matrix multiplication over $F$ at aspect $k$
when $k \ge 0$, $w \ge 0$, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$
such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the tensor of multiplying an $n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$
matrix by a $\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix over $F$ has rank at most
$C n^{w + \varepsilon}$.

The coefficient $C$ and the threshold $N_0$ may depend on $\varepsilon$, but not on $n$.

articles.title: Tensor rank bounds agree with coefficient rank bounds
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $A$, $B$,
$C$ types with $A$ and $C$ finite, and let $T$ be an element of $(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$.
For every natural number $r$, $T$ has tensor rank at most $r$ if and only if its coefficient
array $A \to B \to C \to F$, obtained by the canonical linear equivalence, has trilinear rank at
most $r$.

articles.title: Tensor rank at most $r$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $A$, $B$, $C$ types. An element $T$ of
$(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$ has tensor rank at most $r$ when there are $s \le r$ and
functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ for $i = 1, \dots, s$ such that
$T = \sum_{i=1}^{s} (u_i \otimes v_i) \otimes w_i$.

articles.title: Trivial upper bound on trilinear rank
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring and $A$, $B$, $C$ finite
types. Every array $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ has trilinear rank at most
$|A| \cdot |B| \cdot |C|$.

articles.title: Rank bounds via the trilinear rank
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring and $A$, $B$, $C$ finite types.
For every array $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ and every natural number $r$, $T$ has trilinear rank at
most $r$ if and only if the trilinear rank of $T$ (the least length of a decomposition of $T$
into rank-one arrays) is at most $r$.

articles.title: Trilinear rank at most $r$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring and $A$, $B$, $C$ types. An array
$T : A \to B \to C \to F$ has trilinear rank at most $r$ when there are $s \le r$ and functions
$u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ for $i = 1, \dots, s$ such that
$T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$.

articles.title: Le Gall's 2012 bound on the dual exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the dual matrix
multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\alpha(F) > 0.30298$.

## Sources

- C15b/LG2012 abstract, Le Gall's 2012 improvement is strict.

articles.title: Le Gall's 2014 bound on the square exponent
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the square matrix
multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies
$\omega(F) \le 2.3728639$.

articles.title: Lower bounds for the matrix multiplication exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $W$ be an
element of $[0, \infty]$. If $W \le w$ for every real number $w$ that is a matrix multiplication
rank exponent over $F$, then $W$ is at most the matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$.

articles.title: Matrix coordinates
articles.statement:
The index set of an $m \times n$ matrix: pairs $(i, j)$ of a row index
$i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ and a column index $j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

articles.title: Rank bounds just above the matrix multiplication exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let
$\omega(F)$ be its matrix multiplication exponent, a finite real number. For every real
$\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the
$n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ has rank at most
$C n^{\omega(F) + \varepsilon}$.

articles.title: Upper bounds on the matrix multiplication exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $\omega(F)$
be its matrix multiplication exponent and let $w \ge 0$ be real. Then $\omega(F) \le w$ if and
only if for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every
$n \ge N_0$ the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ has rank at most
$C n^{w + \varepsilon}$.

The right-hand side bounds the rank by $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ for each $\varepsilon > 0$;
it is not an $O(n^w)$ rank bound.

articles.title: Rank exponents bound the matrix multiplication exponent
articles.statement:
If a real number $w$ is a matrix
multiplication rank exponent over a field $F$, then the matrix multiplication exponent
$\omega(F)$ of $F$ satisfies $\omega(F) \le w$.

articles.title: The matrix multiplication exponent is at most three
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the matrix
multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of $F$ satisfies $\omega(F) \le 3$.

articles.title: The matrix multiplication exponent is finite
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the matrix
multiplication exponent of $F$, an element of $[0, \infty]$, is not $\infty$.

articles.title: Matrix multiplication exponent
articles.statement:
The matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of a field
$F$ is the infimum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the real numbers $w$ that are matrix multiplication
rank exponents over $F$; it is $\infty$ when there is no such $w$.

articles.title: Coefficients of the matrix multiplication structure tensor
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let
$m, n, p$ be natural numbers, and write $e_x$ for the standard basis vector with index $x$. The
coordinates of the structure tensor
$\sum_{i < m,\, j < n,\, k < p} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$ in
$F^{m \times n} \otimes F^{n \times p} \otimes F^{p \times m}$ are the matrix multiplication
coefficients: the coordinate at $((i, j), (j', k), (k', i'))$ is $1$ if $j = j'$, $k = k'$ and
$i = i'$, and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Strassen's decomposition of the structure tensor
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and write $e_x$ for
the standard basis vector with index $x$. The $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication structure tensor
$\sum_{i, j, k < 2} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$ in
$F^{2 \times 2} \otimes F^{2 \times 2} \otimes F^{2 \times 2}$ is a sum of at most $7$ pure
tensors $u \otimes v \otimes w$.

articles.title: Direct decomposition of the structure tensor
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $m, n, p$ be
natural numbers, and write $e_x$ for the standard basis vector with index $x$. The matrix
multiplication structure tensor
$\sum_{i < m,\, j < n,\, k < p} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$ in
$F^{m \times n} \otimes F^{n \times p} \otimes F^{p \times m}$ is a sum of at most $mnp$ pure
tensors $u \otimes v \otimes w$.

articles.title: Matrix multiplication structure tensor
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ and natural numbers $m, n, p$, the
structure tensor of multiplying an $m \times n$ matrix by an $n \times p$ matrix over $F$ is
the element $\sum_{i < m} \sum_{j < n} \sum_{k < p} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$
of the trilinear tensor space
$F^{[m] \times [n]} \otimes F^{[n] \times [p]} \otimes F^{[p] \times [m]}$, where
$[m] = \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ and $e_x$ is the standard basis vector at the matrix coordinate $x$.

articles.title: Contracting the matrix multiplication tensor gives the matrix product
articles.statement:
For a field $F$,
matrices $A \in F^{m \times n}$ and $B \in F^{n \times p}$, and indices $i < m$ and $k < p$, the
contraction of the matrix multiplication tensor against $A$ and $B$ at output coordinate
$(i, k)$ equals the entry $(AB)_{ik}$ of the matrix product.

articles.title: Matrix multiplication tensor contraction
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $m, n, p$ be natural
numbers, let $A \in F^{m \times n}$ and $B \in F^{n \times p}$, and let $i < m$ and $k < p$. Write
$T$ for the matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ for $m, n, p$ and, for a natural number $q$,
$[q] = \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$. The contraction of $T$ against $A$ and $B$ at output coordinate
$(i, k)$ is

$$\sum_{a \in [m] \times [n]} \sum_{b \in [n] \times [p]} T(a, b, (k, i)) \, A_a \, B_b,$$

where $A_a$ and $B_b$ are the entries of $A$ and $B$ at the matrix coordinates $a$ and $b$.

articles.title: Direct rank bound for the matrix multiplication tensor
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and natural
numbers $m, n, p$, the coefficient tensor of multiplying an $m \times n$ matrix by an $n \times p$
matrix over $F$ is a sum of at most $mnp$ rank-one trilinear terms.

The decomposition is the direct algorithm, with one term for each triple $(i, j, k)$ with
$i < m$, $j < n$ and $k < p$.

articles.title: Matrix multiplication tensor
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ and natural numbers $m$, $n$, $p$, the matrix
multiplication tensor is the array over $F$ indexed by triples $((i, j), (j', k), (k', i'))$ of an
$m \times n$, an $n \times p$ and a $p \times m$ matrix coordinate, whose entry is $1$ if $j = j'$,
$k = k'$ and $i' = i$, and $0$ otherwise.

These are the coefficients of $\sum_{i, j, k} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$, the
tensor of multiplying an $m \times n$ matrix by an $n \times p$ matrix.

articles.title: Monotonicity of matrix multiplication rank exponents
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let
$w \le w'$ be real numbers. If $w$ is a matrix multiplication rank exponent for $F$, then so
is $w'$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of trilinear rank bounds
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring and $T : A \to B \to C \to F$
an array. If $T$ has trilinear rank at most $r$ and $r \le s$, then $T$ has trilinear rank at
most $s$.

articles.title: Naive bound for square matrix multiplication
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the square matrix
multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le 3$.

## Sources

- C15a, trivial upper bound. The general finite naive circuit construction is not supplied upstream, so this remains a proof request.

articles.title: Conjecture that the square exponent is two
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every field $F$,
the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model equals $2$.

Since $\omega(F) \ge 2$ always holds, this says the trivial lower bound is sharp. It is a
conjecture, recorded as a proposition and not asserted.

articles.title: Rank-one trilinear term
articles.statement:
For a type $F$ with multiplication and types $A$, $B$, $C$, a
rank-one trilinear term is a triple of functions $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$, $w : C \to F$ (its
left, middle and right factors), representing one rank-one summand $u \otimes v \otimes w$ of a
trilinear tensor decomposition.

articles.title: Rectangular inner dimension at dimension one
articles.statement:
For every real aspect $k$, the rectangular
inner dimension at dimension $1$ and aspect $k$, namely $\lceil 1^k \rceil$, equals $1$.

articles.title: Rectangular inner dimension at aspect one
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the rectangular
inner dimension at dimension $n$ and aspect $1$, namely $\lceil n^1 \rceil$, equals $n$, so
aspect $1$ is square matrix multiplication without rounding.

articles.title: Rectangular inner dimension at aspect zero
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, including
$n = 0$, the rectangular inner dimension at dimension $n$ and aspect $0$, namely
$\lceil n^0 \rceil$, equals $1$, so aspect $0$ is the outer product of an $n \times 1$ matrix
and a $1 \times n$ matrix.

articles.title: Rectangular inner dimension
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$ and a real aspect $k$, the
rectangular inner dimension is $\lceil n^k \rceil$, the least natural number that is at least
the real power $n^k$.

It is the inner dimension in the product of an $n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$ matrix and a
$\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix.

articles.title: Rectangular matrix multiplication exponent
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ and a real number $k$, the
rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(k)$ of $F$ is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of
all real $w \ge 0$ with the following property: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real
$C > 0$ and a natural number $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$, the coefficient tensor
$\sum e_{ij} \otimes e_{jl} \otimes e_{li}$ of multiplying an $n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$ matrix
by an $\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix over $F$ is a sum of at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$
rank-one trilinear terms. If $k < 0$, no $w$ qualifies and $\omega(k) = \infty$.

articles.title: Naive bound for rectangular matrix multiplication
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and every real
$k \ge 0$, the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model at
aspect $k$ is at most $2 + k$.

## Sources

- CLLZ rectangular naive upper bound; a general finite circuit construction is missing.

articles.title: Circuit size and tensor rank give the same rectangular exponent
articles.statement:

and every real $k \ge 0$, the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent at aspect $k$ defined

articles.title: Square matrix multiplication rank equals the coefficient tensor rank
articles.statement:

articles.title: Square matrix multiplication rank
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ and a natural number $n$, the square
matrix multiplication rank of $F$ at $n$ is the tensor rank of the structure tensor of
multiplying two $n \times n$ matrices over $F$: the least number of pure tensors whose sum is that
structure tensor.

articles.title: Direct rank bound for the square matrix multiplication tensor
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and
natural number $n$, the square $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ is a sum of at

articles.title: Strassen's rank bound for $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication
articles.statement:
For every field $F$, the
square $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ is a sum of at most $7$ rank-one
trilinear terms.

The seven terms are Strassen's, and the decomposition holds in every characteristic.

articles.title: Square matrix multiplication tensor
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ and a natural number $n$, the square
matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ is the matrix multiplication tensor for multiplying an
$n \times n$ matrix by an $n \times n$ matrix. Its value at a triple of matrix coordinates
$((i, j), (j', k), (k', i'))$ is $1$ when $j = j'$, $k = k'$ and $i = i'$, and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Decompositions bound the tensor rank
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite
types, and let $T$ be a trilinear tensor over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$. If $T$ is a sum of at
most $r$ pure tensors $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ with $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and
$w : C \to F$, then the tensor rank of $T$ is at most $r$.

articles.title: The tensor rank is attained
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types, let
$T$ be a trilinear tensor over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$, and let $R(T)$ be its tensor rank.
Then $T$ is a sum of at most $R(T)$ pure tensors $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ with $u : A \to F$,
$v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$.

articles.title: Tensor rank
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types. The tensor rank of
a trilinear tensor $T$ over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$ is the least $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such
that $T$ is a sum of at most $r$ pure tensors $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ with $u : A \to F$,
$v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$.

It is defined as the trilinear rank of the coefficient array of $T$.

articles.title: The pure tensor of a rank-one term
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $A$, $B$, $C$ types. A
rank-one trilinear term with factors $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$ determines
the pure tensor $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ in the trilinear tensor space over $F$ indexed by
$A$, $B$, $C$.

articles.title: Decompositions bound the trilinear rank
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite
types, and let $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ be a coefficient array. If there are $s \le r$ functions
$u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ with
$T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$,
then the trilinear rank of $T$ is at most $r$.

articles.title: The trilinear rank is attained
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types,
let $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ be a coefficient array, and let $R(T)$ be its trilinear rank. Then
there are $s \le R(T)$ functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ with
$T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$.

articles.title: Trilinear rank
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types. The trilinear
rank of a coefficient array $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ is the least $r \in \mathbb{N}$ for which
there are $s \le r$ functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ with
$T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$.

Such an $r$ exists because $|A| \cdot |B| \cdot |C|$ coordinate terms always suffice.

articles.title: Coefficients of a pure tensor
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ and $C$ be finite types and
let $B$ be a type. For $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$, $w : C \to F$ and $a \in A$, $b \in B$,
$c \in C$, the coefficient array of the pure tensor $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ takes the value
$u(a)\,v(b)\,w(c)$ at $(a, b, c)$.

articles.title: Coefficient array of a trilinear tensor
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ and $C$ be finite
types, let $B$ be a type, and write $F^X$ for the space of functions $X \to F$. The coefficient
map is the $F$-linear isomorphism from $(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$ to the space
of arrays $A \to B \to C \to F$ that sends each pure tensor $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ to the
array $(a, b, c) \mapsto u(a)\,v(b)\,w(c)$.

articles.title: Trilinear tensors
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ and types $A$, $B$, $C$, write $F^X$ for the
$F$-vector space of functions $X \to F$. The space of trilinear tensors over $F$ indexed by
$A$, $B$, $C$ is the tensor product $(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$ over $F$.

articles.title: Boolean gates
articles.statement:
The Boolean gates are a NOT gate and, for each natural number $a$, an AND
gate and an OR gate indexed by $a$, which stand for gates with $a + 1$ inputs. The numbers of
inputs are assigned by the Boolean signature, so there is no AND or OR gate with zero inputs.

articles.title: Boolean AND as a left fold
articles.statement:
For every natural number $a$ and truth values
$x_0, \dots, x_a$, the Boolean interpretation of the AND gate with $a + 1$ inputs, applied to
$x_0, \dots, x_a$, returns $(\cdots((\mathrm{true} \land x_0) \land x_1) \cdots) \land x_a$,
folding conjunction over the inputs from left to right starting from true.

articles.title: Boolean NOT
articles.statement:
Under the Boolean interpretation, the NOT gate applied to a truth value $x$
returns its negation $\lnot x$.

articles.title: Boolean OR as a left fold
articles.statement:
For every natural number $a$ and truth values
$x_0, \dots, x_a$, the Boolean interpretation of the OR gate with $a + 1$ inputs, applied to
$x_0, \dots, x_a$, returns $(\cdots((\mathrm{false} \lor x_0) \lor x_1) \cdots) \lor x_a$,
folding disjunction over the inputs from left to right starting from false.

articles.title: Boolean interpretation
articles.statement:
The Boolean interpretation evaluates the gates of the Boolean
signature on the truth values $\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$: NOT sends its input $x$ to
$\lnot x$, and for each natural number $a$, the AND gate and the OR gate with inputs
$x_0, \dots, x_a$ return $(\cdots((\mathrm{true} \land x_0) \land x_1) \cdots) \land x_a$ and
$(\cdots((\mathrm{false} \lor x_0) \lor x_1) \cdots) \lor x_a$ respectively, that is, the
conjunction and the disjunction of the inputs.

articles.title: Boolean signature
articles.statement:
The Boolean signature has the Boolean gates as its operation symbols,
where NOT has arity $1$ and, for each natural number $a$, the AND gate and the OR gate indexed by
$a$ have arity $a + 1$. In particular, no AND or OR gate takes zero inputs.

articles.title: Values of appended gates
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a program with $g$ gates over $m$ inputs, let
$c \in \mathbb{N}$, and for each $j < c$ let $f_j$ be a line that reads the inputs and the first
$g + j$ gates. Under any interpretation of the gate symbols and any input values $x$, for every
$j < c$ the value of gate $g + j$ of the program obtained by appending $f_0, \dots, f_{c-1}$ to
$p$ is the value of the line $f_j$ on $x$ and the values of gates $0, \dots, g + j - 1$ of that
same program.

articles.title: Appending one more gate keeps the earlier gate values
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a program with $g$
gates over $m$ inputs, let $c \in \mathbb{N}$, and for each $j \le c$ let $f_j$ be a line that
reads the inputs and the first $g + j$ gates. Under any interpretation of the gate symbols and
any input values, for every $k < g + c$ the value of gate $k$ of the program obtained by
appending $f_0, \dots, f_c$ to $p$ equals the value of gate $k$ of the program obtained by
appending $f_0, \dots, f_{c-1}$ to $p$ (no gates when $c = 0$).

articles.title: Appending gates keeps the old gate values
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a program with $g$ gates over $m$
inputs, let $c \in \mathbb{N}$, and for each $j < c$ let $f_j$ be a line that reads the inputs
and the first $g + j$ gates. Under any interpretation of the gate symbols and any input values,
for every $k < g$ the value of gate $k$ of the program obtained by appending
$f_0, \dots, f_{c-1}$ to $p$ equals the value of gate $k$ of $p$.

articles.title: Appending a block of gates
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a straight-line program with $g$ gates over $m$
inputs, let $c \in \mathbb{N}$, and for each $j < c$ let $f_j$ be a line (a gate operation with
its argument wires) that reads the inputs and the first $g + j$ gates. Appending
$f_0, \dots, f_{c-1}$ to $p$ gives the program with $g + c$ gates whose first $g$ gates are
those of $p$ and whose gate $g + j$ is $f_j$ for each $j < c$. It is defined by recursion on
$c$, adding one gate at a time.

articles.title: The carry out of a block of bits
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors and $c$ a carry-in bit,
and for $i \in \mathbb{N}$ let $c_i$ be the carry into bit $i$ when computing $x + y + c$, that
is, $c_i$ holds exactly when $(x \bmod 2^i) + (y \bmod 2^i) + c \ge 2^i$, where $x$, $y$ are
read as natural numbers and $c$ counts as $1$ when true. For all $a, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$, if
$(G, P)$ are the generate and propagate signals of the block of bits $a, \dots, a + \ell - 1$,
then $c_{a + \ell} = G \lor (P \land c_a)$.

articles.title: Carry depth in the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the carry depth of bit $i$
is $0$ if $i = 0$ and $2i + 1$ if $i \ge 1$. It is used as the depth of the carry into bit $i$
of the ripple-carry adder, where the carry into bit $0$ is the carry-in input.

articles.title: Carry out of the carry-lookahead adder
articles.statement:
Let $n, K \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \le 2^K$, let
$x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors and let $c$ be a carry-in bit. Evaluate the $n$-bit Kogge-Stone
carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels over the Boolean XOR/AND/OR basis on the input that lists
the bits of $x$ from least to most significant, then those of $y$ in the same order, then $c$.
Its output $n$, the last of its $n + 1$ outputs numbered from $0$, is the carry out of
$x + y + c$: it is true exactly when $x + y + c \ge 2^n$, where $x$, $y$ are read as natural
numbers and $c$ counts as $1$ when true.

articles.title: Depth of the carry-lookahead adder with logarithmically many levels
articles.statement:
For every
$n \ge 2$, the $n$-bit Kogge-Stone carry-lookahead adder with $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$
levels has depth exactly $2 \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 5$, the depth being the largest depth of
an output with the inputs at depth $0$.

articles.title: Exact depth of the carry-lookahead adder
articles.statement:
For all $K \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2$, the $n$-bit
Kogge-Stone carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels has depth exactly $2K + 3$, the depth being the
largest depth of an output with the inputs at depth $0$.

With $K = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$ levels this is $2 \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 5$,
logarithmic in $n$, while the depth of the ripple-carry adder grows linearly in $n$.

articles.title: Gate count of the carry-lookahead adder
articles.statement:
For all $n, K \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-bit
Kogge-Stone carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels has exactly $5n + 3nK$ gates: $2n$ in the
first level, $3n$ in each of the $K$ Kogge-Stone levels, and $3n$ in the final level.

articles.title: Sum bits of the carry-lookahead adder
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors, $c$ a carry-in bit
and $K$ a natural number with $n \le 2^K$. Evaluate the $n$-bit Kogge–Stone carry-lookahead adder
with $K$ levels in the Boolean interpretation of the XOR/AND/OR basis, on the input made of the
bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ of the adder is bit $i$
(the bit of weight $2^i$) of the sum $x + y + c$ taken modulo $2^n$.

articles.title: Kogge–Stone carry-lookahead adder
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $K$, the $n$-bit
carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels is the circuit over the XOR/AND/OR basis with $2n + 1$
inputs (the bits $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ of one summand, the bits $y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}$ of the
other, and a carry-in $c$) and $n + 1$ outputs, whose gates are those of the $n$-bit adder
program with $K$ Kogge–Stone levels. For $i < n$, output $i$ is the sum gate of bit $i$ in the
final level; output $n$ is the carry gate of bit $n - 1$ in the final level, or the input $c$
when $n = 0$.

When $n \le 2^K$, the outputs are the $n$ bits of $x + y + c$ and its carry out.

articles.title: Carries from the Kogge–Stone prefixes
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors, $c$ a carry-in bit,
and $K$, $i$ natural numbers with $n \le 2^K$ and $i < n$. Let $(G, P)$ be the generate and
propagate signals that bit $i$ holds after $K$ Kogge–Stone levels, those of the block of the at
most $2^K$ bits ending at bit $i$. Then the carry into bit $i + 1$ of $x + y + c$, which is true
exactly when $(x \bmod 2^{i+1}) + (y \bmod 2^{i+1}) + c \ge 2^{i+1}$, equals
$G \lor (P \land c)$.

Since $n \le 2^K$, that block is the whole prefix of bits $0, \dots, i$.

articles.title: Number of carry-lookahead levels
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the number of Kogge–Stone
levels used for $n$ bits is $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$, with $\lfloor \log_2 0 \rfloor = 0$.

This number satisfies $n \le 2^{\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1}$.

articles.title: Depth of the carry gates
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$, $K$ and $i < n$, in the gate program
of the $n$-bit adder with $K$ Kogge–Stone levels, the carry gate of bit $i$ in the final level
(gate $3i + 1$ of that level) has depth $\max(2K + 1, K + 2) + 1$, where inputs have depth $0$
and each gate is one deeper than its deepest argument.

articles.title: The carry gates
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors, $c$ a carry-in bit and $K$ a natural number
with $n \le 2^K$. Evaluate the gate program of the $n$-bit adder with $K$ Kogge–Stone levels in
the Boolean interpretation of the XOR/AND/OR basis, on the input made of the bits of $x$, the bits
of $y$ and $c$. Then for every $i < n$, gate $3i + 1$ of the final level holds the carry into bit
$i + 1$ of $x + y + c$, which is true exactly when
$(x \bmod 2^{i+1}) + (y \bmod 2^{i+1}) + c \ge 2^{i+1}$.

articles.title: Depth of the sum gates
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$, $K$ and $i < n$, in the gate program
of the $n$-bit adder with $K$ Kogge–Stone levels, the sum gate of bit $i$ in the final level
(gate $3i + 2$ of that level) has depth $2$ if $i = 0$ and depth $\max(2K + 1, K + 2) + 2$
otherwise, where inputs have depth $0$ and each gate is one deeper than its deepest argument.

articles.title: The sum gates
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors with bits $x_i$, $y_i$, $c$ a carry-in bit
and $K$ a natural number with $n \le 2^K$. Evaluate the gate program of the $n$-bit adder with
$K$ Kogge–Stone levels in the Boolean interpretation of the XOR/AND/OR basis, on the input made
of the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. Then for every $i < n$, gate $3i + 2$ of the final
level is $x_i \oplus y_i \oplus c_i$, where $c_i$ is the carry into bit $i$ of $x + y + c$, true
exactly when $(x \bmod 2^i) + (y \bmod 2^i) + c \ge 2^i$.

articles.title: Gates of the carry-lookahead adder
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $K$, the gate program of
the $n$-bit adder with $K$ Kogge–Stone levels is the straight-line program over the XOR/AND/OR
basis on $2n + 1$ inputs (the $n$ bits of one summand, the $n$ bits of the other and a carry-in
$c$) made of level $0$ and Kogge–Stone levels $1, \dots, K$, followed by a final level of $3n$
gates. For each bit $i < n$, let $G_i$ and $P_i$ be the generate and propagate gates of bit $i$
after level $K$ and $p_i$ its propagate gate at level $0$. Gate $3i$ of the final level computes
$P_i \land c$, gate $3i + 1$ computes $G_i \lor (P_i \land c)$, and gate $3i + 2$ computes
$p_i \oplus c$ when $i = 0$ and the XOR of $p_i$ with gate $3(i - 1) + 1$ of the final level
otherwise.

articles.title: Combining generate–propagate pairs
articles.statement:
For pairs of Booleans $(G, P)$ and $(G', P')$, their
combination is $(G \lor (P \land G'), P \land P')$.

When $(G, P)$ are the generate and propagate signals of a block of bits placed directly above a
block with signals $(G', P')$, the combination gives the signals of the joined block.

articles.title: Depth of an arithmetic gate
articles.statement:
For each gate of the arithmetic basis (XOR, AND or OR) and all
argument depths $d_0, d_1 \in \mathbb{N}$, the depth interpretation of the arithmetic signature
assigns the gate the depth $\max(d_0, d_1) + 1$.

articles.title: The depth interpretation
articles.statement:
For a signature $\sigma$, the depth interpretation is the
interpretation of $\sigma$ in $\mathbb{N}$ that sends an operation symbol of arity $k$, applied to
argument depths $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$, to $\max(0, d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}) + 1$: a gate is one deeper
than its deepest argument, and a gate without arguments has depth $1$.

articles.title: Gate depths are evaluation in the depth interpretation
articles.statement:
For every program $p$ over a
signature $\sigma$, the depth of each gate of $p$ equals the value of that gate when $p$ is
evaluated under the depth interpretation of $\sigma$ with every input set to $0$.

articles.title: Index of the generate gate
articles.statement:
For $n$-bit Kogge-Stone adders, the generate signal of bit $i$
after level $0$ is held by gate $2i$, and after Kogge-Stone level $k + 1$ by gate
$2n + 3nk + 3i + 1$; here $2n + 3nk$ is the number of gates in levels $0, \dots, k$.

articles.title: Gate-depth formula for the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
Let $c(i)$ be the carry depth of bit $i$:
$c(0) = 0$ and $c(i) = 2i + 1$ for $i \ge 1$. The formula assigns to gate $j$ of the ripple-carry
adder, for every $j \in \mathbb{N}$, the depth $1$ when $j \bmod 5$ is $0$ or $2$, the depth
$\max(1, c(\lfloor j/5 \rfloor)) + 1$ when $j \bmod 5$ is $1$ or $3$, and the depth
$c(\lfloor j/5 \rfloor + 1)$ when $j \bmod 5 = 4$.

articles.title: Generate and propagate signals of a bit
articles.statement:
For bit vectors $x, y$ of width $n$ and an index
$i \in \mathbb{N}$, the generate–propagate pair of bit $i$ is $(x_i \wedge y_i,\ x_i \oplus y_i)$,
where $x_i$ and $y_i$ are bit $i$ of $x$ and $y$, taken to be false when $i \ge n$.

articles.title: Adjacent blocks compose
articles.statement:
Fix bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width, write
$\mathrm{GP}(\ell, m)$ for the generate–propagate pair of the block of the $m$ bits
$\ell, \dots, \ell + m - 1$, and write $h \circ l$ for the block operator with $h$ placed above
$l$. Then for all natural numbers $\ell, a, b$,
$\mathrm{GP}(\ell, a + b) = \mathrm{GP}(\ell + a, b) \circ \mathrm{GP}(\ell, a)$.

articles.title: Generate and propagate signals of a block
articles.statement:
For bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width, a
start bit $\ell$ and a length $m$, the generate–propagate pair $\mathrm{GP}(\ell, m)$ of the block
of bits $\ell, \dots, \ell + m - 1$ is defined by recursion on $m$: the empty block has
$\mathrm{GP}(\ell, 0) = (\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true})$, and
$\mathrm{GP}(\ell, m + 1) = \mathrm{gp}(\ell + m) \circ \mathrm{GP}(\ell, m)$, where
$\mathrm{gp}(\ell + m)$ is the generate–propagate pair of bit $\ell + m$ and $\circ$ is the block
operator with its left argument placed above its right.

articles.title: The Kogge-Stone step
articles.statement:
Fix bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width and write $S_k(i)$ for the
generate–propagate pair of the block of the $\min(i + 1, 2^k)$ bits ending at bit $i$, the pair
bit $i$ holds after $k$ Kogge-Stone levels. For all $k, i \in \mathbb{N}$: if $2^k \le i$, then
$S_{k+1}(i) = S_k(i) \circ S_k(i - 2^k)$, where $\circ$ is the block operator with its left
argument placed above its right; otherwise $S_{k+1}(i) = S_k(i)$.

articles.title: The block held after Kogge-Stone levels
articles.statement:
Fix bit vectors $x, y$ of the same width. For
$k, i \in \mathbb{N}$, the pair $S_k(i)$ that bit $i$ holds after $k$ Kogge-Stone levels is the
generate–propagate pair of the block of the $\min(i + 1, 2^k)$ bits ending at bit $i$, that is,
of the bits $i + 1 - \min(i + 1, 2^k), \dots, i$.

articles.title: Gate count of the first Kogge-Stone levels
articles.statement:
For an $n$-bit adder, the number $L_n(k)$ of
gates in level $0$ together with the first $k$ Kogge-Stone levels is given by $L_n(0) = 2n$ and
$L_n(k + 1) = L_n(k) + 3n$, so $L_n(k) = 2n + 3nk$.

articles.title: Depths after each level
articles.statement:
In the program made of level $0$ and the first $k$ Kogge-Stone
levels of the $n$-bit adder, where inputs have depth $0$ and a gate is one deeper than its deepest
argument, for every bit $i < n$ the gate holding the generate signal of bit $i$ has depth $2k + 1$
and the gate holding its propagate signal has depth $k + 1$.

articles.title: Level-0 gates are unchanged by later levels
articles.statement:
For the $n$-bit adder, every interpretation
of the XOR, AND and OR gates in a type $U$, every assignment of values in $U$ to the $2n + 1$
inputs, and every $K$, each of the $2n$ gates of level $0$ has the same value in the program with
level $0$ and $K$ Kogge-Stone levels as in the program with level $0$ alone.

articles.title: Each Kogge-Stone level is correct
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit vectors and $c$ a carry bit,
and evaluate level $0$ and the first $k$ Kogge-Stone levels of the adder on the bits of $x$, the
bits of $y$ and $c$. For every bit $i < n$, the gate holding the generate signal of bit $i$
carries the generate signal, and the gate holding its propagate signal carries the propagate
signal, of the block of the at most $2^k$ bits ending at $i$, that is, of the bits
$\max(0, i + 1 - 2^k), \dots, i$.

articles.title: Level 0 computes generate and propagate
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit vectors and $c$ a carry
bit, and evaluate level $0$ of the adder on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. For every
bit $i < n$, the gate holding the generate signal of bit $i$ carries the generate signal, and the
gate holding its propagate signal carries the propagate signal, of the block consisting of bit $i$
alone, namely $x_i \wedge y_i$ and $x_i \oplus y_i$.

articles.title: The first Kogge-Stone levels
articles.statement:
For an $n$-bit adder, the program over the XOR, AND and OR
gates on $2n + 1$ inputs obtained from the empty program by appending the $2n$ gates of level
$0$ and then, in turn, the $3n$ gates of each Kogge-Stone level $1, \dots, k$. It has
$2n + 3nk$ gates.

articles.title: Gates of level 0
articles.statement:
Gate $j < 2n$ of level $0$ of the $n$-bit adder of $x$ and $y$ reads the
inputs $\lfloor j/2 \rfloor$ and $n + \lfloor j/2 \rfloor$, which carry bit $\lfloor j/2 \rfloor$
of $x$ and of $y$. For even $j$ it is an AND gate, the generate signal of that bit; for odd $j$ it
is an XOR gate, its propagate signal.

articles.title: Gates of the final level
articles.statement:
Gate $j < 3n$ of the final level of the $n$-bit adder with $K$
Kogge-Stone levels serves bit $i = \lfloor j/3 \rfloor$. Write $G_i$ and $P_i$ for the generate and
propagate gates of bit $i$ after the $K$ levels, $p_i$ for the propagate gate of bit $i$ at level
$0$, and $c$ for the carry input. If $j \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ the gate computes $P_i \wedge c$; if
$j \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ it computes the carry $c_{i+1} = G_i \vee (P_i \wedge c)$ from $G_i$ and the
previous gate; if $j \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ it computes the sum bit $p_i \oplus c_i$, where $c_0 = c$
and, for $i \ge 1$, $c_i$ is the carry gate of bit $i - 1$.

articles.title: Gates of a Kogge-Stone level
articles.statement:
Gate $j < 3n$ of Kogge-Stone level $k + 1$ of the $n$-bit
adder serves bit $i = \lfloor j/3 \rfloor$ and its partner $q$, which is $i - 2^k$ if $2^k \le i$
and $i$ otherwise. Write $G_b$ and $P_b$ for the generate and propagate gates of bit $b$ after
level $k$. If $j \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ the gate computes $P_i \wedge G_q$; if $j \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ it
computes the new generate signal $G_i \vee (P_i \wedge G_q)$ from $G_i$ and the previous gate; if
$j \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ it computes the new propagate signal $P_i \wedge P_q$.

articles.title: Lowest bit of a Kogge-Stone block
articles.statement:
The lowest bit of the block that bit $i$ holds after $k$
Kogge-Stone levels, $i + 1 - \min(i + 1, 2^k)$, that is, $\max(0, i + 1 - 2^k)$.

articles.title: Propagate gate of a bit in the Kogge–Stone adder
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $i$,
$p_n(k, i)$ is the index of the gate holding the propagate signal of bit $i$ after level $k$ of
the $n$-bit carry-lookahead adder: $p_n(0, i) = 2i + 1$, and $p_n(k + 1, i) = 2n + 3nk + 3i + 2$,
where $2n + 3nk$ is the number of gates in levels $0, \dots, k$.

articles.title: Kogge–Stone partner bit
articles.statement:
The bit combined with bit $i$ at level $k + 1$ of the Kogge–Stone
adder is bit $i - 2^k$ if $2^k \le i$, and bit $i$ itself otherwise.

articles.title: Gate depths of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $g \le 5n$ and $j < g$,
evaluating the first $g$ gates of the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder in $\mathbb{N}$, with every
input at depth $0$ and every gate one deeper than its deepest argument, gives gate $j$ the depth
$d(j)$. Here, with $q = \lfloor j / 5 \rfloor$, $c(0) = 0$ and $c(i) = 2i + 1$ for $i \ge 1$,
$d(j) = 1$ if $j \bmod 5 \in \{0, 2\}$, $d(j) = \max(1, c(q)) + 1$ if $j \bmod 5 \in \{1, 3\}$,
and $d(j) = c(q + 1)$ if $j \bmod 5 = 4$.

articles.title: The ripple-carry adder has linear depth
articles.statement:
For every $n \ge 1$, the $n$-bit ripple-carry
adder has depth $2n + 1$, the length of its carry chain.

articles.title: Majority is not in AC0
articles.statement:
The majority language is not in the class $\mathsf{AC}^0$.

## Sources

- M. Ajtai, "Σ₁¹-formulae on finite structures", Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 24 (1983), 1-48; J. Håstad, "Almost optimal lower bounds for small depth circuits" (STOC 1986).

articles.title: Parity is not in AC0
articles.statement:
The parity language, which accepts a bitstring exactly when an odd
number of its entries are true, is not in the class $\mathsf{AC}^0$.

## Sources

- M. Furst, J. Saxe, and M. Sipser, "Parity, circuits, and the polynomial-time hierarchy", Mathematical Systems Theory 17 (1984), 13-27; M. Ajtai, "Σ₁¹-formulae on finite structures", Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 24 (1983), 1-48; J. Håstad, "Almost optimal lower bounds for small depth circuits", Proceedings of the Eighteenth Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC 1986), 6-20.

articles.title: The clique function on adjacency-matrix bits
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$ and a bitstring
$x$, read $x$ as an $n \times n$ adjacency matrix in row-major order: the entry for a pair
$(a, b)$ is the bit of $x$ at position $an + b$, where a position beyond the end of $x$ reads as
false. The clique predicate holds for $n$ and $x$ when there is a set $S$ of exactly
$\lfloor n/3 \rfloor$ vertices among $0, \dots, n - 1$ such that the entry for $(a, b)$ is true
for all distinct $a, b \in S$.

articles.title: Razborov: monotone circuits for clique need superpolynomial size
articles.statement:
For every polynomial
$p$ with natural-number coefficients there is a natural number $n$ with the following property.
Let $C$ be a well-formed monotone flat circuit on $n^2$ inputs, that is, every gate of $C$ is an
input variable, an and gate or an or gate, and refers only to earlier gates. Suppose that for
every bitstring $x$ of length $n^2$, when input variable $i$ is given the $i$-th bit of $x$, $C$
has a last gate with value true if and only if the $n \times n$ matrix read from $x$ in
row-major order has a clique of size $\lfloor n/3 \rfloor$, that is, a set
$S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ of $\lfloor n/3 \rfloor$ vertices whose entries $(a, b)$ are
true for all distinct $a, b \in S$. Then $C$ has more than $p(n^2)$ gates.

## Sources

- A. A. Razborov, "Lower bounds on the monotone complexity of some Boolean functions", Soviet Mathematics Doklady 31 (1985), 354-357.

articles.title: NC^1 is contained in L
articles.statement:
Every decision problem in $\mathsf{NC}^1$ belongs to the class
$\mathsf{L}$ of decision problems decidable in deterministic logarithmic space.

## Sources

- S. Arora and B. Barak, Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach, 2009, Theorem 6.22 (NC¹ ⊆ L); M. Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., 2013, Theorem 9.21 (NC¹ ⊆ L).

articles.title: NC is contained in P
articles.statement:
Every decision problem in $\mathsf{NC}$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.

## Sources

- S. Arora and B. Barak, Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach, 2009, Theorem 6.22 (NC ⊆ P); M. Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., 2013, Theorem 9.21.

articles.title: Arithmetic gate symbols
articles.statement:
The gate symbols of arithmetic circuits are exactly three:
XOR, AND and OR.

articles.title: Boolean interpretation of the arithmetic gates
articles.statement:
The interpretation of the arithmetic
basis in the Booleans: on a first argument $a$ and a second argument $b$, the XOR gate computes
$a \oplus b$, the AND gate computes $a \wedge b$, and the OR gate computes $a \vee b$.

articles.title: Arithmetic basis
articles.statement:
The circuit signature whose operation symbols are the three arithmetic
gate symbols XOR, AND and OR, each of arity $2$.

articles.title: Binary gate line
articles.statement:
For an arithmetic gate symbol $\mathrm{op}$ and wires $u$ and $v$ of a
circuit with $m$ inputs (each wire is an input or one of the $g$ preceding gates), the gate that
applies $\mathrm{op}$ to $u$ as its first argument and $v$ as its second.

articles.title: Value of the carry wire
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit vectors, $c$ a bit, and $i$ and $g$
natural numbers with $5i \le g$. Suppose the first $g$ gates are given values $v_0, \dots, v_{g-1}$
with each $v_j$ equal to the specified value of gate $j$ of the adder on $x$, $y$, $c$. Then, on
the adder input for $x$, $y$, $c$ and with these gate values, the carry wire into bit $i$ carries
the carry into bit $i$ of $x + y + c$: it is true exactly when
$(x \bmod 2^i) + (y \bmod 2^i) + c \ge 2^i$, reading $x$, $y$ and $c$ as natural numbers.

articles.title: Carry wire
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $g$ and $i$ with $5i \le g$, the wire carrying the
carry into bit $i$ of the $n$-bit adder, in a circuit with $2n + 1$ inputs and $g$ gates: for
$i = 0$ it is the carry-in input (input $2n$), and for $i \ne 0$ it is gate $5i - 1$, the
carry-out gate of bit $i - 1$.

articles.title: Gates of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $g$ with $g < 5n$, gate $g$ of
the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder is the following binary gate of the arithmetic basis, whose
arguments are among the $2n + 1$ inputs and the $g$ gates before it. Write $g = 5i + r$ with
$0 \le r < 5$, let $a$ be input $i$ and $b$ input $n + i$, and let $c$ be the carry into bit $i$:
input $2n$ if $i = 0$ and gate $5i - 1$ otherwise. Gate $g$ is the XOR gate with first argument
$a$ and second argument $b$ if $r = 0$, the XOR gate with first argument gate $g - 1$ and second
argument $c$ if $r = 1$, the AND gate with first argument $a$ and second argument $b$ if $r = 2$,
the AND gate with first argument gate $g - 3$ and second argument $c$ if $r = 3$, and the OR gate
with first argument gate $g - 2$ and second argument gate $g - 1$ if $r = 4$.

articles.title: Input of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
For $n$-bit vectors $x$ and $y$ and a bit $c$, the
assignment to the $2n + 1$ inputs of the $n$-bit adder: for $j < n$, input $j$ is bit $j$ of
$x$; for $n \le j < 2n$, input $j$ is bit $j - n$ of $y$; and input $2n$ is $c$. Bit $0$ is the
least significant bit.

articles.title: Gate values of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit vectors and $c$ a bit.
For every $g \le 5n$ and every $j < g$, evaluating the first $g$ gates of the $n$-bit adder with
the Boolean interpretation of the arithmetic gates on the adder input for $x$, $y$, $c$ gives
gate $j$ its specified value on $x$, $y$, $c$.

articles.title: Gate program of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
For $g \le 5n$, the straight-line program over the
arithmetic basis with $2n + 1$ inputs whose gates are, in order, gates $0, 1, \dots, g - 1$ of
the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder; for $g = 0$ it is the empty program.

articles.title: Gate-value specification of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors, $c$ a
bit and $j$ a natural number, and write $j = 5i + r$ with $0 \le r < 5$. Let $x_i$ and $y_i$ be
bit $i$ of $x$ and $y$ (bit $0$ is the least significant, and bits at positions $i \ge n$ are $0$),
and let $c_i$ be the carry into position $i$ when $x$, $y$ and $c$ are added: reading $x$ and $y$
as natural numbers, $c_i = 1$ exactly when $(x \bmod 2^i) + (y \bmod 2^i) + c \ge 2^i$. The
specification assigns to $j$ the bit $x_i \oplus y_i$ if $r = 0$, $(x_i \oplus y_i) \oplus c_i$
if $r = 1$, $x_i \wedge y_i$ if $r = 2$, $(x_i \oplus y_i) \wedge c_i$ if $r = 3$, and $c_{i+1}$
if $r = 4$.

articles.title: Carry out of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors and $c$ a bit, and
evaluate the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with its gates read as Boolean XOR, AND and OR, on the
input whose entry $j$ is bit $j$ of $x$ and entry $n + j$ is bit $j$ of $y$ for $j < n$ (bit $0$
being the least significant), and whose entry $2n$ is $c$. Its output number $n$ (the last,
outputs being numbered from $0$) is the carry out of $x + y + c$: reading $x$ and $y$ as natural
numbers below $2^n$, it is $1$ exactly when $x + y + c \ge 2^n$.

articles.title: Size of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement: The $n$-bit ripple-carry adder has exactly $5n$ gates.

articles.title: Sum bits of the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit vectors, $c$ a bit and $i < n$,
and evaluate the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with its gates read as Boolean XOR, AND and OR, on the
input whose entry $j$ is bit $j$ of $x$ and entry $n + j$ is bit $j$ of $y$ for $j < n$ (bit $0$
being the least significant), and whose entry $2n$ is $c$. Its output number $i$ (outputs being
numbered from $0$) is bit $i$ of the $n$-bit sum $(x + y + c) \bmod 2^n$, reading $x$ and $y$ as
natural numbers below $2^n$.

articles.title: Ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
The $n$-bit ripple-carry adder is the circuit with $2n + 1$ inputs,
$5n$ binary gates, each an XOR, AND or OR gate, and $n + 1$ outputs, built as follows. Write $a_i$
for input $i$, $b_i$ for input $n + i$ and $c_0$ for input $2n$, where $i < n$. For each $i < n$,
gates $g_{5i}, \dots, g_{5i+4}$ form a full adder for position $i$: $g_{5i} = a_i \oplus b_i$,
$g_{5i+1} = g_{5i} \oplus c_i$, $g_{5i+2} = a_i \wedge b_i$, $g_{5i+3} = g_{5i} \wedge c_i$ and
$g_{5i+4} = g_{5i+2} \vee g_{5i+3}$, where the carry $c_i$ is input $2n$ when $i = 0$ and gate
$g_{5i-1}$ otherwise. For $i < n$, output $i$ is gate $g_{5i+1}$, and output $n$ is the carry out
$c_n$: input $2n$ when $n = 0$, otherwise gate $g_{5n-1}$.

articles.title: Shannon: most Boolean functions need exponential circuits
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$n \ge 10$, at least $2^{2^n}/2$ of the Boolean functions $f$ on $n$ input bits have the
following property: for every well-formed flat Boolean circuit $C$ on $n$ inputs without mod
gates whose wire count (the total length of the predecessor lists of its gates) is at most
$\lfloor 2^n / (10 n) \rfloor$, there is an input $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ such that $C$ has no
gates or the value of the last gate of $C$ on $x$ differs from $f(x)$.

## Sources

- C. E. Shannon, "The synthesis of two-terminal switching circuits", Bell System Technical Journal 28 (1949), 59-98.

articles.title: Wire count of a flat circuit
articles.statement:
The wire count of a flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs,
given as a list of gates, is the sum over its gates of the lengths of their predecessor lists:
every reference of a gate to a gate index is counted, with multiplicity, while input variables
and constants contribute nothing and the modulus of a mod gate is not counted.

articles.title: Smolensky: parity is not in AC0(mod 3)
articles.statement:
The parity language, which accepts a bitstring
exactly when an odd number of its entries are true, is not in $\mathsf{AC}^0[3]$, the class
$\mathsf{AC}^0[m]$ for $m = 3$ of decision problems decided by polynomial-size, bounded-depth
families of well-formed flat Boolean circuits in which every mod gate has modulus $3$.

## Sources

- R. Smolensky, "Algebraic methods in the theory of lower bounds for Boolean circuit complexity", Proceedings of the Nineteenth Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC 1987), 77-82.

articles.title: Subtraction by addition
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let $\bar y$ be the bitwise
complement of $y$. Adding $x$ and $\bar y$ with carry in $1$ gives the $n$-bit result $x - y$
(the difference modulo $2^n$), and the carry out is $1$ exactly when there is no unsigned borrow,
that is, when $y \le x$ as unsigned integers.

articles.title: The carry-lookahead adder subtracts
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words, let $\bar y$ be the
bitwise complement of $y$, and let $K$ satisfy $n \le 2^K$. Evaluate the $n$-bit carry-lookahead
adder with $K$ levels, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $\bar y$ and
carry in $1$. Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ is bit $i$ (counting from the least significant
bit $0$) of $x - y$ modulo $2^n$.

articles.title: The overflow adder extends the ripple-carry adder
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let
$c$ be a carry-in bit. Evaluate the $n$-bit overflow adder and the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with
XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. Then for every $o < n + 1$,
output $o$ of the overflow adder equals output $o$ of the ripple-carry adder: the first $n + 1$
outputs (the $n$ sum bits and the carry out) agree.

articles.title: The overflow flag
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words. Evaluate the $n$-bit
overflow adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and carry in $0$.
Its last output (output $n + 1$) is $1$ exactly when the two's complement addition $x + y$
overflows, that is, when the sum of the two's complement values of $x$ and $y$ is at least
$2^{n-1}$ or less than $-2^{n-1}$.

articles.title: Size of the overflow adder
articles.statement:
The $n$-bit overflow adder has $5n + 1$ gates.

This is one gate more than the $5n$ gates of the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder.

articles.title: Sum bits of the overflow adder
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words. Evaluate the $n$-bit
overflow adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and carry in $0$.
Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ is bit $i$ (counting from the least significant bit $0$) of
$x + y$ modulo $2^n$.

articles.title: The overflow adder
articles.statement:
The $n$-bit overflow adder is the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder with one
extra XOR gate. It has the same $2n + 1$ inputs (the bits of the two summands, then the carry in)
and $5n + 1$ gates: the $5n$ gates of the ripple-carry adder, followed by an XOR of the carry into
bit $n - 1$ and the carry into bit $n$ (the carry out). Here the carry into bit $0$ is the carry
in, and for $n = 0$ the index $n - 1$ is read as $0$. Its $n + 2$ outputs are the ripple-carry
adder's $n$ sum bits and carry out, followed by the new gate, the signed-overflow flag.

articles.title: Carry out of ripple-carry subtraction
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let $\bar y$ be
the bitwise complement of $y$. Evaluate the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with XOR, AND and OR
gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $\bar y$ and carry in $1$. Its carry out (output $n$) is $1$
exactly when there is no unsigned borrow in $x - y$, that is, when $y \le x$ as unsigned
integers.

articles.title: The ripple-carry adder subtracts
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let $\bar y$ be the
bitwise complement of $y$. Evaluate the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on
the bits of $x$, the bits of $\bar y$ and carry in $1$. Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ is bit
$i$ (counting from the least significant bit $0$) of $x - y$ modulo $2^n$.

articles.title: Signed overflow is the XOR of the last two carries
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $x$ and $y$ be
$n$-bit words. The two's complement addition $x + y$ overflows (the sum of the two's complement
values of $x$ and $y$ is at least $2^{n-1}$ or less than $-2^{n-1}$) exactly when the carry into
the sign bit $n - 1$ differs from the carry out of it, both carries taken when adding $x$ and $y$
with carry in $0$.

articles.title: Williams: NEXP is not contained in ACC0
articles.statement:
Some decision problem lies in NEXP but not in
$\mathsf{ACC}^0$.

## Sources

- R. Williams, "Non-uniform ACC circuit lower bounds", Journal of the ACM 61 (2014), 1-32 (CCC 2011).

articles.title: Evaluation of an encoded Boolean circuit
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a number of inputs, let $C$ be a
list of gates, each encoded as a (kind, references) pair, and let $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ be a
list of booleans. The evaluation of $C$ on $a$ is the list of values of all gates, in order, of
the flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs obtained by decoding each pair of $C$, under the
assignment that sends each input $i < n$ to $a_i$, or to false when $i$ is at least the length
of $a$.

articles.title: Encoded circuit gates
articles.statement:
An encoded gate of a flat Boolean circuit is a pair $(k, r)$ of a
