articles.title: Converter encoding of the first component
articles.statement:
For a bit list $x$, the bit list obtained by
replacing every bit $b$ of $x$, in order, with the six bits true, true, true, $b$, true, false.

articles.title: Converter encoding of the second component
articles.statement:
For a bit list $w$, the bit list obtained by
replacing every bit $b$ of $w$, in order, with the three bits true, $b$, false.

articles.title: Labels of the pair-encoding converter
articles.statement:
The five labels of the converter program: read the
first component, read the second component, emit the second component, emit the separator, and
emit the first component.

articles.title: Program of the pair-encoding converter
articles.statement:
The program over the converter's four stacks,
five labels and states (a bit or nothing). Each pop either stores the popped bit in the state
(nothing if the stack is empty) or leaves the state unchanged, and each push of the stored bit
uses false when the state holds nothing.

At *read first*: pop the input, storing; if the state is true, pop the input twice without
storing, once storing and twice without storing, push the stored bit onto the first stash and go
to *read first*; otherwise go to *read second*. At *read second*: pop the input, storing; if the
state is true, pop the input once storing and once without storing, push the stored bit onto the
second stash and go to *read second*; otherwise go to *emit second*. At *emit second*: pop the
second stash, storing; if a bit was popped, push it onto the output as a right-tagged bit and go
to *emit second*; otherwise go to *separator*. At *separator*: push the separator onto the
output and go to *emit first*. At *emit first*: pop the first stash, storing; if a bit was
popped, push it onto the output as a left-tagged bit and go to *emit first*; otherwise halt.

articles.title: Runs of the pair-encoding converter
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and configurations $c$ and $d$
of the converter, the statement that $n$ steps of the converter program lead from $c$ to $d$.

articles.title: State of the pair-encoding converter
articles.statement:
The internal state of the converter is an optional
bit: either a bit or nothing. It records the last bit the program stored.

articles.title: Stack contents of the pair-encoding converter
articles.statement:
For bit lists $i$, $a$, $b$ and a list $o$ of
verifier symbols, the contents of the converter's four stacks with $i$ on the input stack, $o$ on
the output stack, $a$ on the first stash and $b$ on the second stash.

articles.title: Stacks of the pair-encoding converter
articles.statement:
The machine that rewrites the canonical encoding
of a pair of bit lists into the verifier's input form has four stacks: the input stack, the
output stack, and two stash stacks, one for each component of the pair.

articles.title: The pair-encoding converter machine
articles.statement:
The converter is the finite multi-stack Turing
machine whose stacks are the input stack, the output stack and the two stash stacks, with bits
as the alphabet of every stack except the output stack, which holds the verifier's symbols. Its
labels are the five phases (read the first component, read the second, emit the second, emit
the separator, emit the first), and it starts in the phase that reads the first component. Its
internal state is an optional bit (the last bit popped), initially empty, and it runs the
converter program. Input is read from the input stack, which holds bits, and output is written
to the output stack.

articles.title: Stack alphabets of the pair-encoding converter
articles.statement:
The output stack of the converter has as
its alphabet the verifier's work alphabet $G = \{0,1\} \sqcup (\{0,1\} \cup \{\#\})$; the input
stack and the two stash stacks have the bits $\{0,1\}$ as their alphabet.

articles.title: Number normalizer restores its work stacks and prepends its answer
articles.statement:
The canonical normalizer restores both work stacks and prepends
its answer to an arbitrary output suffix, within a linear bit bound.

articles.title: Payload normalization adds at most one bit
articles.statement: Normalization adds at most one bit.

articles.title: Payload normalization fixes canonical encodings
articles.statement: Canonical encodings are unchanged.

articles.title: Payload normalization agrees with decode-then-encode
articles.statement:
Normalization agrees with the existing total decoder on every
payload, not just canonical encodings.

articles.title: Normalization of a raw binary natural-number payload
articles.statement: Canonicalize a raw payload without enumerating its decoded value.

articles.title: Number-pair projector as a host component
articles.statement: The concrete two-Nat projector in the existing Host interface.

articles.title: Decoding a pair of naturals fails exactly on a malformed first frame
articles.statement:
Pair Nat decoding fails exactly when the first frame is malformed;
both raw field payloads use Mathlib's total Nat decoder.

articles.title: Canonical payloads of a decoded pair are bounded by the raw input
articles.statement:
Canonical output payload sizes are bounded by the raw input size,
even when either field had a noncanonical final zero bit.

articles.title: Stacks of the number-pair projector
articles.statement: Pair workspace, one reusable Nat buffer, and two canonical outputs.

articles.title: Control labels of the number-pair projector
articles.statement: Pair projection followed by normalization of the two fields.

articles.title: Field-normalizer stack embedding in the number-pair projector
articles.statement: Each normalizer consumes its raw field, sharing only an empty buffer.

articles.title: Label map chaining the two field normalizers
articles.statement: Normalizing the first field continues with the second.

articles.title: Pair-frame splitter stack embedding in the number-pair projector
articles.statement: The pair-frame component acts only on its three own stacks.

articles.title: Pair-frame splitter halt redirection in the number-pair projector
articles.statement: Only actual pair halt labels are redirected.

articles.title: Program of the number-pair projector
articles.statement: All work is performed by the two existing finite components.

articles.title: Number-pair projector normalizes both fields of a raw pair frame
articles.statement:
Every raw pair frame is projected and normalized without changing
the total Nat decoding semantics. Previous output suffixes survive.

articles.title: Embedded number-pair projector preserves outside stacks
articles.statement:
Callers may embed this concrete projector without disturbing
outside stacks. A failed workspace must be cleared before reuse.

articles.title: Number-pair projector fails on malformed framing in linear time
articles.statement:
Malformed pair framing fails in linear time. Private partial
workspace contents must be cleared before another invocation.

articles.title: Number-pair projector yields both canonical payloads on success
articles.statement:
A successful pair decode produces both canonical binary payloads,
with all scratch empty and arbitrary previous output suffixes preserved.

articles.title: Number-pair projector reaches the decoding outcome
articles.statement:
Total decoder outcome with exact successful output and empty
private scratch. Failure does not promise reusable workspace contents.

articles.title: Six-stack invariant of the number-pair projector
articles.statement: Explicit six-stack invariant.

articles.title: Raw pair-frame splitter as a host component
articles.statement: The finite component interface used by fixed nested-codec callers.

articles.title: Stacks of the raw pair-frame splitter
articles.statement: The original input becomes the second field; `left` holds the first.

articles.title: Control labels of the raw pair-frame splitter
articles.statement: Read one frame, restore its order, then report success or failure.

articles.title: Program of the raw pair-frame splitter
articles.statement: Pair framing is split using the existing delimiter and move kernels.

articles.title: Raw field projection agrees with the pair decoder
articles.statement:
Raw field projection agrees with the existing pair decoder. This
is not a runtime assumption or implementation of either element codec.

articles.title: Pair-frame splitter extracts both raw fields
articles.statement:
Extract both raw fields, restore first-field order, and clear
scratch in exactly two steps per first-field bit plus two.

articles.title: Embedded pair-frame splitter preserves caller stacks
articles.statement:
Embedded projection preserves all caller stacks outside the
three-stack workspace, even when framing fails.

articles.title: Pair-frame splitter fails on malformed first-field framing
articles.statement:
Malformed first-field framing reaches the actual failure label.
Scratch may contain a partial field and must be cleared before reuse.

articles.title: Pair-frame splitter projects every well-framed input in linear time
articles.statement:
Every successful raw pair frame is projected within input length
plus one; its two payloads are left unnormalized.

articles.title: Pair-frame splitter reaches the framing outcome
articles.statement:
Total framing outcome, without prematurely accepting either field
as a value of its eventual element type.

articles.title: Stack layout of the raw pair-frame splitter
articles.statement: Explicit stack layout of the projection invariant.

articles.title: Machine step reading one framed payload pair
articles.statement: Consume one framed-payload pair or its terminator.

articles.title: Reading a complete framed block
articles.statement:
Read a complete block, preserving an arbitrary suffix and all stacks
other than the input and reversed-payload destination.

articles.title: Framed block reader fails on truncated framing
articles.statement:
Truncated framing reaches the failure branch within input length
plus one, without assuming that the input is an encoder image. The
destination may contain a partial payload on failure; the caller must
discard or clear it before using that stack again.

articles.title: Unary-to-binary converter as a host component
articles.statement:
The adapter is a finite component of the existing Host. Its input
counter has `n` physical symbols; the bound is linear in that length,
not in the bit length of an arbitrary binary-encoded numeric input.

articles.title: Emitter stack embedding in the unary-to-binary converter
articles.statement: The component retains the existing emitter's heterogeneous alphabets.

articles.title: Label map from the emitter halt to scratch cleanup
articles.statement: The actual emitter halt is followed by charged scratch cleanup.

articles.title: Label enumeration of the unary-to-binary converter
articles.statement:
The finite label enumeration uses the existing emitter enumeration
and two Boolean choices, without a noncomputable list conversion.

articles.title: Control labels of the unary-to-binary converter
articles.statement: Existing emitter labels and the cleanup/unframing continuation.

articles.title: Program of the unary-to-binary converter
articles.statement:
`framed = true` keeps the new frame; otherwise only that frame is
removed, preserving any earlier output below it.

articles.title: Converter turns a unary count into a canonical binary frame
articles.statement:
Emit one canonical Nat frame above any earlier output and restore
all conversion scratch. The old counter is consumed; unrelated stacks,
including `X`, are preserved. Cleanup is part of the charged run.

articles.title: Converter turns a unary count into a raw canonical binary payload
articles.statement:
Convert a unary count to the canonical unframed Nat payload,
preserving an earlier output suffix and clearing every used work stack.

articles.title: Decoded block count is at most the input length
articles.statement: Each decoded block consumes at least its delimiter bit.

articles.title: Quadratic encoding bound for vertex lists below $n$
articles.statement:
Lists of vertices below `n` have a quadratic certificate bound
when their length is at most `n`; no unary Nat encoding is used.

articles.title: Length bound for a list in the first field of a decoded pair
articles.statement: A list in the first field of a decoded pair is raw-input bounded.

articles.title: Decoded list has at most one element per input bit
articles.statement:
A successfully decoded list has at most one element per input bit.
No canonicality assumption on the element payloads is needed.

articles.title: Length bound for the middle list of a decoded triple
articles.statement:
The middle list of a right-associated triple is raw-input bounded.
Used for TSP matrix rows and SET COVER set occurrences.

articles.title: Decoded pair exposes its raw component payloads
articles.statement:
Successful pair decoding exposes the exact raw component payloads.
This includes payloads which are not canonical encodings.

articles.title: Length bound for a list in the second field of a decoded pair
articles.statement: A list in the second field of a decoded pair is raw-input bounded.

articles.title: Framed length bound for lists of $m$-bit naturals
articles.statement:
A list of binary naturals with at most `m` bits per entry has the
stated framed length bound.

articles.title: Parsing a framed head leaves the raw remainder
articles.statement:
Parsing a framed head leaves exactly the raw remainder, including
any later framing failure. The decoder's fuel does not alter this law.

articles.title: List decoder consumes one raw payload at a time
articles.statement:
The canonical list decoder consumes one raw payload at a time.
Both element failure and later framing failure are retained exactly.

articles.title: Malformed first frame makes list decoding fail
articles.statement:
A nonempty input with a malformed first frame fails list decoding.
Empty input is excluded because it is the valid empty list.

articles.title: Cook-Levin for dense CNF-SAT
articles.statement:
Dense CNF-SAT is NP-complete: it lies in NP, and every
decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to dense CNF-SAT.

articles.title: Every NP problem reduces to dense CNF-SAT
articles.statement:
Every decision problem $L$ in NP has a
polynomial-time many-one reduction to dense CNF-SAT: a polynomial-time computable map $f$ on bit
strings such that, for every bit string $x$, $L$ accepts $x$ exactly when dense CNF-SAT accepts
$f(x)$.

articles.title: The chosen accept symbol is encodable
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack Turing machine and
let $a$ be a symbol of its output-stack alphabet. In the tableau encoding of $M$ with $a$ adjoined
to the output alphabet, some index of the effective output-stack alphabet decodes to $a$.

This discharges, for every machine, the accept-symbol hypothesis of the correctness theorem for
the assembled formula.

articles.title: Tableau encoding with a chosen accept symbol
articles.statement:
Given a finite multi-stack Turing machine
$M$ and a symbol $a$ of its output-stack alphabet, this is the encoding of $M$ that numbers the
stacks and the pairs (optional label, state) through their finite enumerations, and whose
effective alphabet on each stack $k$ is the set of symbols some statement of $M$ can push on $k$
(plus the whole input alphabet if $k$ is the input stack), with $a$ added if $k$ is the output
stack. A symbol in that set has code one more than its position in it; any other symbol has
code $0$.

articles.title: The Cook–Levin reduction is polynomial-time
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time Turing machine
that computes a Boolean function on pairs of bit strings, reading a pair $(a, y)$ as the bits of
$a$, a separator, then the bits of $y$, and writing its answer as one bit. For every polynomial
$p$ with natural-number coefficients, the reduction built from $V$ and $p$ is polynomial-time
computable with respect to the canonical bit-string encodings.

articles.title: The Cook–Levin reduction
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time Turing machine that computes a
Boolean function on pairs of bit strings, reading a pair $(a, y)$ as the bits of $a$, a separator,
then the bits of $y$, and writing its answer as one bit; let $t$ be its time bound and fix
constants $c \ge 1$ and $e$ with $t(j) \le (j + c)^e$ for all $j$. For a polynomial $p$ with
natural-number coefficients, the reduction sends a bit string $a$ of length $n$ to the dense bit
encoding of the tableau formula $\Phi$ of $V$, built with the encoding of $V$ whose output
alphabet contains the output symbol $\mathrm{acc}$ for true, for the input prefix $x$ made of the
bits of $a$ followed by the separator, the certificate symbols of $V$ (one per bit) as the
allowed symbols after $x$, the accept symbol $\mathrm{acc}$, width $m = n + 1 + p(n)$ and
$T = (m + c)^e$ steps.

articles.title: Effective alphabets with an adjoined accept symbol
articles.statement:
For a finite multi-stack Turing
machine $M$, a symbol $a$ of its output-stack alphabet and a stack $k$, this is the finite set of
symbols that some statement of $M$ can push on stack $k$ (together with the whole input alphabet
when $k$ is the input stack), with $a$ added when $k$ is the output stack.

articles.title: Correctness of the reduction
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time Turing machine that computes a
Boolean function $f$ on pairs of bit strings, reading a pair $(a, y)$ as the bits of $a$, a
separator, then the bits of $y$, and writing its answer as one bit. Let $p$ be a polynomial with
natural-number coefficients, $R$ a relation on bit strings with $R(a, y)$ iff $f(a, y)$ is true,
and $L'$ a predicate on bit strings such that $L'(a)$ holds iff some bit string $y$ of length at
most $p(|a|)$ satisfies $R(a, y)$. Then for every bit string $a$, $L'(a)$ holds iff the image of
$a$ under the reduction built from $V$ and $p$ is in CNF-SAT.

articles.title: Tableau encoding of the verifier
articles.statement:
For a polynomial-time Turing machine $V$ that computes a
Boolean function on pairs of bit strings, reading a pair $(a, y)$ as the bits of $a$, a separator,
then the bits of $y$, and writing its answer as one bit, this is the tableau encoding of $V$ whose
effective output alphabet is enlarged by the accept symbol: the output symbol of $V$ for true.

articles.title: Input of the verifier on a pair
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a function
of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, whose input alphabet is identified with the pair
alphabet $\mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\ \mathrm{Bool}$, and let $\beta$ be the fixed
bijection from $\{0, 1\}$ onto the Booleans. For bit lists $a$ and $y$, translating the pair
encoding $a \# y$ symbol by symbol into $V$'s input alphabet gives the input-bit symbols of the
indices $\beta^{-1}(b)$ for the bits $b$ of $a$ in order, then the separator symbol, then the
certificate symbols of the bits of $y$ in order.

articles.title: The verifier's run settles on its output
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a machine that computes a function
$f_v$ of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, within $t_V(n)$ steps on an encoding of
length $n$ for a polynomial $t_V$ with natural-number coefficients, with input alphabet
identified with the pair alphabet $\mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\ \mathrm{Bool}$ and output
alphabet identified with the Booleans. Let $a$, $y$ be bit lists of lengths $|a|$, $|y|$, and $T$ a
natural number with $t_V(|a| + 1 + |y|) \le T$. Start $V$ in its initial configuration with its
input stack holding the symbols for the left-tagged bits $\mathrm{inl}(b)$ of $a$, then the
separator $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{none})$, then the symbols for the right-tagged bits
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\ b)$ of $y$, and run it for $T$ steps, a halted configuration staying
unchanged. The result is the halted configuration, in the initial internal state, whose output
stack holds exactly the one output symbol for $f_v(a, y)$ and whose other stacks are empty.

articles.title: Certificate symbol of the verifier
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a
function of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, whose input alphabet is identified with
the pair alphabet $\mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\ \mathrm{Bool}$. For a bit $g$, this is the
symbol of $V$'s input alphabet that corresponds to the right-tagged bit
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\ g)$.

articles.title: Certificate symbols of the verifier
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a
function of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, whose input alphabet is identified with
the pair alphabet $\mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\ \mathrm{Bool}$. This is the list of the
symbols of $V$'s input alphabet corresponding to the right-tagged bits
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\ g)$ for $g = \mathrm{true}$ and $g = \mathrm{false}$, each once, in
the order of a fixed enumeration of the Booleans.

articles.title: Input-bit symbol of the verifier
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a
function of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, whose input alphabet is identified with
the pair alphabet $\mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\ \mathrm{Bool}$, and let $\beta$ be the
fixed bijection from $\{0, 1\}$ onto the Booleans. For an index $i \in \{0, 1\}$, this is the
symbol of $V$'s input alphabet that corresponds to the left-tagged bit $\mathrm{inl}(\beta(i))$.

articles.title: Accept symbol of the verifier
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a function
of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, whose output alphabet is identified with the
Booleans. The accept symbol is the output symbol of $V$ that corresponds to $\mathrm{true}$.

articles.title: Offset of the verifier's time bound
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a
function of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, with time polynomial $t_V$. This is a
natural number $c \ge 1$, fixed by choice, such that for some exponent $e$ we have
$t_V(j) \le (j + c)^e$ for every natural number $j$.

articles.title: Exponent of the verifier's time bound
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a
function of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, with time polynomial $t_V$, and let
$c \ge 1$ be the offset of its time bound, fixed by choice so that some exponent works. This is
an exponent $e$, fixed by choice, with $t_V(j) \le (j + c)^e$ for every natural number $j$.

articles.title: Bits as indices
articles.statement:
The bijection from $\{0, 1\}$, the indices below the number $2$ of
Booleans, onto the Booleans that is inverse to the fixed enumeration of the Booleans.

articles.title: Separator symbol of the verifier
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a
function of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, whose input alphabet is identified with
the pair alphabet $\mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\ \mathrm{Bool}$. This is the symbol of
$V$'s input alphabet that corresponds to the separator $\#$, the element
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{none})$.

articles.title: The accept generator's time bound on the uniform layout
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $k \ge 1$
and $y \ge 1$, the explicit time bound of the accept generator for the layout with all four
constants equal to $k$, with $n_1 = k_1 = k$ and $T = H = y$, is at most $314\,k^5 y^4$.

Every monomial of the bound is at most $k^5 y^4$, and the coefficients sum to $314$, the value of
the bound at $k = y = 1$.

articles.title: Explicit time bound of the accept generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$,
$K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and natural numbers $n_1$, $k_1$, $T$, $H$, let
$W = A + K H g$ and $V = (T + 1) W$ (the number of variables). The bound is $P + (g + n_1)\,C$,
where $C = V(3V + 6) + 10V + 13$ is the cost of one clause and the precomputation cost is
$P = 3 + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + (K(2Hg + 3) + K + 2) + (T(2W + 3) + T + 2) + 1 +
((T + 1)(2W + 3) + (T + 1) + 2) + (2TW + 2) + 2 + (k_1(2Hg + 3) + k_1 + 2)$.

It is at most $314\,(A + K + g + n_1 + k_1 + 1)^5\,(T + H + 1)^4$.

articles.title: Constant of the accept generator's time bound
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size
$A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and natural numbers $n_1$, $k_1$, the constant is
$314\,(A + K + g + n_1 + k_1 + 1)^5$.

articles.title: The accept family of a layout
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks
and $g$ symbol codes, let $n_1, a, k_1, e, T, H$ be natural numbers, $W = A + K H g$ and
$V = (T + 1) W$. The accept family is the CNF formula over $V$ variables made of, first, for each
$u < n_1$ in increasing order, the clause whose only literal is the label variable $X[T, u]$
(variable $T W + u$), positive if $u = a$ and negative otherwise; then, for each $x < g$ in
increasing order, the clause whose only literal is the top-cell variable $C[T, k_1, 0, x]$ of
stack $k_1$ (variable $T W + A + k_1 H g + x$), positive if $x = e$ and negative otherwise. Each
clause is a dense row of $V$ slots: the slot of its variable holds the literal and every other
slot is empty (all slots are empty if the variable is at least $V$).

articles.title: The concrete accept family is a layout-level accept family
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite
multi-stack Turing machine with encoding $E$, let $\mathit{acc}$ be a symbol of the output stack
of $M$, and let $T$, $H$ be natural numbers. The accept family of $E$ for $\mathit{acc}$ at $T$,
$H$ equals, by definition, the accept family of the layout of $E$ at $T$, $H$ with parameters
$n_1 = A_0$, the number of (label, state) codes of $E$; $a$, the (label, state) code of the
halted configuration (no label, initial state); $k_1$, the number $E$ gives the output stack; and
$e$, the code of $\mathit{acc}$.

articles.title: Time bound of the accept generator for a concrete machine
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite
multi-stack Turing machine with encoding $E$, let $\mathit{acc}$ be a symbol of the output stack
of $M$, and let $T$, $H$ be natural numbers with $H > 0$. Let $L$ be the layout of $E$, with
label block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $A_0$ be the number of (label, state)
codes of $E$, let $k_1$ be the number $E$ gives the output stack, and let
$c = 314\,(A + K + g + A_0 + k_1 + 1)^5$. Start the accept generator for $L$, $A_0$, the code of
the halted configuration, $k_1$ and the code of $\mathit{acc}$ at its start label, with internal
state false, $T$ and $H$ in unary on its counters $T_n$ and $H_s$, all other counters empty and
an arbitrary bit list $o$ on its output stack. Within at most $c\,(T + H + 1)^4$ steps it reaches
the label done, with some internal state, and its output stack then holds the binary encoding of
the accept family of $E$ for $\mathit{acc}$ at $T$, $H$ followed by $o$.

articles.title: Correctness of the accept generator, with its explicit time bound
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout
with label block size $A$ and $K$ stacks, and let $n_1, a, k_1, e, T, H$ be natural numbers with
$n_1 \le A$, $k_1 < K$ and $H > 0$. Start the accept generator for $L$, $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$ at
its start label, with internal state false, $T$ and $H$ in unary on its counters $T_n$ and $H_s$,
all other counters empty and an arbitrary bit list $o$ on its output stack. Within a number of
steps at most the explicit time bound for $L$, $n_1$, $k_1$, $T$, $H$, it reaches the label done,
with some internal state, and its output stack then holds the binary encoding of the accept family
of $L$ for $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$ at $T$, $H$ followed by $o$.

The hypotheses say that the code block fits in the label block, that $k_1$ is a stack, and that
there is a top cell.

articles.title: Polynomial time bound of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size
$A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $n_1, a, k_1, e, T, H$ be natural numbers with
$n_1 \le A$, $k_1 < K$ and $H > 0$, and let $c = 314\,(A + K + g + n_1 + k_1 + 1)^5$. Start the
accept generator for $L$, $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$ at its start label, with internal state false,
$T$ and $H$ in unary on its counters $T_n$ and $H_s$, all other counters empty and an arbitrary
bit list $o$ on its output stack. Within at most $c\,(T + H + 1)^4$ steps it reaches the label
done, with some internal state, and its output stack then holds the binary encoding of the accept
family of $L$ for $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$ at $T$, $H$ followed by $o$.

articles.title: The accept generator as a finite multi-stack machine
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol
codes and natural numbers $n_1, a, k_1, e$, this is the finite multi-stack Turing machine whose
stacks are an output stack of bits and one unary counter for each of the generator's sixteen
counter names, whose input stack is the counter $T_n$ and output stack the bit stack, whose labels
are the generator's labels for $n_1$ code clauses and $g$ cell clauses with start label the first
precomputation stage, whose internal states are booleans with initial state false, and whose
transition function is the accept generator for $L$, $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$.

It serves only to check that the generator meets the finiteness conditions of a finite machine.

articles.title: Clause kinds of the accept generator
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n_1$ and $g$, a clause kind is
either a code clause $u$ for some $u < n_1$ or a cell clause $x$ for some $x < g$.

articles.title: Base counter of an accept clause
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$ of the accept generator, the
base counter of its single literal is the counter $\mathsf{TW}$ when $c$ is a code clause and
the counter $\mathsf{CB}$ when $c$ is a cell clause.

articles.title: Entry label of an accept cell clause
articles.statement:
For a generator with $n_1$ code clauses and $g$ cell
clauses and $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the cell-chain label at $x$ is the entry label of cell clause $x$
when $x < g$, and the start of the code chain when $x \ge g$.

articles.title: Literals of an accept cell clause
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$, a stack $k_1$, a symbol code $e_a$,
a time $T$, a height $H$ and $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the literal list of cell clause $x$ is the single
literal whose variable is the cell variable $C[T, k_1, 0, x]$ (time $T$, stack $k_1$, depth $0$
from the top, symbol code $x$, for height $H$) and which is positive exactly when $x = e_a$.

articles.title: Run of the accept cell chain
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes, let
$n_1, a_c, k_1, e_a \in \mathbb{N}$ be the parameters of the generator, and let $F$ give a value
to every counter of the generator such that the scratch counters $\mathsf{Q}$, $\mathsf{tmp}$,
$\mathsf{md}$, $\mathsf{c1}$, $\mathsf{c2}$ are $0$, $F(\mathsf{Vc}) = V$, $F(\mathsf{P}) = 0$,
$F(\mathsf{TW}) + n_1 \le V$ and $F(\mathsf{CB}) + g \le V$. Write
$B(V) = V(3V + 6) + 10V + 13$ for the one-clause step bound. Then for every $x < g$, every
output stack $o$ and every state bit $v$, the generator started at the entry label of cell
clause $x$ with state $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$ reaches the halting label $\mathrm{done}$
within $(x + 1)B(V) + n_1 B(V)$ steps, with state false, counters $F$, and output consisting of
the encodings of the dense clauses over $V$ variables whose single literal is at
$F(\mathsf{TW}) + u$, positive exactly when $u = a_c$, for $u = 0, \dots, n_1 - 1$, then of
those whose single literal is at $F(\mathsf{CB}) + y$, positive exactly when $y = e_a$, for
$y = 0, \dots, x$, then $o$.

articles.title: Counters of the accept generator
articles.statement:
The accept-family generator has sixteen distinct unit
counters, named $\mathsf{Tn}$, $\mathsf{Hs}$, $\mathsf{Gc}$, $\mathsf{HG}$, $\mathsf{Wc}$,
$\mathsf{Kc}$, $\mathsf{K1}$, $\mathsf{Vc}$, $\mathsf{TW}$, $\mathsf{CB}$, $\mathsf{P}$,
$\mathsf{Q}$, $\mathsf{tmp}$, $\mathsf{md}$, $\mathsf{c1}$ and $\mathsf{c2}$.

articles.title: Step bound for one accept clause
articles.statement:
For $V \in \mathbb{N}$, the step budget for one clause of
the accept generator is $B(V) = V(3V + 6) + 10V + 13$.

articles.title: One clause of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes, let
$n_1, a, k_1, e, V \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $c$ be a clause kind of the accept generator (a code
clause $u < n_1$ or a cell clause $x < g$) with base counter $b(c)$, offset $\mathrm{off}(c)$ and
polarity $\sigma(c)$ for $a$ and $e$. Let $F$ be counter values of the generator whose scratch
counters $\mathsf{Q}$, $\mathsf{tmp}$, $\mathsf{md}$, $\mathsf{c1}$, $\mathsf{c2}$ are $0$, with
$F(\mathsf{Vc}) = V$, $F(\mathsf{P}) = 0$ and $p = F(b(c)) + \mathrm{off}(c) < V$. Then for every
output word $o$ and every Boolean state $v$, the accept generator for $L$, $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$
runs in at most $V(3V + 6) + 10V + 13$ steps from the label $\mathrm{e00}(c)$, with state $v$,
counters $F$ and output $o$, to the label after clause $c$, with state false, the same counters
$F$, and output the encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables whose only literal is the
variable $p$ with polarity $\sigma(c)$, followed by $o$.

articles.title: Entry label of an accept code clause
articles.statement:
For a generator with $n_1$ code clauses and $g$ cell
clauses and $u \in \mathbb{N}$, the code-chain label at $u$ is the entry label of code clause $u$
when $u < n_1$, and the halting label $\mathrm{done}$ when $u \ge n_1$.

articles.title: Literals of an accept code clause
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$, a code $a_c$, a time $T$, a height $H$
and $u \in \mathbb{N}$, the literal list of code clause $u$ is the single literal whose variable
is the label/state variable $X[T, u]$ (entry $u$ of the label/state block at time $T$, for
height $H$) and which is positive exactly when $u = a_c$.

articles.title: Start of the accept code chain
articles.statement:
For a generator with $n_1$ code clauses, the code chain
starts at the entry label of code clause $n_1 - 1$ (the last one, as clauses are emitted last
first), or at the halting label $\mathrm{done}$ when $n_1 = 0$.

articles.title: Run of the code-clause chain of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Let $F$ assign values to the
counters of the accept generator (for layout $L$ and parameters $n_1$, $\mathrm{ac}$, $k_1$,
$\mathrm{ea}$) such that the scratch counters $Q$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $c_1$, $c_2$
are $0$, $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$, $F(P) = 0$ and $F(\mathrm{TW}) + n_1 \le V$. Then for every
$u < n_1$, every output word $o$ and every Boolean state $v$, the generator runs in at most
$(u + 1)(V(3V + 6) + 10V + 13)$ steps from the first label of code clause $u$, with state $v$,
counters $F$ and output $o$, to the halting label $\mathrm{done}$, with state false, counters $F$
and output $w_0 w_1 \cdots w_u\, o$. Here $w_i$ is the encoding of the dense clause over $V$
variables whose only literal is variable $F(\mathrm{TW}) + i$, positive if and only if
$i = \mathrm{ac}$.

articles.title: Labels of the accept generator
articles.statement:
For $n_1, g \in \mathbb{N}$, a label is one of: a
precomputation stage; $\mathrm{e00}(c)$, $\mathrm{cv1}(c)$, $\mathrm{cv2}(c)$ or
$\mathrm{fin}(c)$ for a clause kind $c$ (a code clause $u < n_1$ or a cell clause $x < g$);
$\mathrm{lit}(c, s)$ for a clause kind $c$ and a stage $s$ of the literal routine; or the halting
label $\mathrm{done}$. The labels form a finite type with decidable equality.

articles.title: Initial counters of the accept generator
articles.statement:
For $T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, the initial counter
values are $T$ on the counter $\mathrm{Tn}$, $H$ on the counter $\mathrm{Hs}$, and $0$ on every
other counter.

articles.title: Literal routine of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Fix a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol codes and
parameters $n_1$, $\mathrm{ac}$, $\mathrm{ea}$, and a clause kind $c$ with base counter $b(c)$,
offset $\mathrm{off}(c)$ and polarity $\sigma(c)$. The literal routine of $c$ gives the
generator's statement at each label $\mathrm{lit}(c, s)$; below, a stage $s$ stands for the label
$\mathrm{lit}(c, s)$, and moving a counter onto targets means popping it until it is empty and
pushing one unit onto every target for each unit popped. At $\mathrm{cp1}$ it moves $b(c)$ onto
$Q$ and $\mathrm{tmp}$, then goes to $\mathrm{cp2}$. At $\mathrm{cp2}$ it moves $\mathrm{tmp}$
onto $b(c)$, then goes to $\mathrm{eo}$. At $\mathrm{eo}$ it pushes $\mathrm{off}(c)$ units onto
$Q$ and goes to $\mathrm{dec}$. At $\mathrm{dec}$ it pops $P$ and goes to $\mathrm{bad}$ if $P$
was empty, else to $\mathrm{cmp}$. At $\mathrm{cmp}$ it pops one unit from each nonempty one of
$P$ and $Q$, pushing a unit onto $c_1$ for $P$ and onto $c_2$ for $Q$; it repeats
$\mathrm{cmp}$ if both were nonempty, and otherwise goes to $r(o)$, where the ordering $o$ is
$<$ if only $Q$ was nonempty, $=$ if both were empty, and $>$ if only $P$ was nonempty. At
$r(o)$ it moves $c_1$ onto $P$, then goes to $r_B(o)$. At $r_B(o)$ it moves $c_2$ onto $Q$,
then goes to $\mathrm{slot}$ if $o$ is $=$ and to $\mathrm{emL}$ otherwise. At $\mathrm{emL}$ it
prepends the bits false, true to the output and goes to $\mathrm{dec}$. At $\mathrm{bad}$ it
halts. At $\mathrm{slot}$ it prepends the bits true, $\lnot\sigma(c)$ to the output and goes to
$\mathrm{dq}$. At $\mathrm{dq}$ it empties $Q$, then goes to $\mathrm{fin}(c)$.

articles.title: Run of the literal routine of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Let $c$ be a clause kind with base
counter $b(c)$, offset $\mathrm{off}(c)$ and polarity $\sigma(c)$, and let $F$ assign values to
the counters of the accept generator (for layout $L$ and parameters $n_1$, $\mathrm{ac}$, $k_1$,
$\mathrm{ea}$) such that the scratch counters $Q$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $c_1$, $c_2$
are $0$. Let $q, m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $q = F(b(c)) + \mathrm{off}(c)$ and
$F(P) = q + m + 1$. Then for every output word $o$ and every Boolean state $v$, the generator
runs in at most $m(3q + 6) + 2F(b(c)) + 4q + 9$ steps from the label
$\mathrm{lit}(c, \mathrm{cp1})$, with state $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, to the label
$\mathrm{fin}(c)$, with state false, the counters $F$ except that $P$ holds $q$, and output
$s\,z\,o$. Here $s$ is the two bits true, $\lnot\sigma(c)$ (the encoding of a slot holding a
literal of polarity $\sigma(c)$), and $z$ is $m$ copies of the two bits false, true (the
encoding of $m$ empty slots).

articles.title: Stages of the accept generator's literal routine
articles.statement:
The stages of the accept generator's
routine emitting a clause's literal are $\mathrm{cp1}$, $\mathrm{cp2}$, $\mathrm{eo}$,
$\mathrm{dec}$, $\mathrm{cmp}$, $r(o)$ and $r_B(o)$ for each ordering $o \in \{<, =, >\}$,
$\mathrm{emL}$, $\mathrm{bad}$, $\mathrm{slot}$ and $\mathrm{dq}$. They form a finite type with
decidable equality.

articles.title: Next label after a clause of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Let $n_1, g \in \mathbb{N}$; clauses are
emitted last first. After the code clause $u < n_1$ the generator goes to the halting label
$\mathrm{done}$ if $u = 0$, and otherwise to the first label $\mathrm{e00}$ of code clause
$u - 1$. After the cell clause $x < g$ it goes, if $x = 0$, to the start of the code chain (the
first label of code clause $n_1 - 1$, or $\mathrm{done}$ if $n_1 = 0$), and otherwise to the
first label of cell clause $x - 1$.

articles.title: Offset of a clause's literal
articles.statement:
For $n_1, g \in \mathbb{N}$, the offset of a clause kind of
the accept generator is its index: $u$ for the code clause $u < n_1$ and $x$ for the cell clause
$x < g$. It is the distance of the clause's single literal from its base counter.

articles.title: Cost of the precomputation of the accept generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $A$
label/state variables per row, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and for $k_1, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$,
let $W = A + KHg$ be the row width. The step budget of the precomputation is
$3 + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + (K(2Hg + 3) + K + 2) + (T(2W + 3) + T + 2) + 1 +
((T + 1)(2W + 3) + (T + 1) + 2) + (2TW + 2) + 2 + (k_1(2Hg + 3) + k_1 + 2)$.

articles.title: Counters after the precomputation of the accept generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $A$
label/state variables per row, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and for $k_1, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$,
let $W = A + KHg$ be the row width. The counter values after the precomputation are $T + 1$ on
$\mathrm{Tn}$, $H$ on $\mathrm{Hs}$, $g$ on $\mathrm{Gc}$, $Hg$ on $\mathrm{HG}$, $W$ on
$\mathrm{Wc}$, $K$ on $\mathrm{Kc}$, $k_1$ on $\mathrm{K1}$, $(T + 1)W$ on $\mathrm{Vc}$, $TW$ on
$\mathrm{TW}$, $TW + A + k_1Hg$ on $\mathrm{CB}$ (the index of the cell variable of stack $k_1$,
depth $0$ and symbol code $0$ at time $T$), and $0$ on every other counter.

articles.title: Run of the accept generator's precomputation
articles.statement:
Fix a layout $L$ with label/state block
size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and naturals $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$. For all
$T, H \in \mathbb{N}$ and every list $o$ of Booleans, write $W = A + K H g$ for the row width.
The accept generator, started at its first precomputation label with internal state false,
output $o$, $T$ units on counter $\mathsf{Tn}$, $H$ units on $\mathsf{Hs}$ and every other
counter empty, reaches in at most $\mathrm{preB}(L, k_1, T, H)$ steps the first clause label
with internal state false, output still $o$, and counters $\mathsf{Tn} = T + 1$,
$\mathsf{Hs} = H$, $\mathsf{Gc} = g$, $\mathsf{HG} = H g$, $\mathsf{Wc} = W$, $\mathsf{Kc} = K$,
$\mathsf{K1} = k_1$, $\mathsf{Vc} = (T + 1) W$, $\mathsf{TW} = T W$,
$\mathsf{CB} = T W + A + k_1 H g$, and every other counter empty.

articles.title: Generator machine for the accept family
articles.statement:
Fix a layout $L$ with label/state block size
$A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and naturals $n_1$, $a$, $k_1$, $e$. The generator is a
multi-stack machine with a Boolean output stack, the unit counters of the generator, and a
Boolean internal state. Its precomputation pushes $g$ units on $\mathsf{Gc}$, adds
$\mathsf{Hs} \cdot \mathsf{Gc}$ to $\mathsf{HG}$, pushes $A$ units on $\mathsf{Wc}$, pushes $K$
units on $\mathsf{Kc}$, adds $\mathsf{Kc} \cdot \mathsf{HG}$ to $\mathsf{Wc}$, adds
$\mathsf{Tn} \cdot \mathsf{Wc}$ to $\mathsf{TW}$, pushes one unit on $\mathsf{Tn}$, adds
$\mathsf{Tn} \cdot \mathsf{Wc}$ to $\mathsf{Vc}$, drains $\mathsf{TW}$ onto both $\mathsf{CB}$
and $\mathsf{tmp}$ and then $\mathsf{tmp}$ back onto $\mathsf{TW}$, pushes $A$ units on
$\mathsf{CB}$, pushes $k_1$ units on $\mathsf{K1}$, adds $\mathsf{K1} \cdot \mathsf{HG}$ to
$\mathsf{CB}$, and goes to the first clause label; each multiplication uses $\mathsf{md}$ as
its index counter and $\mathsf{tmp}$ as scratch. For each clause $c$ (a code clause of $u < n_1$
or a cell clause of $x < g$) it prepends $[\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{false}]$ to the output,
drains $\mathsf{Vc}$ onto both $\mathsf{P}$ and $\mathsf{tmp}$ and then $\mathsf{tmp}$ back onto
$\mathsf{Vc}$, runs the literal routine of $c$ with polarity parameters $a$ and $e$, drains
$\mathsf{P}$ while prepending $[\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}]$ to the output once per unit, and
goes to the label after $c$. At its final label it halts.

It is meant to be started with $T$ on $\mathsf{Tn}$, $H$ on $\mathsf{Hs}$ and every other
counter empty.

articles.title: Precomputation stages of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Write $A$, $K$ and $g$ for the
label/state block size, the number of stacks and the number of symbol codes of the generator's
layout, and $k_1$ for the index of the stack whose top cell it checks. A precomputation stage is
one of eight plain stages or one of five multiplication stages, each of which carries a stage $s$
of the multiplication routine. Named by the step the generator takes there, in the order it runs
them, they are: push $g$ units on $\mathsf{Gc}$; multiply into $\mathsf{HG}$ at $s$; push $A$
units on $\mathsf{Wc}$; push $K$ units on $\mathsf{Kc}$; multiply into $\mathsf{Wc}$ at $s$;
multiply into $\mathsf{TW}$ at $s$; increment $\mathsf{Tn}$; multiply into $\mathsf{Vc}$ at $s$;
drain $\mathsf{TW}$ onto both $\mathsf{CB}$ and $\mathsf{tmp}$; drain $\mathsf{tmp}$ back onto
$\mathsf{TW}$; push $A$ units on $\mathsf{CB}$; push $k_1$ units on $\mathsf{K1}$; multiply into
$\mathsf{CB}$ at $s$.

articles.title: Empty scratch counters of the accept generator
articles.statement:
An assignment $F$ of a natural number to
each counter of the generator satisfies this predicate when $F$ is zero on the scratch counters
$\mathsf{Q}$, $\mathsf{tmp}$, $\mathsf{md}$, $\mathsf{c1}$ and $\mathsf{c2}$.

The generator keeps these counters empty whenever a clause starts.

articles.title: Polarity of an accept clause's literal
articles.statement:
Fix naturals $n_1$ and $g$, and let $a$ and $e$
be naturals. The polarity of the code clause of $u < n_1$ is true exactly when $u = a$, and the
polarity of the cell clause of $x < g$ is true exactly when $x = e$.

articles.title: First clause label of the accept generator
articles.statement:
Fix naturals $n_1$ and $g$, the numbers
of code clauses and of cell clauses. Clauses are emitted last first, so the label at which clause
emission starts is the start label of the cell clause of $g - 1$ when $g > 0$. When $g = 0$ it is
the start label of the code clause of $n_1 - 1$ if $n_1 > 0$, and the final label if $n_1 = 0$.

articles.title: Label after a literal routine
articles.statement:
For block $(i, k)$ of the cell-shift generator, a clause
kind $c$ and $l \in \mathbb{N}$, with the literals of a clause emitted from the last down to the
first: the label is the finishing stage of clause $c$ in block $(i, k)$ when $l = 0$; otherwise it
is the first stage of the routine for literal $l - 1$ of $c$ in block $(i, k)$ when $l - 1 < 3$,
and the final label $\mathrm{done}$, at which the generator halts, otherwise.

articles.title: Loop body of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol codes and a block
$(i, k)$, the generator's statement at each loop-body stage, with flag $b$ true in the in-range
loop and false in the overflow loop: add the counter $KB$ to the counter $CB$; when $b$ is true,
add the product of the counters $U$ and $Gc$ to $CB$; add $CB$ and then the counter $Wc$ to the
counter $CW$; then start the in-range clauses for the symbols $x = g - 1, \dots, 0$ when $b$ is
true, and the overflow clause otherwise. A clause $c$ (in-range, overflow or pushed fill)
prepends the terminator $00$ to the output, adds the counter $Vc$ to the counter $P$, runs the
literal routines of $c$ from the last down to the first, drains $P$ prepending $01$ per unit, and
goes on to the next clause of its chain; after the last pushed-fill clause it returns to the
fill drain of the block setup, and after the last in-range clause and after the overflow clause
the drain stages empty $CB$ and then $CW$ and return to the head of the in-range loop when $b$ is
true, and of the overflow loop otherwise.

articles.title: Loop-body stages of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a symbol count $g$ and a window depth
$d$, the finite type of stages of the loop body of an $(i, k)$ block: for each flag $b$, two
stages adding the block base, four stages building the second base and two drain stages; one
stage for each stage of the multiplication routine; and for each clause kind $c$ (over $g$ and
$d$), a terminator stage, two stages loading the variable count, one stage for each literal
position $l < 3$ and each stage of the literal routine, and a finishing stage. The flag $b$ is
true in the in-range loop and false in the overflow loop.

articles.title: Encoded blocks of one situation
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $KK$ stacks, family data
$sa, pl, cn, pu$ and $T, H, t, i \in \mathbb{N}$, the bit string obtained by concatenating, for
$k = 0, \dots, KK - 1$ in order, the encoding of the clause block of situation $i$, stack $k$ at
time $t$.

articles.title: Encoded blocks of one time step
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$, family data $sa, pl, cn, pu$ and
$N, T, H, t \in \mathbb{N}$, the bit string obtained by concatenating, for situations
$i = 0, \dots, N - 1$ in order, the encoded blocks of situation $i$ at time $t$.

articles.title: Counter state at the start of a block
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol codes,
$T, H, t \in \mathbb{N}$ and counter contents $F$: $F$ is a loop-body counter state for
$L, T, H, t$, the counters $KB$, $U$, $Ui$, $R$, $Ri$, $Ka$, $CB$ and $CW$ are empty, $HG$ holds
$H \cdot g$ and $Hs$ holds $H$.

articles.title: Boundary before a literal
articles.statement:
For $V, n, l \in \mathbb{N}$ and literal positions
$pos : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the boundary before literal $l$ is $pos(l)$ if $l < n$, and $V$
otherwise.

articles.title: Counter state of a loop body
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$, $KK$ stacks and
$g$ symbol codes, $T, H, t \in \mathbb{N}$ and counter contents $F$, let $W = A + KK \cdot H g$ be
the row width. The condition holds when the scratch counters $Q$, $tmp$, $md$, $c_1$, $c_2$ and
the counter $P$ are empty, $Vc$ holds the variable count $(T + 1) W$, $Gc$ holds $g$, $Wc$ holds
$W$, $TW$ holds $t W$ and $TW1$ holds $(t + 1) W$.

articles.title: Base counter of a literal
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$ and $l \in \mathbb{N}$: if $c$ is an
in-range shift clause, literal $l$ has base $cb$ when $l = 0$, $s$ when $l = 1$ and $cw$ when
$l \ge 2$; if $c$ is an overflow or pushed-fill clause, it has base $s$ when $l = 0$ and $cw$
otherwise.

articles.title: Base counters of literal positions
articles.statement:
The three bases $s$, $cb$ and $cw$ from which a literal
position is computed; at time step $t$, with $W$ the row width, $s$ stands for the counter
$TW1 = (t + 1) \cdot W$ and serves the situation variable.

articles.title: Counters of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
The type with 23 elements, one for each unit counter
of the counter machine that emits the cell-shift clause family: $\mathrm{Tn}$, $\mathrm{Ti}$,
$\mathrm{Hs}$, $\mathrm{Gc}$, $\mathrm{HG}$, $\mathrm{Wc}$, $\mathrm{Vc}$, $\mathrm{TW}$,
$\mathrm{TW1}$, $\mathrm{KB}$, $\mathrm{U}$, $\mathrm{Ui}$, $\mathrm{R}$, $\mathrm{Ri}$,
$\mathrm{CB}$, $\mathrm{CW}$, $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$,
$\mathrm{Ka}$, $\mathrm{c1}$ and $\mathrm{c2}$.

articles.title: Clause kinds of the cell-shift family
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g$ and $d$, a clause kind is
either an in-range shift clause $\mathrm{sh}(x)$ for a symbol code $x < g$, the overflow-fill
clause $\mathrm{ov}$, or a pushed-fill clause $\mathrm{pf}(j)$ for a pushed depth $j < d$. These
are the kinds of clause in the block of a situation $i$ and a stack $k$.

articles.title: Step bound for one clause
articles.statement:
For a natural number $V$ (the number of variables), the step
bound for one clause of at most three literals is $V(3V + 6) + 3(6V + 9) + 3V + 4$, where
$6V + 9$ is the per-literal cost apart from the gap loop.

articles.title: One clause of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be the cell-shift generator for a layout
$L$ with $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, situation offsets $\mathrm{sa}$, push
counts $\mathrm{pl}$, consumed counts $\mathrm{cn}$, pushed codes $\mathrm{pu}$ and $N$
situations. Fix a situation $i < N$, a stack $k < K$, a clause kind $c$ with parameters $g$ and
$d$ and with $n$ literals, positions $\mathrm{pos} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, counter values $F$
and $V \in \mathbb{N}$. For each $l \in \mathbb{N}$ let $b_l$ be the counter holding the base of
literal $l$ of $c$ and $o_l$ the constant offset of literal $l$ of $c$ in block $(i, k)$. Assume
that the scratch counters $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $\mathrm{c1}$ and
$\mathrm{c2}$ are zero in $F$; that $\mathrm{pos}(l) = F(b_l) + o_l$ and $F(b_l) \le V$ for every
$l \in \mathbb{N}$; that $\mathrm{pos}(l) < \mathrm{pos}(l + 1)$ whenever $l + 1 < n$ and
$\mathrm{pos}(n - 1) < V$; and that $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$ and $F(\mathrm{P}) = 0$. Then for every
output word $w$ and flag $v$, $M$ runs in at most $V(3V + 6) + 3(6V + 9) + 3V + 4$ steps (the step
bound for one clause) from the configuration with label $\mathrm{e00}(c)$ of block $(i, k)$, flag
$v$, counter values $F$ and output $w$ to the configuration with the label that follows clause $c$
in block $(i, k)$, flag false, counter values $F$ and output $e$ followed by $w$, where $e$ is the
encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables whose literals are those of $c$ at positions
$\mathrm{pos}$.

articles.title: Literals of a clause kind at given positions
articles.statement:
Let $c$ be a clause kind with $n$ literals
($n = 3$ for an in-range shift clause, $n = 2$ for an overflow-fill or pushed-fill clause) and let
$\mathrm{pos} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. The literals of $c$ at positions $\mathrm{pos}$ are the
list $(\mathrm{pos}(0), b_0), \dots, (\mathrm{pos}(n - 1), b_{n - 1})$ of variable-sign pairs,
where the sign $b_l$ is true (a positive literal) exactly when $l = n - 1$.

articles.title: Constant offsets of the literals of a clause kind
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be the number of symbol codes
of the clause kinds, and let $s, p, c \in \mathbb{N}$ and $q : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
(situation offset, push count, consumed count and pushed codes). The constant offset of literal
$l$ is: for an in-range shift clause $\mathrm{sh}(x)$, $cg + x$ if $l = 0$, $s$ if $l = 1$ and
$pg + x$ otherwise; for the overflow-fill clause $\mathrm{ov}$, $s$ if $l = 0$ and $pg$
otherwise; for a pushed-fill clause $\mathrm{pf}(j)$, $s$ if $l = 0$ and $jg + q(j)$
otherwise.

articles.title: Constant offset of a literal in a block
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol
codes and window depth $d$, let $N \in \mathbb{N}$ be the number of situations, and let
$\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$ and $\mathrm{pu}$ give the situation offsets, push
counts, consumed counts and pushed codes. For a situation $i < N$, a stack $k < K$, a clause kind
$c$ with parameters $g$ and $d$, and $l \in \mathbb{N}$, the constant offset of literal $l$ of $c$
in block $(i, k)$ is the constant offset of literal $l$ of $c$ with situation offset
$\mathrm{sa}(i)$, push count $\mathrm{pl}(i, k)$, consumed count $\mathrm{cn}(i, k)$ and pushed
codes $j \mapsto \mathrm{pu}(i, k, j)$.

articles.title: Coverage of target depths
articles.statement:
Let $p, c, H$ be natural numbers with $p \le H$ and $c \le H$,
and let $m = \max(p, c)$. Every natural number $j < H$ satisfies $j < p$, or $j = u + p$ for some
natural number $u < H - m$, or $j = H - c + p + r$ for some natural number $r < c - p$, where
$c - p$ is truncated subtraction (zero when $c \le p$).

In the cell-shift family these are the pushed-fill, in-range and overflow target depths of a
stack in the row after a time step.

articles.title: Bounds on in-range and overflow target depths
articles.statement:
Let $p, c, H$ be natural numbers with
$p \le H$ and $c \le H$, and let $m = \max(p, c)$. For every natural number $u < H - m$ we have
$p \le u + p$, $u + p < H - c + p$ and $u + p < H$. For every natural number $r < c - p$, where
$c - p$ is truncated subtraction, we have $H - m + p = H - c + p$ and $H - c + p + r < H$.

articles.title: Labels of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $N$, $K$, $g$ and $d$, a label is
one of: a precomputation stage $\mathrm{pre}(s)$; a time-loop label $\mathrm{tHead}$,
$\mathrm{tRest}$, $\mathrm{tw}(s)$ for a multiplication stage $s$, $\mathrm{t1a}$,
$\mathrm{t1b}$, $\mathrm{t1c}$, $\mathrm{t1d}$, $\mathrm{tEnd}$ or $\mathrm{tEnd2}$; a setup or
loop stage $\mathrm{s}(i, k, x)$ of the block of situation $i < N$ and stack $k < K$; a decrement
step $\mathrm{sb}(i, k, r)$ with $r < d + 1$; a loop-body stage $\mathrm{b}(i, k, x)$ of that
block, over clause kinds with parameters $g$ and $d$; or a halting label $\mathrm{bad}$ or
$\mathrm{done}$.

articles.title: Entry label of the situation chain
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, with $N$ the number of
situations and $K$ the number of stacks, this is the end-of-time-step label when $n = 0$ or
$K = 0$; the first setup stage of block $(n - 1, K - 1)$ when $1 \le n \le N$ and $K \ge 1$;
and the terminal (halting) label when $n > N$ and $K \ge 1$. For $n \le N$ it is the label
from which the generator emits the blocks of situations $i < n$ and then ends the time step.

articles.title: Step budget for one block of the shift generator
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g$, $K$, $H$,
$d$ and $V$ (in use: the number of symbol codes, the number of stacks, the stack height, the
window depth and the number of variables), the budget is

$$
1 + (2V + 2) + 1 + \bigl(K(2V + 3) + K + 2\bigr) + (K + 1) + (2H + 2) + d + 1 +
\bigl((2V + 2) + (2V + 2) + d\,c(V) + (V + 1)\bigr) + \bigl(d\,(o + 1) + d + 2\bigr) +
\bigl(H\,(s + 1) + H + 2\bigr) + (H + 1) + (d + 1) + (V + 1),
$$

where $c(V)$ is the step budget of one clause, $o$ is the step budget $o(g, H, d, V)$ of one
iteration of the overflow loop, and $s$ is the step budget $s(g, H, V)$ of one iteration of
the in-range loop.

articles.title: Correctness of the shift generator on one block
articles.statement:
Let $t < T$, assume the
well-formedness conditions for $N$ situations and stack height $H$, let $i < N$ and $k < K$,
where $K$ is the number of stacks, and let $F$ be counter values satisfying the block-start
conditions at time $t$. Then for every output $o$ and every Boolean state $v$, the generator,
started at the first setup stage of block $(i, k)$ with state $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$,
reaches in at most $B$ steps the entry label of the stacks $< k$ of situation $i$, with state
false, counters $F$ and output $e$ followed by $o$. Here $e$ is the encoding of the clause block
of situation $i$, stack $k$ at time $t$, and $B$ is the step budget for one block with
$V = (T + 1) W$ variables, $W$ being the number of variables per time step.

articles.title: Entry label of the stack chain of a situation
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $i$ and $n$, with $N$
the number of situations and $K$ the number of stacks, this is the entry label of the situation
chain for $i$ when $n = 0$; the first setup stage of block $(i, n - 1)$ when $1 \le n \le K$ and
$i < N$; and the terminal (halting) label otherwise. For $i < N$ and $n \le K$ it is the label
from which the generator emits the blocks of stacks $k < n$ of situation $i$ and then the blocks
of situations $< i$.

articles.title: Initial counter values of the shift generator
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $T$ and $H$, the
assignment of counter values that puts $T$ on the time-bound input counter, $H$ on the
stack-height input counter, and $0$ on every other counter of the generator.

articles.title: Correctness of the shift generator on the situation chain
articles.statement:
Let $t < T$, assume the
well-formedness conditions for $N$ situations and stack height $H$, and let $F$ be counter
values satisfying the block-start conditions at time $t$. Then for every $n \le N$, every
output $o$ and every Boolean state $v$, there is a Boolean state $v'$ such that the generator,
started at the entry label of the situation chain for $n$ with state $v$, counters $F$ and
output $o$, reaches in at most $n \cdot (K \cdot B)$ steps the end-of-time-step label with
state $v'$, counters $F$ and output $e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$ followed by $o$. Here $K$ is the
number of stacks, $e_i$ is the concatenated encoding of the clause blocks of situation $i$ for
the stacks $0, \dots, K - 1$ at time $t$, and $B$ is the step budget for one block with
$V = (T + 1) W$ variables, $W$ being the number of variables per time step.

articles.title: Counter holding a literal base
articles.statement:
The map from the three kinds of literal base to
counters of the generator. With $t$ the current time step and $W$ the number of variables per
time step, the situation base goes to the counter holding $(t + 1) W$, the start of row
$t + 1$; the current-row cell base goes to the cell-base counter; and the next-row cell base
goes to the counter holding the cell base plus $W$.

articles.title: First cell variable of a block
articles.statement:
For a layout with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks
and $g$ symbol codes, a stack height $H$, a time $t$ and a stack $k$, this is the number
$k \cdot (H g) + (t W + A)$, where $W = A + K H g$ is the number of variables per time step.
It is the index of the variable for depth $0$ and symbol code $0$ of stack $k$ in row $t$.

articles.title: Correctness of the shift generator on the stack chain of a situation
articles.statement:
Let $t < T$,
assume the well-formedness conditions for $N$ situations and stack height $H$, let $i < N$,
and let $F$ be counter values satisfying the block-start conditions at time $t$. Then for
every $n \le K$, where $K$ is the number of stacks, every output $o$ and every Boolean state
$v$, there is a Boolean state $v'$ such that the generator, started at the entry label of the
stacks $< n$ of situation $i$ with state $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, reaches in at most
$n \cdot B$ steps the entry label of the situation chain for $i$, with state $v'$, counters $F$
and output $e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$ followed by $o$. Here $e_k$ is the encoding of the clause
block of situation $i$, stack $k$ at time $t$, and $B$ is the step budget for one block with
$V = (T + 1) W$ variables, $W$ being the number of variables per time step.

articles.title: Labels of the shift generator
articles.statement:
For a layout with $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and
window depth $d$, and a number $N$ of situations, the labels of the generator are the finite
label type with parameters $N$, $K$, $g$ and $d$.

articles.title: Per-literal step overhead of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For $V \in \mathbb{N}$, the
per-literal overhead is $6V + 9$.

It is the step budget for emitting one literal of a clause over $V$ variables, not counting the
loop that emits the gap before the literal.

articles.title: Entry label of a literal routine of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a situation $i < N$, a
stack $k < K$, a clause kind $c$ and $l \in \mathbb{N}$, the entry label of literal $l$ is the
first stage of the routine emitting literal $l$ of a clause of kind $c$ in block $(i, k)$ when
$l < 3$, and the generator's final label when $l \ge 3$ (that case is never used).

articles.title: Literal routine of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a situation $i < N$, a stack $k < K$, a
clause kind $c$ and a literal index $l < 3$, this is the program fragment, indexed by the stages
of the literal routine, that emits literal $l$ of clause $c$ in block $(i, k)$. Write $B$ for the
base counter of literal $l$ and $a$ for its constant offset in block $(i, k)$. Started with $Q$
and the scratch counters empty, the routine copies the value $b$ of $B$ into the counter $Q$
through a scratch counter, restoring $B$, and adds $a$, so that $Q = b + a$. It then repeats:
decrement the counter $P$, halting if $P$ is already $0$; compare $P$ with $Q$ through two
scratch counters, restoring both; if they differ, push the absent-slot code $01$ onto the output
and repeat; if they are equal, push the slot code of a literal whose sign is positive exactly
when $l$ is the last literal of $c$. Finally it empties $Q$ and jumps to the routine of literal
$l - 1$, or to the end of the clause when $l = 0$.

articles.title: One literal routine of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $i < N$ be a situation, $k < K$ a
stack, $c$ a clause kind and $l < 3$ a literal index. Let $F$ be counter values whose scratch
counters ($Q$, the copy buffer, the multiplication buffer and the two comparison buffers) are
$0$, let $b$ be the value under $F$ of the base counter of literal $l$, and let $a$ be the
constant offset of literal $l$ of $c$ in block $(i, k)$. Let $q, m \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy
$q = b + a$ and $F(P) = q + m + 1$. Then for every output $o$ and internal state $v$, the
generator goes in at most $m(3q + 6) + 2b + 4q + 9$ steps from the start of the routine of
literal $l$, with state $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, to the start of the routine of literal
$l - 1$ (the end-of-clause label of $c$ when $l = 0$), with state false, counters $F$ except
that $P = q$, and output the slot code of literal $l$ (sign positive exactly when $l$ is the last
literal of $c$), followed by $m$ copies of $01$, followed by $o$.

articles.title: The literal routines of one clause of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
Fix $V \in \mathbb{N}$, a
situation $i < N$, a stack $k < K$, a clause kind $c$ with $n$ literals, positions
$p : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, counter values $F$ whose scratch counters are $0$, and an output
$o$. Suppose that for every $l$ the position $p(l)$ is the value under $F$ of the base counter of
literal $l$ plus its constant offset in block $(i, k)$, that this base value is at most $V$, that
$p(l) < p(l + 1)$ whenever $l + 1 < n$, and that $p(n - 1) < V$ if $n \ge 1$. Let
$\beta(l) = p(l)$ for $l < n$ and $\beta(l) = V$ otherwise, and let $E(l)$ be the gap encoding,
from slot $\beta(l)$ up to $V$, of literals $l, \dots, n - 1$ of $c$ at positions $p$, each
with sign positive exactly when it is the last literal. Then for every $l \le n$ and every
internal state $v$ there is a state $v'$ such that the generator goes in at most
$\beta(l)(3V + 6) + l(6V + 9)$ steps from the start of the routine of literal $l - 1$ (the
end-of-clause label of $c$ when $l = 0$), with state $v$, counters $F$ except that
$P = \beta(l)$, and output $E(l)$ followed by $00$ and $o$, to the end-of-clause label of $c$,
with state $v'$, counters $F$ except that $P = \beta(0)$, and output $E(0)$ followed by $00$
and $o$.

articles.title: Stages of the cell-shift literal routine
articles.statement:
The routine emitting one literal has fifteen
stages: two copy stages, an offset stage, a decrement stage, a compare stage, two restore stages
for each comparison outcome (less, equal, greater), an absent-slot emission stage, a failure
stage, a slot emission stage and a drain stage.

articles.title: Increasing literal positions below a bound
articles.statement:
For $p : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and
$n, V \in \mathbb{N}$, the positions $p$ are increasing for $n$ literals below $V$ when
$p(l) < p(l + 1)$ for every $l$ with $l + 1 < n$, and $p(n - 1) < V$ if $n \ge 1$.

articles.title: Label after a clause of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a situation $i < N$ and a stack
$k < K$, in block $(i, k)$: after the in-range clause for symbol $x$ the generator goes to the
start of the in-range clause for symbol $x - 1$, or to the in-range drains when $x = 0$; after
the overflow clause it goes to the overflow drains; after the pushed-fill clause for depth $j$
it goes to the start of the pushed-fill clause for depth $j - 1$, or to the pushed-fill drains
when $j = 0$.

articles.title: Number of literals of a cell-shift clause kind
articles.statement:
An in-range shift clause has $3$
literals, and an overflow clause and a pushed-fill clause have $2$ each.

articles.title: Step budget of one overflow iteration of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For
$g, H, d, V \in \mathbb{N}$, the budget is

$$(2H + 2) + (2d + 2) + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + (H + 1) + 3(2V + 2) + B(V) + 2(V + 1),$$

where $B(V) = V(3V + 6) + 3(6V + 9) + 3V + 4$ is the step budget of one clause. It bounds the
steps of one iteration of the overflow loop.

articles.title: One iteration of the overflow loop of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with
label block size $A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, let $W = A + K H g$ be the
row width and $V = (T + 1) W$ the number of variables, and let the tables $s_a, p, c, p_u$ be well
formed for $N$ situations and height $H$. Let $t < T$, $i < N$, $k < K$ and
$r < c(i, k) - p(i, k)$. Let $F$ be counter values in which $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{tmp}$,
$\mathrm{md}$, $\mathrm{c1}$, $\mathrm{c2}$, $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{Ka}$, $\mathrm{CB}$ and
$\mathrm{CW}$ are $0$, $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$, $F(\mathrm{Gc}) = g$, $F(\mathrm{Wc}) = W$,
$F(\mathrm{TW}) = t W$, $F(\mathrm{TW1}) = (t + 1) W$, $F(\mathrm{KB}) = k H g + t W + A$,
$F(\mathrm{U}) = H - \max(p(i, k), c(i, k))$ and $F(\mathrm{R}) = r$. Then for every output word
$o$ and flag $v$, the generator for these data, started at stage $\mathrm{oC1}$ of block $(i, k)$
with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, reaches stage $\mathrm{oHead}$ of block $(i, k)$ with
flag false, counters $F$ and output $e$ followed by $o$ in at most
$\mathrm{oBodyB}(g, H, d, V) = 3 V^2 + 35 V + 2 g H + 7 H + 2 d + 46$ steps, where $e$ is the
encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables whose literals are those of the overflow clause
$(t, i, k, r)$.

articles.title: Literals of an overflow clause
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks and
$g$ symbol codes, row width $W = A + K H g$, situation offsets $s_a$, push counts $p$, consumed
counts $c$ and numbers $H, t, i, k, r$, write $S[t, i] = (t + 1) W + s_a(i)$ for the situation
variable (the label/state variable $s_a(i)$ of row $t + 1$), and
$C[t', k', j, x] = t' W + A + (k' H + j) g + x$ for the cell variable of row $t'$, stack $k'$,
depth $j$ and symbol code $x$. The overflow clause $(t, i, k, r)$ is the list of two (variable,
sign) literals $\neg S[t, i] \lor C[t + 1, k, H - c(i, k) + p(i, k) + r, 0]$: first the negated
situation variable $S[t, i]$, then the positive cell variable of row $t + 1$, stack $k$, depth
$H - c(i, k) + p(i, k) + r$ and symbol code $0$ (the empty cell). Subtraction is truncated at
zero.

articles.title: Literal positions of an overflow clause
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$, $K$
stacks and $g$ symbol codes, row width $W = A + K H g$, situation offsets $s_a$, push counts $p$,
consumed counts $c$ and numbers $H, t, i, k, r, l$, the position of literal $l$ of the overflow
clause $(t, i, k, r)$ is the situation variable $(t + 1) W + s_a(i)$ if $l = 0$, and otherwise the
cell variable of row $t + 1$, stack $k$, depth $H - c(i, k) + p(i, k) + r$ and symbol code $0$,
namely $(t + 1) W + A + (k H + H - c(i, k) + p(i, k) + r) g$. Subtraction is truncated at $0$.

articles.title: Entry label of the pushed-fill chain
articles.statement:
For a situation $i < N$, a stack $k < K$ and a
number $n$, the label of the generator with $N$ situations, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and
window depth $d$ from which the pushed-fill clauses $j < n$ of block $(i, k)$ are emitted before
the fill drains: the fill-drain stage $\mathrm{fD1}$ of block $(i, k)$ if $n = 0$, the first
stage of the routine emitting pushed-fill clause $n - 1$ of block $(i, k)$ if $1 \le n \le d$,
and the halting label $\mathrm{done}$ (unused) if $n > d$.

articles.title: Literals of a pushed-fill clause
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks
and $g$ symbol codes, row width $W = A + K H g$, situation offsets $s_a$, pushed codes $p_u$ and
numbers $H, t, i, k, j$, write $S[t, i] = (t + 1) W + s_a(i)$ for the situation variable (the
label/state variable $s_a(i)$ of row $t + 1$), and
$C[t', k', j', x] = t' W + A + (k' H + j') g + x$ for the cell variable of row $t'$, stack $k'$,
depth $j'$ and symbol code $x$. The pushed-fill clause $(t, i, k, j)$ is the list of two
(variable, sign) literals $\neg S[t, i] \lor C[t + 1, k, j, p_u(i, k, j)]$: first the negated
situation variable $S[t, i]$, then the positive cell variable of row $t + 1$, stack $k$, depth
$j$ and symbol code $p_u(i, k, j)$. It is used for depths $j$ below the number of symbols that
situation $i$ pushes on stack $k$.

articles.title: Literal positions of a pushed-fill clause
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$,
$K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, row width $W = A + K H g$, situation offsets $s_a$, pushed codes
$p_u$ and numbers $H, t, i, k, j, l$, the position of literal $l$ of the pushed-fill clause
$(t, i, k, j)$ is the situation variable $(t + 1) W + s_a(i)$ if $l = 0$, and otherwise the cell
variable of row $t + 1$, stack $k$, depth $j$ and symbol code $p_u(i, k, j)$, namely
$(t + 1) W + A + (k H + j) g + p_u(i, k, j)$.

articles.title: The pushed-fill chain of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block
size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $W = A + K H g$ be the row width and
$V = (T + 1) W$ the number of variables, and let the tables $s_a, p, c, p_u$ be well formed for
$N$ situations and height $H$. Let $t < T$, $i < N$, $k < K$, and let $F$ be counter values in
which $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $\mathrm{c1}$, $\mathrm{c2}$ and $\mathrm{P}$
are $0$, $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$, $F(\mathrm{Gc}) = g$, $F(\mathrm{Wc}) = W$, $F(\mathrm{TW}) = t W$,
$F(\mathrm{TW1}) = (t + 1) W$ and $F(\mathrm{CW}) = k H g + t W + A + W$. Then for every
$n \le p(i, k)$, every output word $o$ and every flag $v$ there is a flag $v'$ such that the
generator for these data, started at the entry label of the pushed-fill chain for $n$ in block
$(i, k)$ with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, reaches the fill-drain stage $\mathrm{fD1}$
of block $(i, k)$ (before draining) with flag $v'$, counters $F$ and output
$e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$ followed by $o$ in at most $n \cdot \mathrm{clauseB}(V)$ steps, where
$\mathrm{clauseB}(V) = 3 V^2 + 27 V + 31$ and $e_j$ is the encoding of the dense clause over $V$
variables whose literals are those of the pushed-fill clause $(t, i, k, j)$.

articles.title: Cost of the precomputation of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block
size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, numbers $T$ and $H$, and the row width
$W = A + K H g$, this is the step bound

$$
1 + (H (2 g + 3) + H + 2) + 1 + 1 + (K (2 H g + 3) + K + 2) + (K + 1) +
(T (2 W + 3) + T + 2) + (2 W + 2).
$$

articles.title: Counters after the precomputation of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label
block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes and numbers $T, H$, the counter values with $T$ on
$\mathrm{Tn}$, $H$ on $\mathrm{Hs}$, $g$ on $\mathrm{Gc}$, $H g$ on $\mathrm{HG}$, the row width
$W = A + K H g$ on $\mathrm{Wc}$, the number of variables $(T + 1) W$ on $\mathrm{Vc}$, and $0$
on every other counter.

articles.title: The cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$
symbol codes, tables $s_a, p, c, p_u$ and $N$ situations, the counter machine with the unit
counters of the generator and a Boolean output stack, meant to start with $T$ units on
$\mathrm{Tn}$, $H$ on $\mathrm{Hs}$ and everything else empty. Its precomputation puts $g$ units
on $\mathrm{Gc}$, adds $\mathrm{Hs} \cdot \mathrm{Gc}$ to $\mathrm{HG}$, puts $A$ units on
$\mathrm{Wc}$ and $K$ on $\mathrm{Ka}$, adds $\mathrm{Ka} \cdot \mathrm{HG}$ to $\mathrm{Wc}$,
drains $\mathrm{Ka}$, adds $\mathrm{Tn} \cdot \mathrm{Wc}$ to $\mathrm{Vc}$ and then adds
$\mathrm{Wc}$ to $\mathrm{Vc}$. The time loop then pops one unit of $\mathrm{Tn}$ per iteration,
pushing it on $\mathrm{Ti}$; each iteration adds $\mathrm{Tn} \cdot \mathrm{Wc}$ to
$\mathrm{TW}$, adds $\mathrm{TW}$ and then $\mathrm{Wc}$ to $\mathrm{TW1}$, runs the blocks of
all $N$ situations, and drains $\mathrm{TW}$ and $\mathrm{TW1}$. When $\mathrm{Tn}$ is empty it
moves $\mathrm{Ti}$ back onto $\mathrm{Tn}$ and halts at $\mathrm{done}$. The stages of a block
$(i, k)$ run the block routine, its loop-body stages run the loop-body routine, and its
decrement stages pop $\mathrm{U}$ and continue the decrement chain, halting at $\mathrm{bad}$ if
$\mathrm{U}$ is empty. Additions go through the scratch counters $\mathrm{md}$ and $\mathrm{tmp}$
and restore their sources when the scratch counters start empty.

articles.title: Precomputation stages of the shift generator
articles.statement:
The labels of the precomputation that the
cell-shift generator runs before its time loop: six plain stages and three multiplication sites,
each of the latter tagged with a stage of the multiplication routine. For a layout with $A$ label
variables, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and the inputs $T$ (number of time steps) and $H$
(height), in order of execution they set a counter $G$ to $g$; set a counter $HG$ to $H g$ (a
multiplication site); set the row-width counter $W$ to $A$; set a scratch counter to $K$; add
$K \cdot HG$ to $W$ (a multiplication site), so that $W = A + K H g$; empty the scratch counter;
set the variable counter $V$ to $T W$ (a multiplication site); and add $W$ to $V$ in two copy
steps, so that $V = (T + 1) W$.

articles.title: Empty scratch counters of the shift generator
articles.statement:
A valuation $F$ of the generator's counters
satisfies this predicate when the five scratch counters $Q$, $\mathit{tmp}$, $\mathit{md}$, $c_1$
and $c_2$ all have value $0$ under $F$. The generator keeps them empty whenever a clause starts.

articles.title: Step bound for one in-range loop iteration
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g$, $H$ and $V$, with
$B(V)$ the cost bound of one clause over $V$ variables, the bound is
$(2V + 2) + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + (2V + 2) + (2V + 2) + g \cdot B(V) + (V + 1) + (V + 1)$.

articles.title: Label of the decrement chain
articles.statement:
Among the generator labels for $N$ situations, $K$ stacks,
$g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, take a situation $i < N$, a stack $k < K$ and
$n \in \mathbb{N}$. The label is the pushed-fill setup label of block $(i, k)$ if $n = 0$, the
decrement label of block $(i, k)$ with index $n - 1$ if $1 \le n \le d + 1$, and the terminal
label otherwise. It marks the point where $n$ decrements of the counter $U$ remain before the
pushed-fill setup.

articles.title: The decrement chain takes $n$ steps
articles.statement:
Fix a layout with $K$ stacks and window depth $d$,
the generator's remaining parameters with $N$ situations, a situation $i < N$ and a stack $k < K$.
For every $n \le d + 1$, every counter valuation $F$ and every $h$ with $F(U) = h + n$, every flag
$v$ and every output $o$, there is a flag $v'$ such that the generator, started at the
decrement-chain label for $n$ remaining decrements of block $(i, k)$ with flag $v$, counters $F$
and output $o$, reaches in exactly $n$ steps the pushed-fill setup label of block $(i, k)$ with
flag $v'$, the counters $F$ with $U$ set to $h$, and the same output $o$.

articles.title: One iteration of the in-range loop of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with
label block size $A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, let $T, H \in \mathbb{N}$,
let $W = A + K H g$ be the row width and $V = (T + 1) W$ the number of variables, and let the
situation-offset, push-count, consumed-count and pushed-code tables $s_a, p, c, p_u$ be well
formed for $N$ situations and height $H$. Let $t < T$, $i < N$, $k < K$ and $u \in \mathbb{N}$
with $u + \max(p(i, k), c(i, k)) < H$. Let $F$ be counter values in which $\mathrm{Q}$,
$\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $\mathrm{c1}$, $\mathrm{c2}$, $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{CB}$ and
$\mathrm{CW}$ are $0$, $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$, $F(\mathrm{Gc}) = g$, $F(\mathrm{Wc}) = W$,
