$F(\mathrm{TW}) = t W$, $F(\mathrm{TW1}) = (t + 1) W$, $F(\mathrm{KB}) = k H g + t W + A$ and
$F(\mathrm{U}) = u$. Then for every output word $o$ and flag $v$, the generator for these data,
started at the in-range variant of the first loop-body stage $\mathrm{bC1}$ of block $(i, k)$
with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, reaches the in-range loop head $\mathrm{sHead}$ of
block $(i, k)$ with flag false, counters $F$ and output $e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{g-1}$ followed by $o$
in at most $3(2V + 2) + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + g B(V) + 2(V + 1)$ steps, where
$B(V) = V(3V + 6) + 3(6V + 9) + 3V + 4$ is the step budget of one clause and $e_x$ is the
encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables whose literals are the in-range shift literals
for $(t, i, k, u, x)$.

articles.title: Literal signs of a shift clause kind
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$ of a cell-shift block and
$l \in \mathbb{N}$, the sign of literal $l$ of $c$ is positive exactly when $l + 1$ equals the
number of literals of $c$; so only the last literal is positive.

articles.title: The shift block of a situation and a stack
articles.statement:
Fix a layout with $A$ label variables, $K$
stacks and $g$ symbol codes, the generator's parameters $sa$, $pl$, $cn$, $pu$, and
$T, H, t, i, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Write $p = pl(i, k)$, $c = cn(i, k)$, $W = A + K H g$ for the row
width and $V = (T + 1) W$ for the number of variables. The block is the CNF formula consisting, in
this order, of: for each $u < H - \max(p, c)$ and each $x < g$ (ordered by $u$, then $x$), the
dense clause over $V$ variables with the in-range shift literals for $(t, i, k, u, x)$; for each
$r < c - p$, the dense clause over $V$ variables with the overflow literals for $(t, i, k, r)$;
and for each $j < p$, the dense clause over $V$ variables with the pushed-fill literals for
$(t, i, k, j)$. Subtraction is truncated at $0$.

articles.title: Time bound of the shift generator on uniform layouts
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ and $y \ge 1$ be
natural numbers and let $L_k$ be the layout with every constant equal to $k$. Then the explicit
time bound of the shift generator for $L_k$ with $N = k$ situations and $T = H = y$ is at most
$828\, k^7 y^6$.

Every monomial of the bound is then at most $k^7 y^6$, and the coefficients sum to $828$, the
value of the bound at $k = y = 1$.

articles.title: Explicit time bound of the shift generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ and $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$,
the bound is $P + (T(B + 1) + T + 2)$, where $P$ is the cost of the precomputation for $L$, $T$,
$H$ and $B$ is the cost of one iteration of the time loop for $L$, $N$, $T$, $H$.

A separate result bounds it by a constant depending only on $L$ and $N$ times $(T + H + 1)^6$.

articles.title: Constant of the shift-generator time bound
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label/state block size
$A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, and a natural number $N$, the constant is
$828 \cdot (A + K + g + d + N + 1)^7$.

It depends only on $A$, $K$, $g$, $d$ and $N$, not on the time bound $T$ or the height $H$.

articles.title: The cell-shift clause family
articles.statement:
Fix a layout $L$ with $K$ stacks and situation tables
$\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$. For $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, the
shift family is the CNF formula obtained by concatenating the shift blocks of situation $i$ and
stack $k$ at time $t$ for all $t < T$, $i < N$ and $k < K$, ordered lexicographically by
$(t, i, k)$.

articles.title: Literals of an in-range shift clause
articles.statement:
Fix a layout $L$ and tables $\mathrm{sa}$,
$\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$. For a height $H$, write $C[t,k,j,x]$ for the cell variable of
stack $k$, depth $j$ and symbol code $x$ at time $t$, and $X[t,a]$ for the label/state variable
$a$ at time $t$. With $c = \mathrm{cn}(i,k)$ and $p = \mathrm{pl}(i,k)$, the literals of the
clause $(t, i, k, u, x)$ are, as (variable, sign) pairs in this order, $\neg C[t,k,u+c,x]$,
$\neg X[t+1,\mathrm{sa}(i)]$ and $C[t+1,k,u+p,x]$. Writing $S[t,i] = X[t+1,\mathrm{sa}(i)]$ for
the situation variable of situation $i$ at time $t$, this is the clause
$\neg C[t,k,u+c,x] \lor \neg S[t,i] \lor C[t+1,k,u+p,x]$.

When all indices are in range, the literals are in increasing variable order: a row $t$ cell, the
label/state block of row $t+1$, then a row $t+1$ cell.

articles.title: The shift-generator time bound as a polynomial
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label/state block
size $A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, and a natural number $N$, let
$c = 828\,(A + K + g + d + N + 1)^7$ be the constant of the shift-generator time bound; this is
the polynomial $c\,(X + 1)^6$ with natural-number coefficients.

For natural numbers $T$ and $H$, its value at $X = T + H$ is $c\,(T + H + 1)^6$, the bound on
the number of steps of the shift generator started on $T$ and $H$.

articles.title: Literal positions of an in-range shift clause
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$,
$K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, row width $W = A + K H g$, situation offsets $s_a$, push counts
$p$, consumed counts $c$ and numbers $H, t, i, k, u, x, l$, the position of literal $l$ of the
in-range shift clause $(t, i, k, u, x)$ is: if $l = 0$, the cell variable of row $t$, stack $k$,
depth $u + c(i, k)$ and symbol code $x$, namely $t W + A + (k H + u + c(i, k)) g + x$; if
$l = 1$, the situation variable $(t + 1) W + s_a(i)$; and if $l \ge 2$, the cell variable of row
$t + 1$, stack $k$, depth $u + p(i, k)$ and symbol code $x$, namely
$(t + 1) W + A + (k H + u + p(i, k)) g + x$.

articles.title: Correctness of the shift generator, with its explicit time bound
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout, let
$\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$ be situation tables and let
$N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose the tables are well formed for $N$ situations at height
$H$. Start the cell-shift generator for $L$, $\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$,
$\mathrm{pu}$ and $N$ at its first precomputation stage, in state false, with $T$ on the counter
$\mathrm{Tn}$ and $H$ on the counter $\mathrm{Hs}$ in unary, all other counters empty, and an
arbitrary list $o$ of bits on the output stack. Then within at most the explicit time bound of
the shift generator for $L$, $N$, $T$, $H$ steps it reaches its final label $\mathrm{done}$, in
some state, with stacks whose output stack holds the encoding of the cell-shift clause family for
$L$, $\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$, $N$, $T$ and $H$, followed by
$o$.

articles.title: Polynomial time bound for the shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label/state block
size $A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, let $\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$,
$\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$ be situation tables and let $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose
the tables are well formed for $N$ situations at height $H$. Start the cell-shift generator for
$L$, $\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$ and $N$ at its first
precomputation stage, in state false, with $T$ on the counter $\mathrm{Tn}$ and $H$ on the counter
$\mathrm{Hs}$ in unary, all other counters empty, and an arbitrary list $o$ of bits on the output
stack. Then within at most $c\,(T + H + 1)^6$ steps, where $c = 828\,(A + K + g + d + N + 1)^7$
is the constant of the shift-generator time bound for $L$ and $N$, it reaches its final label
$\mathrm{done}$, in some state, with stacks whose output stack holds the encoding of the
cell-shift clause family for $L$, $\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$,
$N$, $T$ and $H$, followed by $o$.

articles.title: The cell-shift generator as a finite stack machine
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$, situation tables
$\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$ and $N$ situations, the cell-shift
generator for these data, bundled as a multi-stack Turing machine with finitely many stacks,
labels and states: its stacks are the Boolean output stack and one counter stack for each counter
of the generator, its input stack is the counter $\mathrm{Tn}$ and its output stack is the Boolean
output stack, its alphabets are the counter-machine alphabets (Booleans on the output stack, a
unit symbol on each counter), its labels are the labels of the shift generator for $L$ and $N$,
execution starts at the first precomputation stage, its internal state is a Boolean, initially
false, and its transition function is the cell-shift generator.

It serves only to check that the generator meets the finiteness conditions of a finite machine.

articles.title: Block stages of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$ and
$K$ stacks, push-count and consumed-count tables $\mathrm{pl}$ and $\mathrm{cn}$, a number $N$ of
situations, a situation $i < N$ and a stack $k < K$, write $p = \mathrm{pl}(i, k)$ and
$c = \mathrm{cn}(i, k)$.
This assigns a statement of the generator to each setup or loop stage of block $(i, k)$; below,
"add $X$ to $Y$" copies counter $X$ onto $Y$ through the scratch counter $\mathrm{tmp}$ in two
stages, restoring $X$, and "drain $X$" empties $X$. The setup pushes $A$ units onto $\mathrm{KB}$,
adds $\mathrm{TW}$ to $\mathrm{KB}$, pushes $k$ units onto $\mathrm{Ka}$, adds
$\mathrm{Ka} \cdot \mathrm{HG}$ to $\mathrm{KB}$ by the multiplication routine (index
$\mathrm{md}$, scratch $\mathrm{tmp}$), drains $\mathrm{Ka}$, adds $\mathrm{Hs}$ to $\mathrm{U}$,
and goes to the label of the decrement chain for $\max(p, c)$. The pushed-fill stages add
$\mathrm{KB}$ and then $\mathrm{Wc}$ to $\mathrm{CW}$ and go to the entry label of the pushed-fill
chain for $p$; the fill drain drains $\mathrm{CW}$, and the next stage pushes $c - p$ units onto
$\mathrm{R}$ (truncated subtraction). The overflow loop pops $\mathrm{R}$, pushing each unit on
the index counter $\mathrm{Ri}$; for each popped unit it adds $\mathrm{U}$ and then $\mathrm{R}$ to
$\mathrm{Ka}$, adds $\mathrm{Ka} \cdot \mathrm{Gc}$ to $\mathrm{CB}$ by the multiplication
routine, drains $\mathrm{Ka}$ and runs the loop body with flag false; when $\mathrm{R}$ is empty it
moves $\mathrm{Ri}$ back onto $\mathrm{R}$. The in-range loop likewise pops $\mathrm{U}$ onto
$\mathrm{Ui}$ and runs the loop body with flag true for each popped unit, and when $\mathrm{U}$ is
empty moves $\mathrm{Ui}$ back onto $\mathrm{U}$. Finally it drains $\mathrm{U}$, $\mathrm{R}$ and
$\mathrm{KB}$ and goes to the entry label of the stack chain of situation $i$ for $k$.

articles.title: Setup and loop stages of a cell-shift block
articles.statement:
The finite type of stages of the setup and
loops of an $(i, k)$ block of the cell-shift generator: the base stages $\mathrm{kbE}$,
$\mathrm{kbC1}$, $\mathrm{kbC2}$, $\mathrm{kbK}$, $\mathrm{kbM}(s)$ for each stage $s$ of the
multiplication routine, $\mathrm{kbD}$, $\mathrm{uC1}$ and $\mathrm{uC2}$; the overflow-loop
stages $\mathrm{oE}$, $\mathrm{oHead}$, $\mathrm{oRest}$, $\mathrm{oC1}$, $\mathrm{oC2}$,
$\mathrm{oR1}$, $\mathrm{oR2}$, $\mathrm{oM}(s)$ for each stage $s$ of the multiplication routine,
and $\mathrm{oD}$; the in-range-loop and drain stages $\mathrm{sHead}$, $\mathrm{sRest}$,
$\mathrm{dU}$, $\mathrm{dR}$ and $\mathrm{dKB}$; and the pushed-fill stages $\mathrm{fC1}$,
$\mathrm{fC2}$, $\mathrm{fW1}$, $\mathrm{fW2}$ and $\mathrm{fD1}$.

articles.title: Step budget for one time step of the shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $K$
stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, let $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, let $V = (T + 1) W$
be the number of variables, $W$ being the number of variables per time step at height $H$, and
let $B$ be the step budget for one block of the shift generator for $g$, $K$, $H$, $d$ and $V$.
The budget is

$$
\bigl(T(2V + 3) + T + 2\bigr) + (2V + 2) + (2V + 2) + N(K B) + (V + 1) + (V + 1).
$$

articles.title: One iteration of the time loop of the shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol
codes, let $\mathrm{sa}$, $\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{pu}$ be situation tables, let
$N, T, H, t \in \mathbb{N}$ with $t < T$, and suppose the tables are well formed for $N$
situations at height $H$. Write $W$ for the number of variables per time step at height $H$ and
$V = (T + 1) W$ for the number of variables. Let $F$ be counter values of the cell-shift generator
with empty scratch counters, with $\mathrm{Vc} = V$, $\mathrm{Gc} = g$, $\mathrm{Wc} = W$,
$\mathrm{Tn} = t$, $\mathrm{HG} = H g$ and $\mathrm{Hs} = H$, and with $\mathrm{P}$,
$\mathrm{TW}$, $\mathrm{TW1}$, $\mathrm{KB}$, $\mathrm{U}$, $\mathrm{Ui}$, $\mathrm{R}$,
$\mathrm{Ri}$, $\mathrm{Ka}$, $\mathrm{CB}$ and $\mathrm{CW}$ all $0$. Then for every output list
$o$ and every Boolean state $v$ there is a Boolean state $v'$ such that the generator, started at
the label $\mathrm{tw}(\mathrm{head})$ (the first stage of the time-loop multiplication) in state
$v$ with counters $F$ and output $o$, reaches the time-loop head $\mathrm{tHead}$ within at most
the step budget for one time step of the shift generator for $L$, $N$, $T$, $H$, in state $v'$
with counters $F$ and output the encoded blocks of time step $t$ followed by $o$.

articles.title: Well-formed situation tables for the cell-shift family
articles.statement:
Given a layout with label/state
block size $A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, a situation-offset table
$\mathrm{sa}$, push-count and consumed-count tables $\mathrm{pl}$ and $\mathrm{cn}$ and a
pushed-code table $\mathrm{pu}$, the tables are well formed for $N$ situations at height $H$ when
$g > 0$, $d \le H$, $\mathrm{sa}(i) < A$ for every $i < N$, and for all $i < N$ and $k < K$:
$\mathrm{pl}(i, k) \le d$, $\mathrm{cn}(i, k) \le d$, and $\mathrm{pu}(i, k, j) < g$ for every
$j < \mathrm{pl}(i, k)$.

articles.title: Entry label of the in-range chain
articles.statement:
For a situation $i < N$, a stack $k < K$ and a number
$n$, the label of the generator with $N$ situations, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window
depth $d$ from which the in-range shift clauses for the symbol codes $x < n$ of the current cell
pair of block $(i, k)$ are emitted before the in-range drains: the in-range drain stage
$\mathrm{dCB}$ of block $(i, k)$ if $n = 0$, the first stage of the routine emitting the in-range
shift clause for symbol code $n - 1$ of block $(i, k)$ if $1 \le n \le g$, and the halting label
$\mathrm{done}$ (unused) if $n > g$.

articles.title: The in-range chain of the cell-shift generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size
$A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, let $H, T \in \mathbb{N}$, let
$W = A + K H g$ be the row width and $V = (T + 1) W$ the number of variables, and let the tables
$\mathrm{sa}, \mathrm{pl}, \mathrm{cn}, \mathrm{pu}$ be well formed for $N$ situations and height
$H$: $g > 0$, $d \le H$, and for all $i < N$ and $k < K$, $\mathrm{sa}(i) < A$,
$\mathrm{pl}(i, k) \le d$, $\mathrm{cn}(i, k) \le d$ and $\mathrm{pu}(i, k, j) < g$ for every
$j < \mathrm{pl}(i, k)$. Let $t < T$, $i < N$, $k < K$ and $u \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$u + \max(\mathrm{pl}(i, k), \mathrm{cn}(i, k)) < H$, let $b = k H g + t W + A$ be the first
cell variable of stack $k$ in row $t$, and let $F$ be counter values in which $\mathrm{Q}$,
$\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $\mathrm{c1}$, $\mathrm{c2}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ are $0$,
$F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$, $F(\mathrm{Gc}) = g$, $F(\mathrm{Wc}) = W$, $F(\mathrm{TW}) = t W$,
$F(\mathrm{TW1}) = (t + 1) W$, $F(\mathrm{CB}) = u g + b$ and $F(\mathrm{CW}) = u g + b + W$.
Then for every $n \le g$, every output word $o$ and every flag $v$ there is a flag $v'$ such that
the generator for these data, started at the entry label of the in-range chain for $n$ in block
$(i, k)$ with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, reaches the in-range drain stage
$\mathrm{dCB}$ of block $(i, k)$ with flag $v'$, counters $F$ and output $e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$
followed by $o$ in at most $n \cdot \mathrm{clauseB}(V)$ steps, where
$\mathrm{clauseB}(V) = V(3V + 6) + 3(6V + 9) + 3V + 4$ and $e_x$ is the encoding of the dense
clause over $V$ variables whose literals are the in-range shift literals for $(t, i, k, u, x)$.

articles.title: Label after a literal routine (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
Let $g, n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $c$
be a clause kind of the generator with parameters $g$ and $n$, and let $l \in \mathbb{N}$. If
$l = 0$, the label is the final routine of $c$, which emits the leading gap. If $l \ge 1$, it is
the start of the routine for literal $l - 1$ of $c$ when $l - 1 < n + 2$, and the halting label
otherwise. The generator goes here after the routine for literal $l$, and with $l$ the number
of literals of $c$ before its first literal routine, so literals are emitted from the last to
the first.

articles.title: Base counter of a clause kind (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$, the
generator counter whose value is added to the literal offsets of $c$ to give the literal
positions: the counter Zr for the start-code clause (I1), and the counter CB for every other
clause kind.

articles.title: Boundary before a literal (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
For a bound $V$, a base $B$, a clause
kind $c$ and $l \in \mathbb{N}$, the boundary before literal $l$ is $B + \mathrm{off}_c(l)$, the
position of literal $l$, when $l$ is less than the number of literals of $c$, and $V$ otherwise.
Here $\mathrm{off}_c(l)$ is the offset of literal $l$ of $c$ determined by the start code $ic$,
the symbol count $g'$ and the certificate codes $ycs$.

articles.title: Step bound for one loop iteration (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
For natural numbers
$m, g, N, V$,

$$\mathrm{bodyB}(m,g,N,V) = 2V + 2 + (N(2g+3) + N + 2) + g + 1 + \mathrm{clauseB}(m,V) + V + 1,$$

where $\mathrm{clauseB}(m, V)$ is the step bound for one clause with at most $m$ literals.

It bounds one iteration of any phase loop, and one I3 iteration including its read.

articles.title: One phase-loop iteration of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$
symbol codes, let $ic, k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$, let $ycs$ be a list of $n$ certificate codes, and let
$p$ be a loop phase with base counter $c_Z(p)$ and loop-count counter $c_N(p)$. Let $F$ give the
value of each generator counter, with the scratch counters empty ($\mathrm{Rest}(F)$),
$F(\mathrm{CB}) = F(\mathrm{P}) = 0$, $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$, $F(\mathrm{Gc}) = g$, $F(c_Z(p)) = Z$
and $F(c_N(p)) = t$. Suppose $t < N$ and $tg + Z \le V$, the clause kind of $p$ has strictly
increasing literal offsets, and all its literals at base $tg + Z$ lie below $V$. Then for every
output $o$ and flag $v$, the counter program of the generator runs in at most
$\mathrm{bodyB}(n + 2, g, N, V)$ steps from label $b_1(p)$ with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output
$o$ to the loop head of $p$ with flag false, counters $F$ and output
$\mathrm{encodeClause}(\mathrm{denseClause}(V, \mathrm{clits}(tg + Z, p)))$ followed by $o$.
Here $\mathrm{clits}(tg + Z, p)$ are the literals of the clause kind of $p$ at base $tg + Z$.

articles.title: Loop-count counter of a phase (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
Let $k_0$ be the index of the
input stack in the tableau layout. For a loop phase $p$, the generator counter whose units count
the remaining iterations of the loop of $p$: Fn for the I6 phase, En for both the I5 and the I4
phase, N2 for the I2 phase over the stacks $k > k_0$, and N1 for the I2 phase over the stacks
$k < k_0$.

articles.title: Base counter of a phase (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
Let $k_0$ be the index of the input
stack in the tableau layout. For a loop phase $p$, the generator counter holding the base of the
loop of $p$, the cell base of its iteration $0$: Z6 for the I6 phase, Z45 for both the I5 and the
I4 phase, Z2 for the I2 phase over the stacks $k > k_0$, and Z1 for the I2 phase over the stacks
$k < k_0$.

articles.title: Counters of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
The unit-counter stacks of the generator are
indexed by a finite type with 27 distinct elements: Tn, Xn, En, Fn, Gc, Mm, Hs, HG, Wc, Vc, KA,
ZA, Z45, Z6, Z1, Z2, N1, N2, CB, Zr, P, Q, tmp, md, c1, c2 and Id. Equality on it is
decidable.

articles.title: Clause kinds of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
For $g, n \in \mathbb{N}$, a clause kind is
either the start-code clause (I1), an input clause (I3) with a symbol code $c < g$, or the clause
of one of the five loop phases $p$. The parameter $n$ only indexes the type. There are finitely
many clause kinds and their equality is decidable.

articles.title: Step bound for one clause (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $m$ and $V$,

$$\mathrm{clauseB}(m, V) = V(3V + 6) + m \cdot \mathrm{litE}(V) + 3V + 4,$$

where $\mathrm{litE}(V) = 6V + 9$ is the per-literal cost apart from the gap loop.

It bounds the steps the generator takes to emit one clause with at most $m$ literals over $V$
variables.

articles.title: Run of one clause (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes, let
$i_c$ and $k_0$ be natural numbers and let $y$ be a list of $n$ certificate codes. Let $c$ be a
clause kind for $g$ and $n$ that is well formed for $i_c$, $g$ and $y$, and let $V, B$ be natural
numbers such that all literals of $c$ at base $B$ (for $i_c$, $g$ and $y$) are in range below $V$.
Let $F$ be counter values of the generator with empty scratch counters such that $F(b) = B$ for
the base counter $b$ of $c$, $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$ and $F(P) = 0$. Then for every output $o$ and
flag $v$, the counter part of the generator for $L$, $i_c$, $k_0$, $y$ runs within the step bound
$\mathrm{clauseB}(n + 2, V)$ for one clause from the clause-start label of $c$, with flag $v$,
counters $F$ and output $o$, to the label after $c$, with flag false, counters $F$ and output
$w \cdot o$, where $w$ is the dense encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables built from the
literal list of $c$ at base $B$ (for $i_c$, $g$ and $y$).

articles.title: Literals of a clause kind
articles.statement:
Given natural numbers $i_c$ and $g'$, a list $y$ of natural
numbers, a base position $B$ and a clause kind $c$, the literal list of $c$ at base $B$ is the
list of the pairs $(B + \mathrm{off}(c, l), \mathrm{sg}(c, l))$ for $l = 0, 1, \dots,
\mathrm{nl}(c) - 1$ in order, where $\mathrm{nl}(c)$ is the number of literals of $c$,
$\mathrm{off}(c, l)$ is the offset of literal $l$ (computed from $i_c$, $g'$ and $y$) and
$\mathrm{sg}(c, l)$ is its sign.

articles.title: Dense clauses of positive literals depend only on their positions
articles.statement:
Let $\ell$ and
$\ell'$ be lists of literals (pairs of a position and a sign) in which every sign is positive. If
every natural number $v$ is a position of $\ell$ exactly when it is a position of $\ell'$, then
for every $V$ the dense clause over $V$ variables with literals $\ell$ equals the dense clause
over $V$ variables with literals $\ell'$: order and repetitions in the lists are irrelevant.

articles.title: Stacks of a counter machine with an extra input stack
articles.statement:
Given stack contents $S$ of a
counter machine with counters indexed by $C$ (a list over the alphabet of each of its stacks)
and a list $x$ of symbols from $G$, the combined stack contents give each stack $k$ of the
counter machine the list $S(k)$ and give the extra input stack the list $x$.

articles.title: Codes of input symbols
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be an encoding of a finite multi-stack Turing machine $M$,
and let $g$ be the number of symbol codes of the layout of $E$. A symbol $z$ of the input stack
of $M$ is sent to its symbol code under $E$, viewed as an element of $\{0, \dots, g - 1\}$; the
code is below $g$ because every input symbol is an effective symbol of the input stack.

articles.title: Concatenating consecutive blocks of indices
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a function from the natural
numbers to a type $\alpha$ and let $H$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers. Concatenating, for
$k = s, s + 1, \dots, s + r - 1$ in order, the lists
$[\varphi(kH), \varphi(kH + 1), \dots, \varphi(kH + H - 1)]$ gives the list
$[\varphi(sH), \varphi(sH + 1), \dots, \varphi(sH + rH - 1)]$.

articles.title: Labels of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g$ and $n$, the labels are: a
label for each stage of the first precomputation part and one for each stage of the second; for
each loop phase $p$, a loop-head label, a counter-reset label, two base-copy labels, a
multiplication label for each multiplication stage and a base-drain label; for the input loop,
a head label, two base-copy labels, a multiplication label for each multiplication stage, a read
test for each code $i < g$ and a base-drain label; an error label; for each clause kind $c$ for
$g$ and $n$, a clause-start label, two labels copying the variable count, a literal label for
each literal index $l < n + 2$ and each literal stage, and a label emitting the leading gap; and
a final label. The label type has decidable equality and is finite.

articles.title: The I3 loop on the whole input
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes, consider the
init generator for a start code, a stack $k_0$ and a list of $\ell$ certificate codes, and let
$x = (x_0, \dots, x_{s-1})$ be a list of codes $x_j < g$. Suppose its counters $F$ have $Q$,
$\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $c_1$, $c_2$, $\mathrm{CB}$ and $P$ equal to $0$,
$\mathrm{Vc} = V$, $\mathrm{Gc} = g$, $\mathrm{ZA} = Z$ and $\mathrm{Xn} = s$, that
$jg + Z + g \le V$ for every $j < s$, and that $s \le N_b$. Then for every output $o$ and every
flag $v$, the generator, started at the head of the I3 loop with flag $v$, counters $F$, output
$o$, and $x_{s-1}, \dots, x_1, x_0$ on its input stack (top first), reaches in at most
$s\beta + 1$ steps the head of the I2 loop over the stacks above $k_0$, with flag false, the
counters of $F$ except $\mathrm{Xn} = 0$, an empty input stack, and output
$e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{s-1}$ followed by $o$. Here $e_j$ is the encoding of the dense clause over
$V$ variables whose only literal is the positive literal of variable $jg + Z + x_j$, and
$\beta = 3V^2 + 12V + (\ell + 2)(6V + 9) + (2g + 4)N_b + g + 10$.

articles.title: The I3 loop
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes, consider the init generator for a
start code, a stack $k_0$ and a list of $\ell$ certificate codes, and let
$x = (x_0, \dots, x_{s-1})$ be a list of codes $x_j < g$. Suppose its counters $F$ have $Q$,
$\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $c_1$, $c_2$, $\mathrm{CB}$ and $P$ equal to $0$,
$\mathrm{Vc} = V$, $\mathrm{Gc} = g$ and $\mathrm{ZA} = Z$, that $jg + Z + g \le V$ for every
$j < s$, and that $s \le N_b$. Then for every $r \le s$, every output $o$ and every flag $v$, the
generator, started at the head of the I3 loop with flag $v$, the counters of $F$ except
$\mathrm{Xn} = r$, output $o$, and $x_{r-1}, \dots, x_1, x_0$ on its input stack (top first),
reaches in at most $r\beta + 1$ steps the head of the I2 loop over the stacks above $k_0$, with
flag false, the counters of $F$ except $\mathrm{Xn} = 0$, an empty input stack, and output
$e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{r-1}$ followed by $o$. Here $e_j$ is the encoding of the dense clause over
$V$ variables whose only literal is the positive literal of variable $jg + Z + x_j$, and
$\beta = 3V^2 + 12V + (\ell + 2)(6V + 9) + (2g + 4)N_b + g + 10$.

articles.title: Counter part of one I3 iteration
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes. Suppose the
counters $F$ of the init generator's counter part have $Q$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $c_1$,
$c_2$ and $\mathrm{CB}$ equal to $0$, $\mathrm{Gc} = g$, $\mathrm{ZA} = Z$ and
$\mathrm{Xn} = r + 1$. Then for every output $o$ and flag $v$, the counter part, started at the
head of the I3 loop with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, reaches the first read test (the
halting label if $g = 0$) in at most $1 + (2Z + 2) + (r(2g + 3) + r + 2)$ steps, with flag false,
output $o$, and the counters of $F$ except that $\mathrm{Xn} = r$ and $\mathrm{CB} = rg + Z$.

articles.title: Certificate clauses of the initial row (I4)
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size
$A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $k_0$ be a stack, let $y = (y_1, \dots, y_r)$ be a list
of natural numbers and let $n, m, T, H$ be natural numbers. For a depth $j$ and a code $x$ write
$C_{j,x} = A + (k_0 H + j)g + x$ for the row-$0$ variable saying that stack $k_0$ holds code $x$
at depth $j$. This is the CNF over $V = (T + 1)(A + KHg)$ variables that has, for
$i = 0, 1, \dots, m - n - 1$ in order (no clauses if $m \le n$), the dense clause over $V$
variables whose literals are the positive literals of the variables $C_{n+i,0}$, $C_{n+i,y_1}$,
$\dots$, $C_{n+i,y_r}$: the cell at depth $n + i$ is empty or holds one of the codes in $y$.

In use, $y$ lists the certificate codes, sorted and distinct.

articles.title: Start-code clause of the initial row (I1)
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$, a label/state code $i_c$ and
natural numbers $T$ and $H$, the start-code formula consists of a single clause: the dense clause
over the variables of $L$ for $T$ time steps and depth $H$ whose only literal is the positive
literal on the time-$0$ label/state variable with code $i_c$.

articles.title: Input clauses of the initial row (I3)
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol codes, a stack
number $k_0$, a list $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{\ell - 1})$ of codes below $g$ and natural numbers $T$
and $H$, the input formula has, for each $j = 0, 1, \dots, \ell - 1$ in order, one dense clause
over the variables of $L$ for $T$ time steps and depth $H$, whose only literal is the positive
literal on the time-$0$ cell variable of stack $k_0$ at depth $j$ with code $x_j$.

articles.title: Row-0 clauses for the other stacks
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size $A$, $K$
stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $k_0$ be a stack, and let $T, H$ be natural numbers. This is the
CNF over $V = (T + 1)(A + KHg)$ variables that has, for every stack $k < K$ with $k \ne k_0$ and
every depth $j < H$ (stacks in increasing order, then depths in increasing order), the dense
clause over $V$ variables whose only literal is the positive literal of variable
$A + (kH + j)g$, the row-$0$ variable saying that stack $k$ holds code $0$ (the empty cell) at
depth $j$.

articles.title: Row-0 prefix clauses
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$
symbol codes, let $k_0$ be a stack, let $n, m, T, H$ be natural numbers, and write
$z_j = A + (k_0 H + j)g$ for the row-$0$ variable saying that stack $k_0$ holds code $0$ (the
empty cell) at depth $j$. This is the CNF over $V = (T + 1)(A + KHg)$ variables that has, for
$i = 0, 1, \dots, m - n - 1$ in order (no clauses if $m \le n$), the dense clause over $V$
variables whose literals are the negative literal of variable $z_{n+i}$ and the positive literal
of variable $z_{n+i+1}$: an empty cell at depth $n + i$ forces an empty cell at depth
$n + i + 1$.

articles.title: Row-0 tail clauses
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$
symbol codes, let $k_0$ be a stack, let $m, T, H$ be natural numbers, and write
$z_j = A + (k_0 H + j)g$ for the row-$0$ variable saying that stack $k_0$ holds code $0$ (the
empty cell) at depth $j$. This is the CNF over $V = (T + 1)(A + KHg)$ variables that has, for
$i = 0, 1, \dots, H - m - 1$ in order (no clauses if $H \le m$), the dense clause over $V$
variables whose only literal is the positive literal of variable $z_{m+i}$.

articles.title: Alphabets of a counter machine with an input stack
articles.statement:
For a counter type $C$ and an input
alphabet $G$, each stack of the counter machine with counters $C$ keeps its alphabet there
(Booleans on the output stack, a single symbol on each counter stack), and the input stack has
alphabet $G$.

articles.title: Stacks of a counter machine with an input stack
articles.statement:
For a counter type $C$, the stacks are
those of the counter machine with counters $C$ (its output stack and one counter stack for each
element of $C$), plus one additional input stack.

articles.title: Literals of a clause kind in range
articles.statement:
Given the start code $i_c$, a code count $g'$, the
certificate codes $y$, a bound $V$, a base $B$ and a clause kind $c$ of the init generator, all
literals of $c$ are in range when $B + \mathrm{off}_c(l) < V$ for every literal index $l$ less
than the number of literals of $c$, where $\mathrm{off}_c(l)$ is the offset of literal $l$ of $c$
determined by $i_c$, $g'$ and $y$.

articles.title: Time bound of the init generator at uniform parameters
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $k \ge 1$
and $y \ge 1$, let $L$ be the uniform layout with all four parameters equal to $k$. Then the time
bound of the init generator for $L$ with $n_Y = k_0 = q = k$ and $T = n = e = f = y$ is at most
$18928\,k^5 y^5$.

Every monomial of the bound is then at most $k^5 y^5$, and $18928$ is the value of the bound at
$k = y = 1$.

articles.title: Time bound of the init generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $A$ label/state variables,
$K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and let $n_Y, k_0, q, T, n, e, f$ be natural numbers. Put
$H = n + e + f$ and let $V = (T + 1)(A + K H g)$ be the number of variables. The bound is the
precomputation cost $\mathrm{preB}(L, k_0, q, T, n, e, f)$, plus $6$ times the phase-loop cost
$\mathrm{loopB}(n_Y + 2, g, K H + H, V)$, plus the clause cost $\mathrm{clauseB}(n_Y + 2, V)$.

The generator uses it with $q = K - k_0 - 1$.

articles.title: Constant of the init generator's time bound
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $A$ label/state
variables, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and natural numbers $n_Y$ and $k_0$, the constant is
$18928\,(A + K + g + n_Y + k_0 + 1)^5$.

It depends only on $A$, $K$, $g$, the number $n_Y$ of certificate codes and the input stack
$k_0$.

articles.title: Initial counters of the init generator
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $T, n, e, f$, the counters
$\mathrm{Tn}$, $\mathrm{Xn}$, $\mathrm{En}$ and $\mathrm{Fn}$ of the generator hold $T$, $n$, $e$
and $f$ respectively, and every other counter holds $0$.

In use, $n$ is the length of the input code list, $e = m - n$ and $f = H - m$, where $m$ is the
depth at which the certificate block ends and $H$ is the stack height.

articles.title: The init family
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout, let $i_c$ be a label/state code, let $k_0$ be a
stack, let $y$ be a list of natural numbers, let $x$ be a list of symbol codes of $L$ of length
$\ell$, and let $m, T, H$ be natural numbers. The init family is the CNF formula obtained by
concatenating, in this order: the start-code clause of the initial row for $i_c$, $T$, $H$ (I1);
the row-$0$ clauses for the stacks other than $k_0$ for $T$, $H$ (I2); the input clauses of the
initial row for $k_0$, $x$, $T$, $H$ (I3); the certificate clauses of the initial row for $k_0$,
$y$, $n = \ell$, $m$, $T$, $H$ (I4); the row-$0$ prefix clauses for $k_0$, $n = \ell$, $m$, $T$,
$H$ (I5); and the row-$0$ tail clauses for $k_0$, $m$, $T$, $H$ (I6).

articles.title: The init family of an encoding is a layout-level init family
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be an encoding of a
machine $M$, let $x$ and $Y$ be lists of symbols of the input stack of $M$, and let $m, T, H$ be
natural numbers. The init family of $E$ for $x, Y, m, T, H$ equals the layout-level init family
over the layout of $E$ with start code the code of the pair of the main label and the initial
state of $M$, stack $k_0$ the number of the input stack, code list the codes of the symbols of $Y$
in increasing order without repetitions, input codes the codes of the symbols of $x$, and the
same $m, T, H$.

The family of $E$ lists the certificate symbols $Y$ in their given order, possibly with repeated
codes; the equality holds because order and repetitions do not change these clauses.

articles.title: The init generator at the stack cap
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be an encoding of a machine $M$ with window
depth $d$, let $x$ and $Y$ be lists of symbols of the input stack of $M$, let $m, T$ be natural
numbers with $|x| \le m$, let $H = m + (T + 1)d + 1$ be the stack cap, and let $o$ be a bit
string. Let $C$ be the time constant for the layout of $E$, the number of distinct codes of $Y$
and the number $k_0$ of the input stack. Start the generator for $E$ (start code: the code of
the pair of the main label and the initial state; stack $k_0$; code list: the distinct codes of
$Y$ in increasing order) at its start label with state false, with the counters $\mathrm{Tn},
\mathrm{Xn}, \mathrm{En}, \mathrm{Fn}$ holding $T$, $|x|$, $m - |x|$, $H - m$ in unary and all
other counters empty, $o$ on the output stack, and the list of codes of $x$, reversed, on the
input stack. Then within $C\,(T + H + 1)^5$ steps it reaches the final label $\mathrm{done}$,
and its output stack there is the bit encoding of the init family of $E$ for $x, Y, m, T, H$
followed by $o$.

articles.title: Time and output of the init generator for an encoding
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be an encoding of a
machine $M$, let $x$ and $Y$ be lists of symbols of the input stack of $M$, let $m, T, H$ be
natural numbers with $|x| \le m < H$, and let $o$ be a bit string. Let $C$ be the time constant
for the layout of $E$, the number of distinct codes of $Y$ and the number $k_0$ of the input
stack. Start the generator for $E$ (start code: the code of the pair of the main label and the
initial state; stack $k_0$; code list: the distinct codes of $Y$ in increasing order) at its
start label with state false, with the counters $\mathrm{Tn}, \mathrm{Xn}, \mathrm{En},
\mathrm{Fn}$ holding $T$, $|x|$, $m - |x|$, $H - m$ in unary and all other counters empty, $o$
on the output stack, and the list of codes of $x$, reversed, on the input stack. Then within
$C\,(T + H + 1)^5$ steps it reaches the final label $\mathrm{done}$, and its output stack there
is the bit encoding of the init family of $E$ for $x, Y, m, T, H$ followed by $o$.

articles.title: Correctness of the init generator, with its explicit time bound
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with
$A$ label/state variables, $K$ stacks and $g > 0$ symbol codes, let $i_c < A$ and $k_0 < K$, and
let $Y$ be a strictly increasing list of codes with $0 < y < g$ for every $y \in Y$. Let $xs$ be a
list of codes below $g$ with $n = |xs|$, let $T, e, f$ be natural numbers with $f > 0$, and let
$o$ be a bit string. Start the generator for $L, i_c, k_0, Y$ at its start label with state false,
with the counters $\mathrm{Tn}, \mathrm{Xn}, \mathrm{En}, \mathrm{Fn}$ holding $T, n, e, f$ in
unary and all other counters empty, $o$ on the output stack, and $xs$ reversed on the input
stack. Then within $\mathrm{initBound}(L, |Y|, k_0, K - k_0 - 1, T, n, e, f)$ steps it reaches
the final label $\mathrm{done}$, and its output stack there is the bit encoding of the
layout-level init family for $L, i_c, k_0, Y, xs$, $m = n + e$, $T$ and $H = n + e + f$, followed
by $o$.

articles.title: Polynomial time bound for the init generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $A$ label/state
variables, $K$ stacks and $g > 0$ symbol codes, let $i_c < A$ and $k_0 < K$, and let $Y$ be a
strictly increasing list of codes with $0 < y < g$ for every $y \in Y$. Let $xs$ be a list of
codes below $g$ with $n = |xs|$, let $T, e, f$ be natural numbers with $f > 0$, and let $o$ be a
bit string. Start the generator for $L, i_c, k_0, Y$ at its start label with state false, with
the counters $\mathrm{Tn}, \mathrm{Xn}, \mathrm{En}, \mathrm{Fn}$ holding $T, n, e, f$ in unary
and all other counters empty, $o$ on the output stack, and $xs$ reversed on the input stack.
Then within $C\,(T + n + e + f + 1)^5$ steps, where $C = 18928\,(A + K + g + |Y| + k_0 + 1)^5$,
it reaches the final label $\mathrm{done}$, and its output stack there is the bit encoding of the
layout-level init family for $L, i_c, k_0, Y, xs$, $m = n + e$, $T$ and $H = n + e + f$, followed
by $o$.

articles.title: The init generator as a finite multi-stack machine
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol
codes, a start code $i_c$, a stack $k_0$ and a code list $Y$, this is the finite multi-stack
Turing machine whose stacks are the generator's counters, its Boolean output stack and an extra
input stack, with the extra stack as input stack and the Boolean stack as output stack; whose
stack alphabets are unit symbols on the counters, bits on the output stack and codes below $g$
on the input stack; whose labels are the generator's labels, starting at the first
precomputation label; whose internal state is a Boolean starting at false; and whose transition
function is the generator for $L, i_c, k_0, Y$.

It records only that the generator is a finite machine.

articles.title: The initial-row generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes, let $i_c$ and $k_0$
be natural numbers and let $y$ be a list of certificate codes. The generator assigns to each label
of the initial-row generator for $L$ and $y$ a machine statement with a Boolean flag on the stacks
of the counter machine with the generator's counters plus an input stack of codes below $g$, as
follows. At the read test label $\mathrm{rd}(i)$ for a code $i < g$, it is the read test for code
$i$ that goes on success to the clause-start label of the input clause with code $i$ and on
failure to the label after a failed read test for $i$. At every other label, it is the statement
of the counter part of the generator for $L$, $i_c$, $k_0$, $y$ at that label, translated along
the embedding of the counter stacks into the generator's stacks, with labels unchanged.

articles.title: Labels of the initial-row generator for a layout
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ and a list $y$ of
certificate codes, the label type of the generator is the type of labels of the initial-row
generator with parameters $g$, the number of symbol codes of $L$, and $n$, the length of $y$.

articles.title: The counter stacks inside the generator's stacks
articles.statement:
For a counter index type $C$ and an
input alphabet $G$, the stack embedding of a counter machine over $C$ into the same machine with
one extra input stack over $G$: each stack (the output stack or a counter) goes to its copy among
the extended machine's stacks, with the identity map on its alphabet.

articles.title: Per-literal step cost of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
For $V \in \mathbb{N}$, the
per-literal cost is $6V + 9$.

It bounds the steps the generator spends on one literal apart from the gap loop.

articles.title: Entry label of a literal routine (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$ and
$l \in \mathbb{N}$, among the generator labels with parameters $g$ and $n$: the first stage of the
routine for literal $l$ of $c$ if $l < n + 2$, and the label $\mathrm{done}$ otherwise (that
case is never used).

articles.title: The literal routine of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$ and a literal
index $l < n + 2$, where $n$ is the number of certificate codes, the counter program at the
stages of the routine for literal $l$ of $c$. It copies the base counter of $c$ into the counter
$Q$ (restoring the base counter through a scratch counter) and adds the offset of literal $l$ to
$Q$. It then repeats: pop a unit from the counter $P$ (halting if $P$ is empty) and compare $P$
with $Q$, restoring both. If they are equal, it prepends the slot code of the sign of literal $l$
to the output, empties $Q$ and goes to the label before literal $l$: the routine for literal
$l - 1$, or the leading gap of the clause if $l = 0$. Otherwise it prepends the gap code $01$ to
the output and repeats.

articles.title: Run of one literal routine (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
For a layout and a list of $n$
certificate codes, let $c$ be a clause kind with base counter $b$, let $l < n + 2$ be a literal
index with offset $\mathrm{off}(l)$, and let $F$ be counter values whose scratch counters $Q$,
$\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $c_1$, $c_2$ are $0$. Let $\gamma \in \mathbb{N}$, let
$q = F(b) + \mathrm{off}(l)$ and suppose $F(P) = q + \gamma + 1$. Then for every output $o$ and
flag $v$, the counter program runs in at most $\gamma(3q + 6) + 2F(b) + 4q + 9$ steps from the
first stage of the routine for literal $l$ of $c$, with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, to
the label before literal $l$ (the routine for literal $l - 1$, or the leading gap if $l = 0$),
with flag false, counters $F$ except $P = q$, and output $s \cdot (01)^{\gamma} \cdot o$, where
$s$ is the slot code of the sign of literal $l$.

articles.title: Run of the literal routines of a clause (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
Let $c$ be a clause
kind with $k$ literals at base $B$, the $j$-th at position $B + \mathrm{off}(j)$, such that the
offsets are strictly increasing and every position is below $V$. For $l \le k$ let $b_l$ be
$B + \mathrm{off}(l)$ if $l < k$ and $V$ otherwise, let $\lambda_l$ be the list of literals of
$c$ (position and sign) from index $l$ on, and let the label before literal $l$ be the first
stage of the routine for literal $l - 1$, or the leading-gap stage of $c$ if $l = 0$. Write
$E(a, \lambda)$ for the gap encoding of the slots $a, \dots, V - 1$ with literals $\lambda$. Let
$F$ be counter values whose scratch counters $Q$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $c_1$, $c_2$ are
$0$ and whose base counter for $c$ equals $B$, and let $o$ be an output. Then for every $l \le k$
and flag $v$ there is a flag $v'$ such that the counter program runs in at most
$b_l(3V + 6) + l(6V + 9)$ steps from the label before literal $l$, with flag $v$, counters $F$
except $P = b_l$ and output $E(b_l, \lambda_l) \cdot 00 \cdot o$, to the leading-gap stage of
$c$, with flag $v'$, counters $F$ except $P = b_0$ and output $E(b_0, \lambda_0) \cdot 00 \cdot o$.

articles.title: Lookup in an all-positive literal list
articles.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a list of pairs of a natural
number and a boolean in which every boolean is true. For every $v \in \mathbb{N}$, looking up $v$
in $\lambda$ (the boolean of the first pair with first entry $v$, if any) gives true if $v$ is
the first entry of some pair in $\lambda$, and no value otherwise.

articles.title: Step bound of one phase loop (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
For $m, g, N, V \in \mathbb{N}$,
the cost of one phase loop with count bound $N$ is $N(\beta + 1) + N + 2$, where $\beta$ is the
cost of one loop iteration with clauses of at most $m$ literals, $g$ symbol codes, count bound
$N$ and $V$ variables.

articles.title: Stages of the literal routine (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
The stages of the generator's
routine that emits one literal of a clause: two stages copying the clause base into a target
counter, a stage adding the literal's offset to the target, a stage decrementing the position
counter, a stage comparing the position with the target, two restore stages for each comparison
outcome (less, equal or greater), a stage emitting one empty slot, a halting error stage, a stage
emitting the literal's slot, and a stage draining the target counter.

articles.title: Label after a failed read test
articles.statement:
For a code $i < g$, the label reached when the read test
for $i$ fails is the read test for $i + 1$ if $i + 1 < g$, and the halting error label otherwise.

articles.title: Label after a clause
articles.statement:
The label the generator moves to after emitting a clause of kind $c$:
the halting label after the start-code clause, the end of the input-loop iteration (which drains
the clause base) after an input clause, and the end of the loop iteration of phase $p$ (which
drains the clause base) after a clause of phase $p$.

articles.title: Label after a phase loop
articles.statement:
Write $k_0$ for the stack holding the input. The label the
generator moves to when the loop of phase $p$ finishes: the loop head of the prefix phase after
the tail phase, the loop head of the certificate phase after the prefix phase, the head of the
input loop after the certificate phase, the loop head of the phase for the stacks $k < k_0$ after
the phase for the stacks $k > k_0$, and the first step of the start-code clause after the phase
for the stacks $k < k_0$.

articles.title: Number of literals of a clause kind
articles.statement:
For clause kinds over $g$ codes and $n$ certificate
codes, a clause of the certificate phase has $n + 1$ literals, a clause of the prefix phase has $2$,
and every other clause kind has $1$.

articles.title: Literal offsets
articles.statement:
Fix numbers $i_c$ and $g'$ and a list $y = (y_1, \dots, y_r)$ of
numbers. The offset from the clause base of literal $l$ in a clause of kind $c$ is $i_c$ for the
start-code clause; $x$ for the input clause with code $x$; for the certificate phase, $y_l$ if
$1 \le l \le r$ and $0$ otherwise; for the prefix phase, $0$ if $l = 0$ and $g'$ otherwise; and $0$
for the other three phases.

articles.title: Loop phases of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
The five phase loops of the generator for the
initial-row clauses, in the order the generator runs them (its input loop runs between the
certificate phase and the two stack phases): the tail phase (the row-$0$ cells of the stack $k_0$
holding the input, past the certificate block, are empty), the prefix phase (an empty cell in the
certificate block is followed by an empty cell), the certificate phase (each certificate cell is
empty or holds a certificate code), and two stack phases making every stack other than $k_0$
empty, first the stacks $k > k_0$, then the stacks $k < k_0$.

articles.title: One phase loop
articles.statement:
Fix a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol codes, a start code $i_c$, a stack index
$k_0$ and a list $y$ of $n$ certificate codes, and let $M$ be the counter part of the initial-row
generator for these parameters. Let $p$ be a loop phase with loop counter $N_p$ and base counter
$Z_p$, and let $F$ be counter values with the scratch counters $Q$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$,
$c_1$, $c_2$ empty, $F(\mathrm{CB}) = F(P) = F(\mathrm{Id}) = 0$, $F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$,
$F(\mathrm{Gc}) = g$, $F(Z_p) = Z$ and $F(N_p) = N$, where $N \le N_b$. Suppose the literal offsets
of phase $p$ (for $i_c$, $g$ and $y$) are strictly increasing and, for every $t < N$,
$tg + Z \le V$ and every literal of the phase-$p$ clause at base $tg + Z$ has position below $V$.
Then for every output $o$ and flag $v$, $M$ goes in at most $N_b(b + 1) + N_b + 2$ steps from the
loop head of phase $p$ with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$ to the label after the loop of
phase $p$ with flag false, counters $F$ and output $B_0 B_1 \cdots B_{N-1}\, o$. Here $B_t$ is the
encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables with the literals of the phase-$p$ clause at base
$tg + Z$, and $b$ is the loop-iteration cost bound for $n + 2$ literals, $g$ codes, loop count
$N_b$ and $V$ variables.

articles.title: Step bound for the precomputation
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $A$ label/state variables, $K$
stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and numbers $k_0, q, T, n, e, f$, write $h = n + e + f$. The bound is

$$
1 + (2n + 2) + (2e + 2) + (2(n + e) + 2) + (2f + 2) + (h(2g + 3) + h + 2) + 1 + 1 +
(K(2hg + 3) + K + 2) + (K + 1) + 1 + ((T + 1)(2(Khg + A) + 3) + (T + 1) + 2) + 1 + 1 +
(k_0(2hg + 3) + k_0 + 2) + (k_0 + 1) + (2(k_0 hg + A) + 2) + (n(2g + 3) + n + 2) +
(2(k_0 hg + A) + 2) + ((n + e)(2g + 3) + (n + e) + 2) + 1 + (2(k_0 hg + A) + 2) + (2hg + 2) +
1 + (k_0(2h + 3) + k_0 + 2) + (k_0 + 1) + 1 + (q(2h + 3) + q + 2) + (q + 1).
$$

The precomputation uses it with $q = K - k_0 - 1$.

articles.title: Counters after the precomputation
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $A$ label/state variables, $K$
stacks and $g$ symbol codes, a stack index $k_0$ and numbers $T, n, e, f$, write $H = n + e + f$.
The counter values after the precomputation are $\mathrm{Tn} = T + 1$, $\mathrm{Xn} = n$,
$\mathrm{En} = e$, $\mathrm{Fn} = f$, $\mathrm{Gc} = g$, $\mathrm{Mm} = n + e$, $\mathrm{Hs} = H$,
$\mathrm{HG} = Hg$, $\mathrm{Wc} = A + KHg$ (the row width), $\mathrm{Vc} = (T + 1)(A + KHg)$ (the
number of variables), $\mathrm{ZA} = A + k_0Hg$, $\mathrm{Z45} = A + (k_0H + n)g$,
$\mathrm{Z6} = A + (k_0H + n + e)g$, $\mathrm{Z1} = A$, $\mathrm{Z2} = A + (k_0 + 1)Hg$,
$\mathrm{N1} = k_0H$ and $\mathrm{N2} = (K - k_0 - 1)H$ (truncated subtraction), and $0$ for every
other counter.

articles.title: Run of the precomputation (initial-row generator)
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $K$ stacks,
let $i_c$ and $k_0$ be natural numbers and let $y$ be a list of certificate codes. For all natural
numbers $T, n, e, f$ and every output $o$, the counter part of the generator for $L$, $i_c$,
$k_0$, $y$ runs within $\mathrm{preB}(L, k_0, K - k_0 - 1, T, n, e, f)$ steps, the step bound for
the precomputation (with truncated subtraction), from the label $\mathrm{eg}$ of the first
precomputation part (its first stage), with flag false, the initial counters for $T, n, e, f$ and
output $o$, to the loop head of the tail phase, with flag false, the counters after the
precomputation for $L, k_0, T, n, e, f$ and output $o$.

articles.title: The counter part of the initial-row generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with label block size
$A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $i_c$ and $k_0$ be natural numbers and let $y$ be a list
of $n$ certificate codes. The counter part assigns to each label of the initial-row generator for
$g$ and $n$ a statement of the counter machine with the generator's counters and a Boolean flag,
as follows. Every pop sets the flag to whether a unit was popped, and pushes leave it unchanged.
Below, to copy $a$ into $b$ is to use two labels, the first moving $a$ unit by unit into both $b$
and the scratch counter tmp and the second moving tmp back into $a$; to multiply $a \cdot b$ into
$c$ is to run the multiplication routine adding $a \cdot b$ to $c$ with loop index md and scratch
tmp; to add $j$ to $a$ is to prepend $j$ units to $a$ in one step; and to drain $a$ is to empty
it one unit per step.

The first precomputation part adds $g$ to Gc; copies Xn into Mm, En into Mm, Mm into Hs and Fn
into Hs; multiplies Hs $\cdot$ Gc into HG; adds $A$ to Wc and $K$ to KA; multiplies KA $\cdot$ HG
into Wc and drains KA; increments Tn; and multiplies Tn $\cdot$ Wc into Vc. The second part adds
$A$ to ZA and $k_0$ to KA, multiplies KA $\cdot$ HG into ZA and drains KA; copies ZA into Z45 and
multiplies Xn $\cdot$ Gc into Z45; copies ZA into Z6 and multiplies Mm $\cdot$ Gc into Z6; adds
$A$ to Z1; copies ZA into Z2 and HG into Z2; adds $k_0$ to KA, multiplies KA $\cdot$ Hs into N1
and drains KA; adds $K - k_0 - 1$ (truncated subtraction) to KA, multiplies KA $\cdot$ Hs into N2,
drains KA and goes to the loop head of the tail phase.

For a loop phase $p$ with loop-count counter $N_p$ and base counter $Z_p$, the loop head pops
$N_p$; if a unit was popped it pushes a unit onto Id and goes to the body, otherwise it goes to
the counter-reset label, which moves Id back into $N_p$ and goes to the label after the loop of
$p$. The body, made of the base-copy and multiplication labels of $p$, copies $Z_p$ into CB,
multiplies $N_p \cdot$ Gc into CB and goes to the clause-start label of the clause of phase $p$;
the base-drain label of $p$ drains CB and goes to the loop head of $p$. The head of the input
loop pops Xn and goes to the loop head of the phase for the stacks $k > k_0$ if Xn was empty;
otherwise its base-copy and multiplication labels copy ZA into CB, multiply Xn $\cdot$ Gc into CB
and go to the first read test, or to the error label if $g = 0$. The base-drain label of the
input loop drains CB and goes to the head of the input loop. The read tests, the error label and
the final label halt.

For a clause kind $c$, the clause-start label prepends $00$ to the output; the two labels copying
the variable count then copy Vc into $P$ and go to the label after the literal routine for $c$ and
$\mathrm{nl}(c)$, the number of literals of $c$; the labels of literal $l$ of $c$ run the literal
routine of $c$ for $l$; and the leading-gap label of $c$ drains $P$, prepending $01$ to the output
for each unit, and then goes to the label after $c$.

The read tests $\mathrm{rd}(i)$ halt here; the generator replaces them by tests on its input
stack.

articles.title: Labels of the first precomputation part
articles.statement:
The finite type of labels with which the
generator sets the counters $G_c = g$, $M_m = m$, $H_s = H$, $HG = H \cdot g$, $W_c = W$ and
$V_c = V$, where $g$ is the number of symbol codes, $m$ the end of the certificate block, $H$ the
stack height, $W$ the row width and $V$ the number of variables. It consists of thirteen single
labels and three multiplication loops, each with one label per multiplication stage.

articles.title: Labels of the second precomputation part
articles.statement:
The finite type of labels with which the
generator computes the row-0 cell bases $Z_A, Z_{45}, Z_6, Z_1, Z_2$ and the loop counts
$N_1, N_2$. It consists of sixteen single labels and five multiplication loops, each with one label
per multiplication stage.

articles.title: Row-0 cells fit in the variable range
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with $A$ label/state variables,
$KK$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and all $T, H, q \in \mathbb{N}$ with $q < KK \cdot H$, we have
$A + q g + g \le V$, where $V$ is the number of variables of $L$ for time bound $T$ and stack
height $H$.

articles.title: The first read test
articles.statement:
For $g, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the generator label that tests for input
code $0$ when $g > 0$, and the error label when $g = 0$.

articles.title: Read test for one code
articles.statement:
Given labels $\mathrm{hit}(i)$ and $\mathrm{miss}(i)$ for the
codes $i < g$, the read test for code $i$ is the statement, on a counter machine's stacks plus an
input stack of codes, that peeks at the top of the input stack and sets the flag to whether it
equals $i$. If it does, the test pops it and goes to $\mathrm{hit}(i)$; otherwise (including when
the input stack is empty) it goes to $\mathrm{miss}(i)$.

articles.title: The read chain
articles.statement:
Let $M'$ be a machine on a counter machine's stacks plus an input stack of
codes $< g$, with labels $\mathrm{rd}(i)$, $\mathrm{hit}(i)$ and $\mathrm{miss}(i)$ for $i < g$,
such that at $\mathrm{rd}(i)$ it runs the read test for code $i$ with these hit and miss labels,
and $\mathrm{miss}(i) = \mathrm{rd}(i + 1)$ whenever $i + 1 < g$. Then for all counter stacks $S$,
codes $c$, input lists $xs$, all $k$ and codes $i$ with $i + k = c$, and every flag $v$, the
machine $M'$ goes in exactly $k + 1$ steps from label $\mathrm{rd}(i)$, flag $v$, stacks $S$ and
input $c$ followed by $xs$ to label $\mathrm{hit}(c)$, flag true, stacks $S$ and input $xs$.

articles.title: Empty scratch counters
articles.statement:
An assignment $F$ of natural numbers to the generator's counters
has empty scratch counters when $F(Q) = F(\mathrm{tmp}) = F(\mathrm{md}) = F(c_1) = F(c_2) = 0$.

articles.title: Run lifting
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a counter machine (unit counters indexed by $C$ and a Boolean
output stack) and $M'$ a machine on the same stacks plus an input stack over $G$, such that $M'$
embeds $M$ along the inclusion of the counter stacks with the same labels (at every label whose
statement is not the halt statement, $M'$ runs $M$'s statement). If $M$ runs in $n$ steps from
optional label $l$, flag $v$ and stacks $S$ to a label $l'$, flag $v'$ and stacks $S'$, then for
every input list $xs$ over $G$, $M'$ runs in $n$ steps from label $l$, flag $v$, stacks $S$ and
input stack $xs$ to label $l'$, flag $v'$, stacks $S'$ and input stack $xs$.

This is an instance of run embedding.

articles.title: Literal signs of an init-family clause kind
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$ of the init-family
generator and a literal index $l \in \mathbb{N}$, the sign of literal $l$ of $c$ is positive in
every case except one: for the prefix-form phase (clause group I5), literal $0$ is negative and
every literal $l \ne 0$ is positive.

articles.title: Well-formed init-family clause kinds
articles.statement:
Fix natural numbers $i_c$ and $g'$ and a list $Y$ of
natural numbers, which determine the offsets of the literals of each clause kind from the base.
A clause kind $c$ is well formed when these offsets are strictly increasing: for every
$l \in \mathbb{N}$ with $l + 1$ less than the number of literals of $c$, the offset of literal $l$
of $c$ is less than the offset of literal $l + 1$ of $c$.

articles.title: Sorted certificate code list
articles.statement:
Given an encoding $E$ of a machine $M$ and a list $Y$ of
symbols of the input stack of $M$, this is the list of the distinct codes that $E$ assigns to the
symbols of $Y$ on the input stack, sorted in strictly increasing order.

Besides the empty cell, these are the codes allowed in the certificate cells of the initial row
(clause group I4).

articles.title: Empty-cell variable of the initial row
articles.statement:
For a variable layout $L$, a stack number $k_0$, a
number $H$ of tracked depths per stack and a depth $j$, this is the index of the cell variable
of $L$ at time $0$ for stack $k_0$, depth $j$ and symbol code $0$ (the empty cell $\bot$), namely
$A + (k_0 H + j)\,g$, where $A$ is the size of the label/state block of $L$ and $g$ is its number
of symbol codes.

articles.title: Label after a situation clause in the transition-family generator
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be the number
of situations. For a natural number $i$, the label the generator moves to after the clause of
situation $i$ is the end-of-time-step label if $i = 0$. Otherwise it is the first label of the
clause routine for situation $i - 1$ if $i - 1 < N$, and the end-of-time-step label again if
$i - 1 \ge N$.

articles.title: Label after a literal routine in the transition-family generator
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be the number
of situations and $m$ the number of literals per clause, let $i < N$ be a situation and $j$ a
natural number. After the routine for literal $j$ of the clause of situation $i$, the generator
moves to the label that emits the leading gap of that clause if $j = 0$. Otherwise it moves to the
first label of the routine for literal $j - 1$ if $j - 1 < m$, and to the halting label if
$j - 1 \ge m$.

articles.title: Resting counter values in the transition-family time loop
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with
label/state block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $T$, $H$, $t$ be natural numbers,
and write $W = A + KHg$ for the number of variables per time step and $V = (T + 1)W$ for the total
number of variables. Counter values $F$ of the generator are at rest at time $t$ when the scratch
counters $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{Ka}$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $\mathrm{c1}$, $\mathrm{c2}$
are all $0$, $F(\mathrm{TW}) = tW$, $F(\mathrm{HG}) = Hg$, $F(\mathrm{Wc}) = W$ and
$F(\mathrm{Vc}) = V$.

articles.title: Encoded transition clauses of one time step
articles.statement:
Given a layout $L$, tables
$la, na : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and
$wa : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and natural numbers $N$, $T$, $H$,
$t$, this is the bit string obtained by concatenating, for $i = 0, 1, \dots, N - 1$ in this order,
the encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables whose literals are the literals of clause
$(t, i)$, where $V$ is the number of variables of $L$ for $T$ and $H$.

articles.title: Boundary before a literal of a transition clause
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $K$ stacks and
window depth $d$, let $la$, $na$, $wa$ be the tables and $T$, $H$, $t$, $i$, $j$ natural numbers. If
$j$ is less than the number $m = Kd + 2$ of literals of a transition clause, this is the position
of literal $j$ of clause $(t, i)$; otherwise it is the number $V$ of variables of $L$ for $T$ and
$H$.

articles.title: Step bound for one time-loop iteration of the transition-family generator
articles.statement:
For a layout
$L$ and natural numbers $N$, $T$, $H$, let $W$ be the number of variables per time step of $L$ at
height $H$ and $C$ the step bound for one whole clause of $L$ for $T$ and $H$. The bound is
$T(2W + 3) + TW + T + 3 + NC$.

articles.title: Index of a cell variable in the transition-family layout
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with
label/state block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and natural numbers $H$, $t$, $k$,
$j$, $x$, the variable for stack $k$, depth $j$ from the top and symbol code $x$ at time $t$ has
index $tW + A + (kH + j)g + x$, where $W = A + KHg$ is the number of variables per time step. It is
meant for $k < K$, $j < H$ and $x < g$ but is defined for all values.

articles.title: Counters of the transition-family generator
articles.statement:
The generator for the transition clause
families keeps fifteen unit counters, each on its own stack: $\mathrm{Tn}$, $\mathrm{Ti}$,
$\mathrm{Hs}$, $\mathrm{Gc}$, $\mathrm{HG}$, $\mathrm{Ka}$, $\mathrm{Wc}$, $\mathrm{Vc}$,
$\mathrm{TW}$, $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{tmp}$, $\mathrm{md}$, $\mathrm{c1}$ and
$\mathrm{c2}$.

articles.title: Step bound for one clause of the transition-family generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with
label/state block size $A$, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, and let $T$, $H$ be
natural numbers. With $W = A + KHg$, $V = (T + 1)W$, $m = Kd + 2$ and
$E = 6V + K(2Hg + 3) + 2K + 2W + 22$, the bound is $V(3V + 6) + mE + 3V + 4$.

articles.title: Run of the transition-family generator on one clause
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with tables
$la$, $na$, $wa$, let $N$ be the number of situations, let $T$, $H$, $t$ be natural numbers with
$t < T$, and let $i < N$ be a situation whose tables are well formed at height $H$. Let $F$ be
counter values at rest in the time loop at time $t$ (for $T$ and $H$) with $F(\mathrm{P}) = 0$,
let $o$ be a bit string and $v$ a Boolean machine state. Started at the first label of the clause
routine for situation $i$ with state $v$, counter values $F$ and output stack $o$, the generator
reaches, in at most $C$ steps, the label after the clause of situation $i$ with state false,
counter values $F$, and output stack the encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables with the
literals of clause $(t, i)$ followed by $o$. Here $V$ is the number of variables of $L$ for $T$
and $H$, and $C$ is the step bound for one whole clause of $L$ for $T$ and $H$.

articles.title: Constant offset of a literal position
articles.statement:
For a layout with label block size $A$, $K$
stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, and tables $\mathrm{la}, \mathrm{na} : \mathbb{N}
\to \mathbb{N}$ and $\mathrm{wa} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the
constant part of the position of literal $j$ of situation $i$ is $\mathrm{la}(i)$ if $j = 0$, is
$A + ((j - 1) \bmod d)\,g + \mathrm{wa}(i, \lfloor (j - 1)/d \rfloor, (j - 1) \bmod d)$ if
$1 \le j \le Kd$, and is $\mathrm{na}(i)$ if $j > Kd$.

articles.title: Dense clause from a list of literals
articles.statement:
Given $V \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $\ell$ of pairs
$(p, b)$ of a variable index $p$ and a sign $b$, the dense clause over $V$ variables has, for each
$v < V$, slot $v$ equal to the literal $x_v$ if the first pair in $\ell$ with index $v$ is
$(v, \mathrm{true})$, the literal $\neg x_v$ if it is $(v, \mathrm{false})$, and empty if $\ell$
has no pair with index $v$. Pairs with index at least $V$ are ignored.

articles.title: Successor of a number with a non-maximal remainder
articles.statement:
Let $c$ and $d$ be natural numbers
with $0 < d$ and $(c \bmod d) + 1 < d$. Then $\lfloor (c + 1) / d \rfloor = \lfloor c / d \rfloor$
and $(c + 1) \bmod d = (c \bmod d) + 1$.

articles.title: Encoding a dense clause block by block
articles.statement:
Let $\ell = [(p_1, b_1), \dots, (p_n, b_n)]$ be
a list of literals with $p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_n < V$. Then the bit encoding of the dense clause
over $V$ variables with literals $\ell$ is the gap encoding of $\ell$ from slot $0$ to $V$,
followed by the clause terminator $00$.

articles.title: The transition clause family
articles.statement:
Fix a layout with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks, $g$
symbol codes and window depth $d$, tables $\mathrm{la}, \mathrm{na} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
and $\mathrm{wa} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and
$T, H, N \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $W = A + KHg$, let $X[t, a]$ be the variable $tW + a$, and let
$C[t, k, j, x]$ be the variable $tW + A + (kH + j)g + x$. The family is the CNF formula that
lists, for each time $t < T$ and within it each situation $i < N$, the dense clause over
$(T + 1)W$ variables built from the literal list $\neg X[t, \mathrm{la}(i)]$, then
$\neg C[t, k, j, \mathrm{wa}(i, k, j)]$ for $k < K$ and $j < d$ in lexicographic order, then
$X[t + 1, \mathrm{na}(i)]$.

articles.title: Stack alphabets of the generator
Shifting the start of a gap encoding
articles.statement:
Let $m \le m'$ and let
$\ell = [(p_1, b_1), \dots, (p_n, b_n)]$ be a list of literals with
$m' \le p_1 < \dots < p_n < V$ (if $\ell$ is empty, require $m' \le V$). Then the gap encoding
of $\ell$ from slot $m$ to $V$ is $m' - m$ copies of the absent-slot block $01$ followed by the
gap encoding of $\ell$ from slot $m'$ to $V$.

articles.title: Gap encoding of a dense clause
articles.statement:
For a starting slot $m$, a list $\ell$ of literals
$(p, b)$ (variable index $p$, sign $b$) and a number of variables $V$, the gap encoding of $\ell$
from slot $m$ to $V$ is defined by recursion on $\ell$. For the empty list it is $V - m$ copies of
the absent-slot block $01$. For a list whose first literal is $(p, b)$ and whose remaining literals
form the list $r$, it is $p - m$ copies of $01$, then the two-bit slot encoding of the literal
with sign $b$ (the bit $1$ followed by the negation of $b$), then the gap encoding of $r$ from
slot $p + 1$ to $V$. Subtraction is truncated at $0$.

When the positions in $\ell$ are strictly increasing, at least $m$ and less than $V$, this is the
encoding of the slots $m, \dots, V - 1$ of the dense clause over $V$ variables with literals
$\ell$.

articles.title: Uniform bound on the generator's time
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k \ge 1$ and $y \ge 1$, the
explicit time bound of the generator for the layout whose label block size, number of stacks,
number of symbol codes and window depth all equal $k$, with $N = k$ situations and $T = H = y$, is
at most $323\,k^5 y^5$.

Every monomial of the bound is at most $k^5 y^5$, and its coefficients sum to $323$, its value at
$k = y = 1$.

articles.title: Time bound of the generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ and $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, the time
bound of the whole generator is $P + T(B + 1) + T + 2$, where $P$ is the time bound of the
precomputation for $L$, $T$ and $H$, and $B$ is the time bound of one iteration of the time loop
for $L$, $N$, $T$ and $H$.

The bound is explicit; that it is at most $C\,(T + H + 1)^5$ for a constant $C$ depending only
on $L$ and $N$ is proved separately.

articles.title: Constant of the generator's time bound
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ with label/state block size $A$,
$K$ stacks, $g$ symbol codes and window depth $d$, and for $N$ situations, the constant is
$323\,(A + K + g + d + N + 1)^5$.

articles.title: Correctness of the clause-family generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout,
$\mathit{la}, \mathit{na} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and
$\mathit{wa} : \mathbb{N}^3 \to \mathbb{N}$ tables, and $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose the
tables are well formed at height $H$ for every situation $i < N$. Start the generator for $L$,
$\mathit{la}$, $\mathit{na}$, $\mathit{wa}$ and $N$ at its first precomputation stage, in state
false, with $T$ on the time counter and $H$ on the height counter in unary, all other counters
empty, and an arbitrary list $o$ of bits on the output stack. Then after finitely many steps it
reaches its final label $\mathsf{done}$ (not the error stage of the literal routine, which also
halts), in some state, with stacks whose output stack holds the encoding of the clause family for
$L$, $\mathit{la}$, $\mathit{na}$, $\mathit{wa}$, $T$, $H$ and $N$, followed by $o$.

articles.title: Time-bound polynomial of the clause-family generator
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$ and a number $N$
of situations, this is the polynomial $c\,(X + 1)^5$ with natural-number coefficients, where $c$
is the constant of the generator's time bound for $L$ and $N$.

Evaluated at $T + H$ it is $c\,(T + H + 1)^5$, the generator's time bound, in the polynomial form
that polynomial-time computability of a multi-stack machine uses.

articles.title: Correctness of the clause-family generator, with its explicit time bound
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a
layout, $\mathit{la}, \mathit{na} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and
$\mathit{wa} : \mathbb{N}^3 \to \mathbb{N}$ tables, and $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose the
tables are well formed at height $H$ for every situation $i < N$. Start the generator for $L$,
$\mathit{la}$, $\mathit{na}$, $\mathit{wa}$ and $N$ at its first precomputation stage, in state
false, with $T$ on the time counter and $H$ on the height counter in unary, all other counters
empty, and an arbitrary list $o$ of bits on the output stack. Then within $B(L, N, T, H)$ steps,
where $B$ is the generator's explicit time bound, it reaches its final label $\mathsf{done}$ (not
the error stage of the literal routine, which also halts), in some state, with stacks whose output
stack holds the encoding of the clause family for $L$, $\mathit{la}$, $\mathit{na}$, $\mathit{wa}$,
$T$, $H$ and $N$, followed by $o$.

articles.title: Polynomial time bound for the clause-family generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout,
$\mathit{la}, \mathit{na} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and
$\mathit{wa} : \mathbb{N}^3 \to \mathbb{N}$ tables, and $N, T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose the
tables are well formed at height $H$ for every situation $i < N$. Start the generator for $L$,
$\mathit{la}$, $\mathit{na}$, $\mathit{wa}$ and $N$ at its first precomputation stage, in state
false, with $T$ on the time counter and $H$ on the height counter in unary, all other counters
empty, and an arbitrary list $o$ of bits on the output stack. Then within $c\,(T + H + 1)^5$
steps, where $c$ is the constant of the generator's time bound for $L$ and $N$, it reaches its
final label $\mathsf{done}$ (not the error stage of the literal routine, which also halts), in some
state, with stacks whose output stack holds the encoding of the clause family for $L$,
$\mathit{la}$, $\mathit{na}$, $\mathit{wa}$, $T$, $H$ and $N$, followed by $o$.

articles.title: The clause-family generator as a finite stack machine
articles.statement:
For a layout $L$, tables
$\mathit{la}$, $\mathit{na}$, $\mathit{wa}$ and $N$ situations, the generator program for these
data, bundled as a multi-stack Turing machine with finitely many stacks, labels and states: its
stacks are the generator's stacks (the Boolean output stack and the counters), its input stack is
the time counter and its output stack is the Boolean output stack, its alphabets are the
generator's alphabets, its labels are the generator's labels for $N$ situations and literal
numbers below the number of literals of a clause, execution starts at the first precomputation
stage, and its internal state is a Boolean, initially false.

articles.title: Stacks of the clause-family generator
articles.statement:
The stacks of the counter machine over the
generator's counters: one stack of Booleans for the output and one unit counter for each of the
generator's fifteen counters.

articles.title: Labels of the clause-family generator
articles.statement:
For $N, m \in \mathbb{N}$, a label is one of: a
precomputation stage; the head or the tail of the time loop; a stage of the multiplication
routine of a time step; for a situation $i < N$, one of three labels that start clause $i$, a
stage of the routine emitting literal $j$ of clause $i$ for some $j < m$, or the label that
finishes clause $i$; the label that ends a time step; or the final label $\mathsf{done}$, where a
successful run halts. There are finitely many labels; the generator uses $m$ equal to the number
of literals of a clause.

articles.title: Increasing literal sequences
articles.statement:
Let $f$ assign to each $j \in \mathbb{N}$ a literal
$f(j) = (p_j, b_j)$ with position $p_j \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $m, V \in \mathbb{N}$. Suppose
$p_j < p_{j+1}$ whenever $j + 1 < m$, and $p_j < V$ when $j + 1 = m$. Then for all
$n, a, \mathit{lo} \in \mathbb{N}$ with $a + n = m$ such that $\mathit{lo} \le V$ if $n = 0$ and
$\mathit{lo} \le p_a$ if $n > 0$, the list $f(a), f(a + 1), \dots, f(a + n - 1)$ has increasing
literal positions from $\mathit{lo}$ below $V$.

articles.title: Increasing literal positions
articles.statement:
For $\mathit{lo}, V \in \mathbb{N}$, a list of literals
$(p_1, b_1), \dots, (p_n, b_n)$ with positions $p_k \in \mathbb{N}$ and signs $b_k$ has increasing
literal positions from $\mathit{lo}$ below $V$ when $\mathit{lo} \le p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_n < V$;
for the empty list ($n = 0$) the condition is $\mathit{lo} \le V$.

articles.title: Initial counters of the transition-clause generator
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $T$ and $H$,
the initial counter assignment gives the counter $\mathrm{Tn}$ the value $T$, the counter
$\mathrm{Hs}$ the value $H$, and every other counter of the generator the value $0$.

articles.title: Stack index of a literal in a transition clause
articles.statement:
For a layout with $K$ stacks and window
depth $d$, the stack index $k_A(j)$ of literal $j$ is $\lfloor (j - 1)/d \rfloor$ when
$1 \le j \le Kd$, and $0$ when $j = 0$ or $j > Kd$.

With the row offset $k_B$ and the constant offset $c_i$ of situation $i$, the position of literal
$j$ of clause $(t, i)$ at height $H$ is $tW + k_A(j)\,Hg + k_B(j)\,W + c_i(j)$, where $g$ is the
number of symbol codes and $W$ the number of variables per time step.

articles.title: Row offset of a literal in a transition clause
articles.statement:
For a layout with $K$ stacks and window
depth $d$, the row offset $k_B(j)$ of literal $j$ is $0$ when $j \le Kd$ and $1$ when $j > Kd$.

Among the literals $0, \dots, Kd + 1$ of a transition clause it is $1$ only for the last one,
the next-label literal, which refers to the following time step.

articles.title: Variable layout of the transition clauses
articles.statement:
A layout consists of four natural numbers
derived from the verifier: the size $A$ of the label/state block of a row, the number $K$ of
stacks, the number $g$ of symbol codes (code $0$ is the empty cell), and the window depth $d$.

articles.title: Per-literal time bound of the transition-clause generator
articles.statement:
For a layout with label/state
block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and for $T, H \in \mathbb{N}$, let
$W = A + KHg$ be the number of variables per time step and $V = (T + 1)W$ the number of
variables. The per-literal time bound is $6V + K(2Hg + 3) + 2K + 2W + 22$.

It bounds the steps spent on one literal apart from the loop that emits the gap before it.

articles.title: Entry label of a literal routine (transition-clause generator)
articles.statement:
Among the labels of the
