$CB$) with flag false, the same counters, and output stack $e_y \, o$ (concatenation).

articles.title: Literal sign of a clause kind
articles.statement:
For a clause kind $c$ of a cell, $\mathrm{sg}(c)$ is the
sign shared by all literals of $c$: true (positive) for the at-least-one clause and false
(negative) for every at-most-one clause $\mathrm{amo}(x, y)$.

articles.title: Step budget for one time step of the one-hot generator
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $A$
label/state variables per row, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $T$ and $H$ be natural
numbers, $W = A + K H g$ the row width and $V = (T + 1) W$ the number of variables, and let
$\kappa$ be the step budget of one iteration of the $k$ loop for $g$, $K$, $H$ and $V$. The
budget is $T(2W + 3) + T + 2 + \bigl(K(\kappa + 1) + K + 2\bigr) + V + 1$.

articles.title: Generator run over one time step
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a layout with $A$ label/state variables per
row, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, let $t \le T$ and $H$ be natural numbers, and write
$W = A + K H g$ for the row width, $V = (T + 1) W$ for the number of variables and $p_i$ for the
variable with index $i$. Let $F$ assign a value to each counter of the one-hot generator such
that the scratch counters are empty ($\mathrm{Rest}(F)$),
$F(CB) = F(P) = F(KB) = F(TW) = F(Hi) = F(Kd) = 0$, $F(Vc) = V$, $F(Gc) = g$, $F(HG) = H g$,
$F(Hs) = H$, $F(Wc) = W$, $F(Kc) = K$ and $F(Tn) = t$. For $k < K$ and $j < H$ let
$b_{k,j} = t W + A + (k H + j) g$ be the base of cell $(k, j)$, and let $E_{k,j}$ be the encoding
of the CNF formula consisting of the dense clause over $V$ variables with the positive literals
$p_{b_{k,j}}, \dots, p_{b_{k,j} + g - 1}$, followed, for $y = 0, \dots, g - 1$ in turn and within
each for $x = 0, \dots, y - 1$ in turn, by the dense clause over $V$ variables whose only literals
are $\lnot p_{b_{k,j} + x}$ and $\lnot p_{b_{k,j} + y}$. Let $E$ be the concatenation of the
$E_{k,j}$ for $k = 0, \dots, K - 1$ and within each for $j = 0, \dots, H - 1$. Then for every
output list $o$ and every flag $v$, the one-hot generator of $L$, started at the first label of
the stage computing $TW := t W$ with flag $v$, output stack $o$ and each counter $c$ holding
$F(c)$, reaches within the time-step budget of $L$, $T$ and $H$ (T Body B) steps the head of the
time loop with flag false, the same counters, and output stack $E \, o$ (concatenation).

articles.title: Well-formed clause kinds
articles.statement:
A clause kind of a cell is well formed when it is the
at-least-one clause, or an at-most-one clause $\mathrm{amo}(x, y)$ with $x < y$.

articles.title: Entry label for the first rows of a cell
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be the number of symbol codes of the
one-hot generator. For a natural number $y$, this is the label of the generator at which the
at-least-one clause starts when $y \le 1$; when $2 \le y \le g$, the label starting the
at-most-one clause for the pair $(y - 2, y - 1)$; and when $y \ge 2$ and $y > g$, the final
label $\mathrm{done}$.

From here, for $y \le g$, the generator emits the clauses of the rows below $y$, then the
at-least-one clause.

articles.title: Budgeted runs transport along equal counter values
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a counter machine, let
$K, X \in \mathbb{N}$, let $F$ and $F'$ be counter values with $F = F'$, let $l$ be a label or
the halting state, $v$ a flag, $o$ a list of Booleans and $d$ a configuration. If there is $n$
with $K + n \le X$ such that $M$ goes in exactly $n$ steps from the configuration with label $l$,
flag $v$ and stacks $\mathrm{st}(F', o)$ to $d$, then the same holds from the configuration with
label $l$, flag $v$ and stacks $\mathrm{st}(F, o)$.

articles.title: Gap emission in the counter view
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a counter machine, let $P, Q, T_1, T_2$ be
pairwise distinct counters, let $y$ be a list of Booleans, let $\mathrm{dec}$, $\mathrm{cmp}$,
$\mathrm{emit}$, $z$, $\mathrm{next}$ be labels, and let $r$, $r'$, $\mathrm{out}$ assign a label
to each comparison outcome $\omega$, which is one of $\mathrm{lt}$, $\mathrm{eq}$, $\mathrm{gt}$.
In the instructions below, every pop sets the flag to true if a unit was popped and to false if
the stack was empty, and pushing or prepending leaves the flag unchanged.
Suppose that at $\mathrm{dec}$, $M$ pops a unit from $P$ and goes to $\mathrm{cmp}$, or to $z$ if
$P$ was empty; at $\mathrm{cmp}$, $M$ pops a unit from each of $P$ and $Q$, pushes a unit onto
$T_1$ if $P$ was nonempty and onto $T_2$ if $Q$ was nonempty, and goes back to $\mathrm{cmp}$ if
both were nonempty, and otherwise to $r(\mathrm{lt})$, $r(\mathrm{eq})$ or $r(\mathrm{gt})$
according as only $Q$, neither, or only $P$ was nonempty; for each $\omega$, at $r(\omega)$, $M$
pops a unit from $T_1$, then pushes a unit onto $P$ and stays at $r(\omega)$, or goes to
$r'(\omega)$ if $T_1$ was empty; at $r'(\omega)$, $M$ pops a unit from $T_2$, then pushes a unit
onto $Q$ and stays at $r'(\omega)$, or goes to $\mathrm{out}(\omega)$ if $T_2$ was empty;
$\mathrm{out}(\mathrm{eq}) = \mathrm{next}$ and
$\mathrm{out}(\mathrm{lt}) = \mathrm{out}(\mathrm{gt}) = \mathrm{emit}$; and at $\mathrm{emit}$,
$M$ prepends $y$ to the output stack and goes to $\mathrm{dec}$. Let $q, g \in \mathbb{N}$ and
let $F$ be counter values with $F(P) = q + g + 1$, $F(Q) = q$ and $F(T_1) = F(T_2) = 0$. Then
for every flag $v$ and every list $o$ of Booleans, $M$ goes in exactly
$g(3q + 6) + 3q + 4$ steps from label $\mathrm{dec}$, flag $v$ and stacks $\mathrm{st}(F, o)$
to label $\mathrm{next}$, flag false and stacks $\mathrm{st}(F', y^g o)$, where $F'$ agrees
with $F$ except that $F'(P) = q$, and $y^g o$ is $g$ copies of $y$ followed by $o$.

articles.title: Stages of the multiplication routine
articles.statement:
The stages of the counter-machine multiplication
routine form the four-element type with elements head, body, l2 and rest.

articles.title: The multiplication routine of a counter machine
articles.statement:
Let $a, a_d, b, c, t$ be
counters, let $\mathrm{mk}$ assign a label to each stage of the multiplication routine, and let
$\mathrm{next}$ be a label. The routine assigns to each stage the following counter-machine
instruction. At head: pop a unit from $a$, then push a unit onto $a_d$ and go to
$\mathrm{mk}(\mathrm{body})$, or go to $\mathrm{mk}(\mathrm{rest})$ if $a$ was empty. At body:
pop a unit from $b$, then push a unit onto each of $c$ and $t$ and go to
$\mathrm{mk}(\mathrm{body})$, or go to $\mathrm{mk}(\mathrm{l2})$ if $b$ was empty. At l2: pop a
unit from $t$, then push a unit onto $b$ and go to $\mathrm{mk}(\mathrm{l2})$, or go to
$\mathrm{mk}(\mathrm{head})$ if $t$ was empty. At rest: pop a unit from $a_d$, then push a unit
onto $a$ and go to $\mathrm{mk}(\mathrm{rest})$, or go to $\mathrm{next}$ if $a_d$ was empty.
In each instruction the pop sets the flag to true if a unit was popped and to false if the
counter was empty, and the pushes leave the flag unchanged.

Started at head with $a, a_d, b, c, t$ distinct and $a_d$ and $t$ empty, the routine ends at
$\mathrm{next}$ having added $a \cdot b$ to $c$, with every other counter unchanged; $a_d$
serves as the loop index and $t$ as scratch.

articles.title: Alphabets of a counter machine
articles.statement:
For a type $C$, the output stack $\mathrm{out}$ of a
counter machine with counters indexed by $C$ has the Booleans as its alphabet, and each counter
stack $c_x$ has a one-element alphabet.

articles.title: Stacks of a counter machine
articles.statement:
For a type $C$, the stacks of a counter machine with
counters indexed by $C$ are an output stack $\mathrm{out}$ and one counter stack $c_x$ for each
$x \in C$.

articles.title: A runtime `for` loop in the counter view
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a counter machine, let $c \ne c_d$
be counters, and let $\mathrm{head}$, $\mathrm{body}$, $\mathrm{rest}$, $\mathrm{next}$ be labels
such that at $\mathrm{head}$, $M$ pops a unit from $c$, then pushes a unit onto $c_d$ and goes to
$\mathrm{body}$, or goes to $\mathrm{rest}$ if $c$ was empty; and at $\mathrm{rest}$, $M$ pops a
unit from $c_d$, then pushes a unit onto $c$ and stays at $\mathrm{rest}$, or goes to
$\mathrm{next}$ if $c_d$ was empty. Each of these pops sets the flag to true if a unit was popped
and to false if the stack was empty, and the pushes leave the flag unchanged. Let
$n, B \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{blk}$ assign a list of Booleans to each natural number, and
let $f$ be counter values with $f(c) = n$ and $f(c_d) = 0$; for $t < n$ write $g_t$ for the
counter values that agree with $f$ except that $g_t(c) = t$ and $g_t(c_d) = n - t$, and write
juxtaposition of lists for concatenation. Suppose that for every $t < n$ and every list $o$ of
Booleans, $M$ goes in at most $B$ steps from label $\mathrm{body}$, flag true and stacks
$\mathrm{st}(g_t, o)$ to label $\mathrm{head}$, some flag and stacks
$\mathrm{st}(g_t, \mathrm{blk}(t)\, o)$. Then for every flag $v$ and every list $o$ of Booleans,
$M$ goes in at most $n(B + 1) + n + 2$ steps from label $\mathrm{head}$, flag $v$ and stacks
$\mathrm{st}(f, o)$ to label $\mathrm{next}$, flag false and stacks
$\mathrm{st}(f, \mathrm{blk}(0)\, \mathrm{blk}(1) \cdots \mathrm{blk}(n-1)\, o)$.

The body runs with $c$ holding $t = n - 1, \dots, 0$ in that order, so the blocks end up in
ascending order.

articles.title: Stacks holding given counter values
articles.statement:
For a type $C$, counter values
$f : C \to \mathbb{N}$ and a list $o$ of Booleans, $\mathrm{st}(f, o)$ is the stack contents of a
counter machine whose output stack $\mathrm{out}$ holds $o$ and whose counter stack $c_x$ holds
exactly $f(x)$ copies of the unit symbol, for each $x \in C$.

articles.title: Chaining step of the host program
articles.statement:
For a host label $l$, the chaining step is the host
statement that sets the Boolean internal state to false (the state in which every generator
starts) and then jumps to $l$.

articles.title: Host stack renaming for the accept generator
articles.statement:
The map from the stacks of the accept
generator to the host stacks that sends the output stack to the shared output stack and the
counter stack of each accept counter $x$ to the counter $x$ of the host's accept block.

articles.title: Host stack renaming for the shift generator
articles.statement:
The map from the stacks of the shift
generator to the host stacks that sends the output stack to the shared output stack and the
counter stack of each shift counter $x$ to the counter $x$ of the host's shift block.

articles.title: Host stack renaming for the init generator
articles.statement:
The map from the stacks of the init
generator to the host stacks that sends the output stack to the shared output stack, the input
stack to the host's input-code stack, and the counter stack of each init counter $x$ to the
counter $x$ of the host's init block.

articles.title: Host stack renaming for the situation-definition generator
articles.statement:
The map from the stacks of
the clause-family generator, used as the situation-definition generator, to the host stacks that
sends the output stack to the shared output stack and the counter stack of each counter $x$ to
the counter $x$ of the host's situation-definition block.

articles.title: Host stack renaming for the update generator
articles.statement:
The map from the stacks of the
clause-family generator, used as the update generator, to the host stacks that sends the output
stack to the shared output stack and the counter stack of each counter $x$ to the counter $x$ of
the host's update block.

articles.title: Embedding of the accept generator into the host
articles.statement:
For $g$ input codes, the stack embedding
of the accept generator's stacks into the host stacks that sends the output stack to the shared
output stack and the counter stack of each accept counter $x$ to the counter $x$ of the host's
accept block, identifying each stack's alphabet with itself.

articles.title: Embedding of the shift generator into the host
articles.statement:
For $g$ input codes, the stack embedding
of the shift generator's stacks into the host stacks that sends the output stack to the shared
output stack and the counter stack of each shift counter $x$ to the counter $x$ of the host's
shift block, identifying each stack's alphabet with itself.

articles.title: Embedding of the init generator into the host
articles.statement:
For $g$ input codes, the stack embedding
of the init generator's stacks (with input alphabet the $g$ codes) into the host stacks that
sends the output stack to the shared output stack, the input stack to the host's input-code
stack, and the counter stack of each init counter $x$ to the counter $x$ of the host's init
block, identifying each stack's alphabet with itself.

articles.title: Embedding of the situation-definition generator into the host
articles.statement:
For $g$ input codes, the
stack embedding of the clause-family generator's stacks, used as the situation-definition
generator, into the host stacks that sends the output stack to the shared output stack and the
counter stack of each counter $x$ to the counter $x$ of the host's situation-definition block,
identifying each stack's alphabet with itself.

articles.title: Embedding of the update generator's stacks into the host
articles.statement:
For $g \in \mathbb{N}$, this is
the stack embedding of the family generator's stacks (a Boolean output stack and one unit counter
stack per counter) into the host stacks with $g$ input codes, used for the update generator: the
output stack goes to the host's shared output stack, and the counter stack $x$ goes to the stack
$x$ of the host's private update block. Distinct stacks go to distinct host stacks, and each
stack's alphabet is identified with its host stack's alphabet by the identity.

articles.title: Alphabets of the Cook–Levin host machine
articles.statement:
For $g \in \mathbb{N}$, the host stacks carry
the following alphabets: the shared output stack holds Booleans, the input-code stack holds codes
in $\{0, \dots, g - 1\}$, and every stack of every private counter block has a one-element
alphabet.

articles.title: Stacks of the Cook–Levin host machine
articles.statement:
The host has a shared output stack, an input-code
stack, and five private counter blocks: an update block and a situation-definition block, each
with one stack per counter of the family generator, and a shift block, an accept block and an
init block, with one stack per counter of the shift, accept and init generator respectively.

articles.title: Labels of the Cook–Levin host machine
articles.statement:
For parameters $N, n_L, K, g, d, n_1, n_Y$, the
host labels consist of a copy of the family generator's labels (for $N$ situations and $n_L$
literals) for the update phase, a second copy of them for the situation-definition phase, a copy
of the shift generator's labels (for $N$ situations, $K$ stacks, $g$ symbols and depth $d$), a
copy of the accept generator's labels (for $n_1$ code clauses and $g$ symbols), a copy of the
init generator's labels (for $g$ symbols and $n_Y$ certificate codes), and one final label.

articles.title: The host as a finite multi-stack Turing machine
articles.statement:
Given the five generator programs (update
and situation-definition programs over the family generator's stacks, a shift program, an accept
program, and an init program whose input alphabet has $g$ codes), the host machine is the finite
multi-stack Turing machine whose stacks are the host stacks, with the input-code stack as input
stack and the shared output stack as output stack, whose alphabets are the host alphabets, whose
labels are the host labels, whose start label is the init generator's start label, whose
internal state is a Boolean with initial value false, and whose program is the host program built
from the five generator programs.

This is a finiteness check only: the input and output stacks are provisional until the
precomputation is attached.

articles.title: The host program
articles.statement:
Given the five generator programs (update, situation definition, shift,
accept and init), the host program runs init, then update, then situation definition, then shift,
then accept. At each label of a generator other than its final label, the host executes that
generator's statement with the generator's stacks embedded into the host stacks (output onto the
shared output stack, counters onto the generator's own private counter block, and for init the
input stack onto the host's input-code stack) and its labels renamed into the host's copy of
them. At a generator's final label the host performs one chaining step: it resets the Boolean
state to false and jumps to the start label of the next generator, and after accept it jumps to
the final host label, where it halts.

articles.title: Correctness of the assembled formula
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack Turing machine with
encoding data $E$, let $x$ and $Y$ be lists of input symbols of $M$, let $\mathit{acc}$ be an
output symbol of $M$, and let $m, T \in \mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $|x| \le m$ and that
$\mathit{acc}$ is one of the effective symbols of the output stack under $E$. Then the formula
$\Phi(x, Y, \mathit{acc}, m, T)$ emitted by the host is satisfiable if and only if there is a list
$y$ of input symbols, all belonging to $Y$, such that the concatenation $xy$ has length at most
$m$ and the idle-extended run of $M$ from the initial configuration on input $xy$ is, after $T$
steps, an accepting configuration for $\mathit{acc}$: halted, in the initial internal state, with
$\mathit{acc}$ on top of the output stack.

The proof carries the soundness and completeness of the five families through the
concatenation.

articles.title: The formula emitted by the host
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack Turing machine with
encoding data $E$, let $x$ and $Y$ be lists of input symbols, let $\mathit{acc}$ be an output
symbol, and let $m, T \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $H = m + (T + 1) d + 1$ be the stack cap, where $d$ is
the window depth of $M$. The CNF formula $\Phi(x, Y, \mathit{acc}, m, T)$ is the concatenation, in
this order, of the accept family for $\mathit{acc}$, the shift family, the situation-definition
family, the update family, and the init family for $x$, $Y$ and $m$, all at run length $T$ and
stack cap $H$.

articles.title: Step bound of the host
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack Turing machine with encoding data
$E$, let $Y$ be a list of input symbols, and let $m, T \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $H = m + (T + 1) d + 1$,
where $d$ is the window depth of $M$, and let $R = T + H + 1$. Let $L$ be the layout of $E$ and $N$
its number of situations. Let $c_I$ be the init generator's constant for $L$, the number of
distinct codes of symbols of $Y$, and the number of the input stack; let $c_F$ be the family
generator's constant for $L$ and $N$; let $c_S$ be the shift generator's constant for $L$ and $N$;
and let $c_A$ be the accept generator's constant for $L$, the number of (label, state) codes, and
the number of the output stack. The step bound is

$$c_I R^5 + c_F R^5 + c_F R^5 + c_S R^6 + c_A R^4 + 5,$$

the bounds of the init, update, situation-definition, shift and accept generators plus five
chaining steps.

articles.title: The host on the real generators of a machine
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack Turing
machine with encoding data $E$, let $Y$ be a list of input symbols, and let $\mathit{acc}$ be an
output symbol. This is the host program whose five generators are the real ones for $M$. The
update generator is the family generator of $E$ for the (label, state) codes, window codes and
next (label, state) codes of the situations of $E$. The situation-definition generator is the
family generator of $E$ for the same (label, state) codes and window codes, with the positions of
the situation variables in place of the next codes. The shift generator is the one of $E$. The
accept generator is the one for the number of (label, state) codes, the code of the halted label
with the initial internal state, the number of the output stack, and the code of $\mathit{acc}$
on the output stack. The init generator is the one for the code of the start label and initial
state of $M$, the number of the input stack, and the sorted distinct codes of the symbols of $Y$.
The input itself is not a parameter: the init generator reads it from the host's input-code
stack.

articles.title: The assembled generator, after the precomputation
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be an encoding of a machine
$M$, let $x$ and $Y$ be lists of input symbols of $M$, let $a$ be a symbol of its output stack,
and let $m, T \in \mathbb{N}$ with $|x| \le m$. Put $H = m + (T + 1)d + 1$, where $d$ is the
window depth of $M$. Let $S_0$ be host stacks whose output stack holds a word $o$, whose input
stack holds the symbol codes of $x$ in reverse order, whose update, situation-definition, shift
and accept blocks each hold $T$ on the time counter, $H$ on the height counter and nothing on the
other counters, and whose init block holds $T$, $|x|$, $m - |x|$ and $H - m$ on its four size
counters and nothing on the others. Then the host program on the real generators of $E$ for $Y$
and $a$, started at the init generator's start label with state bit false on $S_0$, reaches its
final label within the step bound $\mathrm{realB}(E, Y, m, T)$ (the five generators' bounds plus
five chaining steps), with some state bit and with output stack the dense encoding of the formula
$\Phi(E, x, Y, a, m, T)$ followed by $o$.

articles.title: Sequencing
articles.statement:
Let $P_u$, $P_s$ (update and situation definition), $P_h$ (shift), $P_a$
(accept) and $P_i$ (init) be generator programs that halt at their label `done`, and let $\xi$ be
a list of input codes. Suppose that for each generator $j \in \{u, s, h, a, i\}$ there are counter
values $F_j$, a word $w_j$ and a bound $B_j$ such that, for every output word $o$, the run of $P_j$
from its start label with state bit false, on stacks holding the counters $F_j$ and the output $o$
(for init, also $\xi$ on its input stack), reaches `done` within $B_j$ steps, with some state bit
and with output $w_j o$. Let $o$ be a word and let $S_0$ be host stacks whose output stack holds
$o$, whose input stack holds $\xi$, and whose private block of each generator $j$ holds the
counters $F_j$. Then the host program on $P_u, P_s, P_h, P_a, P_i$, started at the init
generator's start label with state bit false on $S_0$, reaches its final label within
$B_i + B_u + B_s + B_h + B_a + 5$ steps, with some state bit and with output
$w_a w_h w_s w_u w_i o$.

articles.title: Step budget of the counter program
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural-number coefficients
and natural numbers $c, e, d, n$, let $m = n + 1 + k(n)$, $T = (m + c)^e$ and
$H = m + (T + 1)d + 1$. The step budget of the counter program at $(k, c, e, d, n)$ is

$$
1 + h + (k(n) + 1) + (n + 1) + 2 + (2m + 2) + 3 + p + 1 + (d(2T + 3) + d + 2) + 1 +
(dT + d + 2) + (m + 1) + (T + 1) + (H + 1),
$$

where $h$ is the exact step count of the Horner rounds over the coefficient list of $k$ with
base $n$ from accumulator $0$, and $p = e\left((m + c + 1)^e (3(m + c) + 5) + 5\right) + 1$ is
the step budget of the power loop with $e$ rounds, start value $1$ and base $m + c$.

articles.title: Counters of the counter program
articles.statement:
A counter of the counter program is either a scratch
counter $s(x)$, for one of the twelve scratch counter names $x$, or a target counter $t(y)$, for
one of the twelve target counter names $y$: the counters are the disjoint union of the scratch
counters and the target counters.

articles.title: Coefficient list of a polynomial
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients
and natural degree $d$ (where $d = 0$ when $p = 0$), the coefficient list of $p$ is
$[p_d, p_{d-1}, \dots, p_1, p_0]$, where $p_i$ is the coefficient of $X^i$ in $p$.

articles.title: The counter program's run
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a polynomial with natural-number coefficients, let
$c, e, d, n$ be natural numbers, and put $m = n + 1 + k(n)$ and $T = (m + c)^e$. Start the
counter program for $k, c, e, d$ at its first label with any flag, any output stack $o$, the
scratch counter $N$ equal to $n$ and every other counter equal to $0$. Then, in a number of
steps at most the step budget of the counter program at $(k, c, e, d, n)$, it reaches its label
$\mathrm{done}$ with flag false, output stack $o$, and counter values $T$ on the targets
$uT, sT, hT, aT, iT$; $m + (T + 1)d + 1$ on the targets $uH, sH, hH, aH$; $n + 1$ on $iX$;
$k(n)$ on $iE$; $(T + 1)d + 1$ on $iF$; $m + c$ on the scratch counter $B$; $d$ on the scratch
counter $Dd$; and $0$ on every other counter.

articles.title: The counter program
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural-number coefficients, whose
coefficient list $\kappa_0, \dots, \kappa_{D-1}$ has length $D$, and $c, e, d \in \mathbb{N}$,
the counter program is the program with the labels of the counter program for $D$ Horner rounds
that acts on a Boolean output stack and on the scratch and target counters of the counter
program as follows. It runs $D$ Horner rounds, round $i$ with coefficient $\kappa_i$, base $N$,
accumulator $P$, product counter $Q$, index counter $AD$ and scratch counter $TMP$. It moves $P$
onto both $Mc$ and the target $iE$, moves $N$ onto both $Mc$ and the target $iX$, and adds one
unit to each of $Mc$ and $iX$. It adds $Mc$ to $B$, restoring $Mc$ through $TMP$, adds $c$ units
to $B$, $e$ units to $KC$ and one unit to $Tc$, and runs the power loop with base $B$, round
counter $KC$, accumulator $Tc$, product counter $Q$, index counter $AD$ and scratch counter
$TMP$. It adds $d$ units to $Dd$, adds $Dd \cdot Tc$ to $Fx$ (index counter $AD$, scratch
counter $TMP$) and adds $d + 1$ more units to $Fx$. It moves $Fx$ onto both $Hc$ and the target
$iF$ and moves $Mc$ onto $Hc$. Finally it moves $Tc$ onto each of the targets
$uT, sT, hT, aT, iT$, moves $Hc$ onto each of the targets $uH, sH, hH, aH$, and halts.

Started with $n$ on $N$ and every other counter empty, the program computes $P = k(n)$ by
Horner's rule, $m = n + 1 + k(n)$ on $Mc$, $T = (m + c)^e$ on $Tc$, $dT + d + 1$ on $Fx$ and
$m + dT + d + 1$ on $Hc$, and so loads the twelve target counters.

articles.title: Stack renaming of the counter program
articles.statement:
The stack renaming of the counter program into the
full machine sends the output stack to the host's output stack, each scratch counter $x$ to the
full machine's private counter for $x$, and each target counter $y$ to the host counter that
receives $y$.

articles.title: Embedding of the counter program's stacks
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g, r$, the stack embedding
of the counter program into the full machine with $g$ input codes and $r$ raw input symbols
renames stacks by the stack renaming of the counter program and identifies the alphabet of each
stack with that of its image by the identity (Booleans on the output stack, the one-point type
on each counter).

articles.title: Embedding of the host's stacks
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g, r$, the stack embedding of the
host into the full machine with $g$ input codes and $r$ raw input symbols sends each host stack
to the same host stack of the full machine and identifies their alphabets by the identity.

articles.title: Start counter values
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the start counter values of the counter
program give the scratch counter $N$ the value $n$ and every other counter the value $0$.

articles.title: Counter values after the Horner loop
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural-number
coefficients and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the assignment of values to the counters of the
counter program that gives the scratch counter $N$ the value $n$, the scratch counter $P$ the
value $k(n)$, and every other counter the value $0$.

The counter program reaches these values after its Horner loop has evaluated $k(n)$.

articles.title: Counter values before the power loop
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural-number
coefficients and $c, e, n \in \mathbb{N}$, write $m = n + 1 + k(n)$. This is the assignment of
values to the counters of the counter program that gives the scratch counters $\mathit{Mc}$,
$B$, $\mathit{KC}$ and $\mathit{Tc}$ the values $m$, $m + c$, $e$ and $1$, the target counters
$\mathit{iX}$ and $\mathit{iE}$ the values $n + 1$ and $k(n)$, and every other counter the value
$0$.

articles.title: Counter values after the power loop
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural-number
coefficients and $c, e, n \in \mathbb{N}$, write $m = n + 1 + k(n)$. This is the assignment of
values to the counters of the counter program that gives the scratch counters $\mathit{Mc}$,
$B$ and $\mathit{Tc}$ the values $m$, $m + c$ and $(m + c)^e$, the target counters $\mathit{iX}$
and $\mathit{iE}$ the values $n + 1$ and $k(n)$, and every other counter the value $0$.

articles.title: Counter values at the end of the counter program
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with
natural-number coefficients and $c, e, d, n \in \mathbb{N}$, write $m = n + 1 + k(n)$ and
$T = (m + c)^e$. This is the assignment of values to the counters of the counter program that
gives the scratch counters $B$ and $\mathit{Dd}$ the values $m + c$ and $d$, gives each target
counter its target value ($T$ for $\mathit{uT}$, $\mathit{sT}$, $\mathit{hT}$, $\mathit{aT}$ and
$\mathit{iT}$; $m + (T + 1)d + 1$ for $\mathit{uH}$, $\mathit{sH}$, $\mathit{hH}$ and
$\mathit{aH}$; $n + 1$ for $\mathit{iX}$; $k(n)$ for $\mathit{iE}$; $(T + 1)d + 1$ for
$\mathit{iF}$), and gives every other scratch counter the value $0$.

articles.title: Alphabets of the full machine
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g, r$, the alphabet of a stack of the
full machine is the host's alphabet with $g$ input codes on each host stack,
$\{0, 1, \dots, r - 1\}$ on the raw input stack, and the one-point type on each private
counter.

articles.title: Stacks of the full machine
articles.statement:
The full machine has one stack for each host stack, one
stack for the raw input, and one stack for each scratch counter of the counter program.

articles.title: Labels of the full machine
articles.statement:
For $D \in \mathbb{N}$ and a type $\Lambda$ of host labels,
the labels of the full machine are the read-loop label, one label for each label of the counter
program with $D$ Horner rounds, and one label for each element of $\Lambda$.

articles.title: The full program
articles.statement:
Let $\gamma : \mathrm{Fin}\,r \to \mathrm{Fin}\,g$ code the raw
symbols, let $\sigma \in \mathrm{Fin}\,g$ be a separator code, let $k$ be a polynomial with
natural-number coefficients, let $c, e, d \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $h$ be a host program with
labels $\Lambda$ and start label $\lambda_0 \in \Lambda$. The full program, whose counter-program
labels have $D$ Horner rounds for $D$ the length of the coefficient list of $k$, runs at the
read-loop label the read loop for $\gamma$ and $\sigma$ over all raw symbols; at a
counter-program label $l$ other than the final one, the counter program for $k, c, e, d$ at $l$,
embedded with its scratch counters on the full machine's private counters, its target counters on
the corresponding host counters and its output on the host output; at the final counter-program
label, a step that sets the state to false and jumps to the host label $\lambda_0$; and at a host
label $l$, the statement $h(l)$ on the host stacks.

articles.title: Stacks during the read loop
articles.statement:
For a list $s$ of raw symbols in $\mathrm{Fin}\,r$, a list
$w$ of input codes in $\mathrm{Fin}\,g$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $o$ of booleans, these are
the stack contents of the full machine in which the raw-input stack holds $s$, the host input
stack holds $w$, the host output stack holds $o$, the scratch counter $N$ holds $n$ units, and
every other stack is empty.

During the read loop, $s$ is the unread rest of the input and $w$ holds the codes read so far.

articles.title: Step bound of the full machine
articles.statement:
For an encoding $E$ of a machine $M$, a list $Y$ of
symbols of the input stack alphabet of $M$, a polynomial $k$ with natural-number coefficients and
$c, e, n \in \mathbb{N}$, write $m = n + 1 + k(n)$ and $T = (m + c)^e$. The bound is
$n + 1 + C + 1 + R$, where $C$ is the step budget of the counter program for $k$, $c$, $e$,
$d = \operatorname{depth} M$ and $n$, and $R$ is the host's step bound for $E$ and $Y$ at $m$
and $T$.

It bounds the number of steps of the full machine on a raw input of length $n$.

articles.title: The full program on the real generators
articles.statement:
For an encoding $E$ of a machine $M$, a list
$Y$ of symbols of the input stack alphabet of $M$, a symbol $a$ of the output stack alphabet of
$M$, a map $\iota$ from the raw symbols $\mathrm{Fin}\,r$ to input stack symbols of $M$, an input
stack symbol $\sigma$ of $M$ (the separator), a polynomial $k$ with natural-number coefficients
and $c, e \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the full program in which each raw symbol $i$ is coded by the
code of $\iota(i)$ under $E$, the separator code is the code of $\sigma$ under $E$,
$d = \operatorname{depth} M$, the host program is the host running the real generators of $M$
for $Y$ and $a$, and the host starts at the start label of its initial-row generator.

articles.title: The composed machine, raw input to formula
articles.statement:
From the raw input `s` (all other stacks
empty, output `o`), the full machine halts its host part at `fin` within `fullB` steps, having
prepended exactly `encodeCNF (Phi …)` for `x = s.map ι ++ [sep]`, `m = |s| + 1 + k(|s|)`,
`T = (m + c)^e`. **No hypotheses** (`|x| ≤ m` is discharged here).

articles.title: Polynomial time bound of the composed machine
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack machine
with encoding data $E$, let $Y$ be a list of symbols of the input stack of $M$, $a$ a symbol of
its output stack, $\iota$ a map from the raw symbols $\mathrm{Fin}\,r$ to symbols of the input
stack, $\sigma$ a symbol of the input stack (the separator), $k$ a polynomial with
natural-number coefficients and $c, e \in \mathbb{N}$. Then there is a polynomial $p$ with
natural-number coefficients such that the following holds for every raw input
$s = s_1 \cdots s_n$ over $\mathrm{Fin}\,r$ and every list $o$ of booleans. Write
$m = n + 1 + k(n)$, $T = (m + c)^e$ and $x = \iota(s_1) \cdots \iota(s_n)\,\sigma$. The full
program on the real generators for $E$, $Y$, $a$, $\iota$, $\sigma$, $k$, $c$ and $e$, started at
its read-loop label with flag false, $s$ on the raw input stack, $o$ on the host output stack and
every other stack empty, reaches the host's final label within $p(n)$ steps, with some flag and
some stack contents in which the host output stack holds the dense encoding of the formula
$\Phi(x, Y, a, m, T)$ emitted by the host, followed by $o$.

articles.title: The full machine as a finite multi-stack Turing machine
articles.statement:
Given $r \in \mathbb{N}$, an
encoding $E$ of the machine $M$, a list $Y_s$ of input symbols of $M$, an output symbol $a$ of
$M$, a map $\iota$ from $\{0, \dots, r - 1\}$ to input symbols of $M$, an input symbol $\sigma$ of
$M$ (the separator), a polynomial $k$ with natural coefficients and $c, e \in \mathbb{N}$: the
finite multi-stack machine whose stacks are the full stacks (the host's stacks, the raw input
stack and the scratch counters) with the full alphabets, whose labels are the full labels, with
start label the read label, internal states the booleans with initial state false, and program
the full program built from these data. Its input stack is the raw input stack and its output
stack is the host's output stack.

articles.title: Horner-round labels indexed by natural numbers
articles.statement:
For a number $D$ of Horner rounds,
$i \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Horner-round stage $s$: the counter-program label for stage $s$ of
Horner round $i$ if $i < D$, and otherwise the label $x_1$ that follows the Horner rounds.

Indices $i \ge D$ are never reached.

articles.title: One Horner round
articles.statement:
Let $b, \mathit{acc}, q, d, t$ be pairwise distinct counters of a
counter machine $M$, let $a \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mu$ assign a label to each Horner-round stage
and let $\nu$ be a label. Suppose that for every Horner-round stage $s$ the label $\mu(s)$ runs
the Horner-round statement for $b, \mathit{acc}, q, d, t, a$ with stage labels $\mu$ and exit
label $\nu$ at stage $s$. Let $F$ be counter values with $F(q) = F(d) = F(t) = 0$, let $v$ be a
flag and $o$ an output, and let $h$ be the step count of one Horner round. Then $M$ runs from the
first multiplication stage $\mu(\mathrm{mul\ head})$ with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$
in exactly $h(F(\mathit{acc}), F(b))$ steps to the label $\nu$ with flag false, output $o$, and
counters $F$ except that $\mathit{acc}$ holds $F(\mathit{acc}) \cdot F(b) + a$.

articles.title: The statements of one Horner round
articles.statement:
For counters $b, \mathit{acc}, q, d, t$, a number
$a \in \mathbb{N}$, stage labels $\mu$ and an exit label $\nu$: the statements performing
$\mathit{acc} \leftarrow \mathit{acc} \cdot b + a$ in four stages, each stage reaching the next
through $\mu$. The multiplication stages add $\mathit{acc} \cdot b$ to $q$ (with index counter $d$
and scratch counter $t$), then the drain stage empties $\mathit{acc}$, the move stage transfers
$q$ into $\mathit{acc}$, and the add stage pushes $a$ units onto $\mathit{acc}$ and continues at
$\nu$.

articles.title: Step count of one Horner round
articles.statement:
For an accumulator value $A$ and a base $b$, the number
$A(2b + 3) + A + 2 + (A + 1) + (Ab + 1) + 1$: the exact number of steps one Horner round takes
from $\mathit{acc} = A$ with base $b$.

articles.title: The Horner step count is polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $cs$ be a list of natural numbers and let
$A : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a polynomial function, that is, there is a polynomial $q$ with
natural-number coefficients such that $A(n) = q(n)$ for all $n$. Then $n \mapsto h(n, A(n))$ is a
polynomial function in the same sense, where $h(b, a)$ is the step count of the Horner rounds over
$cs$ with base $b$ from accumulator $a$.

articles.title: Step count of the Horner rounds
articles.statement:
For a list $cs$ of coefficients, a base $b$ and an
accumulator value $A$: $0$ if $cs$ is empty, and if $cs$ is $a$ followed by $cs'$, the step count
$h(A, b)$ of one Horner round from $A$ with base $b$ plus the step count of $cs'$ with base $b$
from accumulator $A b + a$. This is the exact number of steps of the Horner rounds.

articles.title: Horner's rule
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $p$ with natural coefficients and every
$b \in \mathbb{N}$, running Horner rounds with base $b$ on the coefficients of $p$ (highest degree
first), starting from accumulator $0$, yields $p(b)$.

articles.title: Splitting off the starting accumulator in Horner evaluation
articles.statement:
For a list
$c_1, \dots, c_\ell$ of natural numbers and natural numbers $b$ and $A$, write $h(x)$ for the
Horner value of $c_1, \dots, c_\ell$ with base $b$ from accumulator $x$: the number obtained
from the starting value $x$ by replacing the current value $y$ by $y b + c_i$ for
$i = 1, \dots, \ell$ in turn. Then $h(A) = A b^{\ell} + h(0)$.

articles.title: Horner value
articles.statement:
For a list $c_1, \dots, c_\ell$ of natural numbers and natural numbers $b$
and $A$, the Horner value of $c_1, \dots, c_\ell$ with base $b$ from accumulator $A$ is the number
obtained from the starting value $x = A$ by replacing $x$ by $x b + c_i$ for $i = 1, \dots, \ell$
in turn; for the empty list it is $A$.

articles.title: Horner rounds
articles.statement:
Let $b, \mathit{acc}, q, d, t$ be pairwise distinct counters of a counter
machine $M$, let $c_0, \dots, c_{\ell-1}$ be natural numbers, let $\mu$ assign a label
$\mu(i, s)$ to each $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and each Horner-round stage $s$, and let $\nu$ be a label.
Suppose that for every $i < \ell$ and every stage $s$ the label $\mu(i, s)$ runs, at stage $s$,
the statement of one Horner round for $b, \mathit{acc}, q, d, t$ and the number $c_i$, with
stage labels $\mu(i, \cdot)$ and exit label $\mu(i + 1, \mathrm{mul\ head})$ if $i + 1 < \ell$
and $\nu$ otherwise. Then for all $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $i + j = \ell$, all counter values
$F$ with $F(q) = F(d) = F(t) = 0$, every flag $v$ and every output $o$, there is a flag $v'$ such
that $M$ runs in exactly $h$ steps from the label $\mu(i, \mathrm{mul\ head})$ if $i < \ell$ and
$\nu$ otherwise, with flag $v$, counters $F$ and output $o$, to the label $\nu$ with flag $v'$,
output $o$, and counters $F$ except that $\mathit{acc}$ holds the Horner value of
$c_i, \dots, c_{\ell-1}$ with base $F(b)$ from accumulator $F(\mathit{acc})$. Here $h$ is the
step count of the Horner rounds over $c_i, \dots, c_{\ell-1}$ with base $F(b)$ from accumulator
$F(\mathit{acc})$.

articles.title: Stages of a Horner round
articles.statement:
The Horner-round stages are $\mathsf{mul}(s)$, one for each
stage $s$ of a multiplication site, and the three stages $\mathsf{drn}$, $\mathsf{mv}$ and
$\mathsf{add}$. In a Horner round they label the multiplication, draining the accumulator,
moving the product into the accumulator, and adding the coefficient.

articles.title: Initial configuration of the full machine
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be encoding data for a finite
multi-stack Turing machine $M$, and let $r$ be a natural number. Fix a list $Y$ of input-stack
symbols of $M$, an output-stack symbol $a$ of $M$, a map $\iota$ from $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$ to
input-stack symbols of $M$, a separator input-stack symbol $\sigma$ of $M$, a polynomial $k$ with
natural-number coefficients and natural numbers $c$ and $e$. On every raw input $s$, a word over
$\{0, \dots, r-1\}$, the initial configuration of the full machine built from these data is at
the read-loop label with internal state false, its raw-input stack holds $s$, and all its other
stacks (the code stack, the output stack, the scratch counters and the remaining host stacks)
are empty.

articles.title: Polynomial functions on the naturals
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is
polynomial when there is a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients such that
$f(n) = p(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Total length bound
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural-number coefficients and
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, the total length bound is $m = n + 1 + k(n)$.

So a word $x$ of length $n + 1$ followed by a word $y$ has length at most $m$ exactly when $y$
has length at most $k(n)$.

articles.title: Labels of the counter program
articles.statement:
For $D \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of Horner rounds, the
labels of the counter program are $p_1$; a label $\mathrm{hr}(i, s)$ for each round $i < D$ and
each Horner-round stage $s$; the labels $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4, c_1, c_2, x_6, x_7, x_8$; a label
$w_2(s)$ for each power-loop stage $s$; $x_9$; a label $\mathrm{ml}(s)$ for each stage $s$ of a
multiplication site; the labels $x_{10}, x_{11}, x_{12}, x_{13}, x_{14}$; and
$\mathrm{done}$.

articles.title: Step budget of the power loop
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $j$ (the number of rounds), $p$ (the
start value) and $b$ (the base), the step budget of the power loop is
$j \, (p \, (b + 1)^j \, (3 b + 5) + 5) + 1$.

articles.title: The power loop
articles.statement:
Let $b, k, p, q, a, t$ be pairwise distinct counters of a counter machine
$M$, let $\mu$ assign a label to each power-loop stage and let $\nu$ be a label. Suppose that for
every power-loop stage $s$ the label $\mu(s)$ runs the power-loop program for $b, k, p, q, a, t$
with stage labels $\mu$ and exit label $\nu$ at stage $s$. Let $j \in \mathbb{N}$, let $F$ be
counter values with $F(k) = j$ and $F(q) = F(a) = F(t) = 0$, let $v$ be a flag and $o$ an
output. Then $M$ runs from the head stage $\mu(\mathrm{hd})$ with flag $v$, counters $F$ and
output $o$ to the label $\nu$ with flag false, output $o$, and counters $F$ except that $p$ holds
$F(p) \cdot F(b)^j$ and $k$ holds $0$, within $j\,(F(p)\,(F(b) + 1)^j\,(3F(b) + 5) + 5) + 1$
steps, the step budget of the power loop for $j$ rounds, start value $F(p)$ and base $F(b)$.

articles.title: Power-loop program
articles.statement:
Given six counters $b$, $k$, $p$, $q$, $a$, $t$, a label for each
power-loop stage and an exit label, the power loop is the following program on the stages. At
the head stage it pops one unit from $k$; if $k$ was empty it goes to the exit label, otherwise
to the first multiplication stage. The multiplication stages add $p \cdot b$ to $q$ (a
multiplication site with index counter $a$ and scratch counter $t$) and then go to the drain
stage. The drain stage empties $p$ and goes to the move stage. The move stage moves the contents
of $q$ onto $p$ and returns to the head stage.

When the six counters are distinct and $q = a = t = 0$ at the start, each round multiplies $p$ by
$b$, so the loop replaces $p$ by $p \cdot b^k$ and ends with $k = 0$.

articles.title: The precomputation
articles.statement:
Fix the full program built from a code map $c_f$ from the raw alphabet
$\mathrm{Fin}\,r$ to the code alphabet $\mathrm{Fin}\,g$, a separator code $c_s$, a polynomial $k$
with natural coefficients, constants $c, e, d \in \mathbb{N}$, a host program and its start label.
Let $s = s_1 \cdots s_n$ be a raw input word and $o$ a list of booleans. Started at the read-loop
label with flag false, raw input stack $s$, output stack $o$ and every other stack empty, the full
program reaches the host's start label with flag false within $n + 1 + B + 1$ steps, where $B$ is
the counter program's step budget for $k, c, e, d$ at $n$. The stacks it reaches satisfy: the
output stack is still $o$; the input stack is $c_s, c_f(s_n), \dots, c_f(s_1)$; for every target
$y$, the host counter receiving $y$ has length equal to the target value of $y$ for $k, c, e, d$
at $n$; and every host stack other than the output stack, the input stack and the host counters
receiving targets is empty.

These are the preloads that the assembled generator's run expects.

articles.title: Scratch counters of the counter program
articles.statement:
The type of the twelve private counters of the
precomputation's counter program, with constructors $N$, $P$, $Q$, $AD$, $TMP$, $KC$, $Mc$, $B$,
$Tc$, $Fx$, $Dd$, $Hc$.

articles.title: Target counters of the counter program
articles.statement:
The type of the twelve counters that the
precomputation's counter program loads for the host, with constructors $uT$, $uH$, $sT$, $sH$,
$hT$, $hH$, $aT$, $aH$, $iT$, $iX$, $iE$, $iF$.

They hold the twelve preloads of the assembled generator's run.

articles.title: Stages of the power loop
articles.statement:
The labels of one power-loop site: a head stage, a
multiplication stage $\mathrm{mul}(s)$ for each stage $s$ of a multiplication site, a drain stage
and a move stage.

articles.title: The read loop
articles.statement:
Given a code map $c_f$ from the raw alphabet $\mathrm{Fin}\,r$ to the code
alphabet $\mathrm{Fin}\,g$, a separator code $c_s$ and a list $L$ of raw symbols, the read-loop
statement tests the symbols $i$ of $L$ in order against the top of the raw input stack. At the
first $i$ found on top, it pops it, pushes $c_f(i)$ on the host input stack and one unit on the
scratch counter $N$, and goes back to the read-loop label (with the flag true). If no symbol of
$L$ is on top, in particular when the raw input is empty, it pushes $c_s$ on the input stack, sets
the flag to false and goes to the first label of the counter program.

The full program takes $L$ to be all of $\mathrm{Fin}\,r$, so each step reads one input symbol.

articles.title: The read loop's run
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a program of the full machine whose read-loop label carries
the read loop over all of $\mathrm{Fin}\,r$, with code map $c_f$ and separator code $c_s$, and let
$o$ be a list of booleans. For every raw input $s = s_1 \cdots s_\ell$, list of codes $w$,
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and flag $v$: started at the read-loop label with flag $v$, raw input stack $s$,
input stack $w$, scratch counter $N = n$, output stack $o$ and every other stack empty, $M$ runs in
exactly $\ell + 1$ steps to the counter program's first label, with flag false, raw input stack
empty, input stack $c_s, c_f(s_\ell), \dots, c_f(s_1)$ followed by $w$, scratch counter
$N = n + \ell$, output stack $o$ and every other stack empty.

articles.title: Unit targets of a multi-target transfer
articles.statement:
For a list $y_1, \dots, y_j$ of counters, the list
of transfer targets that pushes one unit on each counter $y_i$, in the same order.

articles.title: Host counter of each target
articles.statement:
The map from the twelve targets to host stacks: $uT$ and $uH$
go to the counters $T_n$ and $H_s$ of the update generator's block, $sT$ and $sH$ to those of the
situation-definition generator's block, $hT$ and $hH$ to those of the shift generator's block,
$aT$ and $aH$ to those of the accept generator's block, and $iT$, $iX$, $iE$, $iF$ to the counters
$T_n$, $X_n$, $E_n$, $F_n$ of the init generator's block.

articles.title: The precomputed time bound
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural coefficients and
$c, e, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the time bound is $T = (m + c)^e$, where $m = n + 1 + k(n)$.

articles.title: Target counter values
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $k$ with natural-number coefficients and natural
numbers $c, e, d, n$, let $m = n + 1 + k(n)$, $T = (m + c)^e$ and let $H = m + (T + 1)d + 1$ be
the stack cap. The target values on the twelve target counters assign $T$ to each of
$u_T, s_T, h_T, a_T, i_T$, assign $H$ to each of $u_H, s_H, h_H, a_H$, and assign $n + 1$ to
$i_X$, $k(n)$ to $i_E$ and $(T + 1)d + 1$ to $i_F$.

In particular the value at $i_F$ is $H - m$.

articles.title: Counters after a multi-target transfer
articles.statement:
Given counter values $F : C \to \mathbb{N}$, a
counter $x \in C$ and a list $Y$ of counters, the counter values after transferring $x$ to $Y$
form the function that sends $x$ to $0$, sends every $z \ne x$ occurring in $Y$ to
$F(z) + F(x)$, and sends every other $z$ to $F(z)$.

articles.title: Multi-target transfer
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a counter machine with counters indexed by $C$, a
Boolean output stack and a Boolean state, let $x \in C$, and let $Y$ be a list of distinct
counters not containing $x$. Suppose the instruction at label $\ell$ is the transfer loop that
pops counter $x$ and pushes one unit on every counter of $Y$, returning to $\ell$ while $x$ is
nonempty and continuing at label $\ell'$ once it is empty. Then for all counter values
$F : C \to \mathbb{N}$, every state bit $v$ and every output stack $o$, the machine runs in
exactly $F(x) + 1$ steps from label $\ell$ with state $v$, counter values $F$ and output stack $o$
to label $\ell'$ with state false, output stack $o$ and the counter values after transferring
$x$ to $Y$: counter $x$ becomes $0$, each counter of $Y$ gains $F(x)$, and every other counter
keeps its value.

articles.title: Binary-index translation of a dense clause
articles.statement:
Let $k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $c$ be a dense
clause with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{L-1}$. Its binary-index translation with offset $k_0$ is the
clause that has, for each slot $j$ holding a literal of polarity $b$, the literal of polarity $b$
on variable $2^{k_0 + L - 1 - j} - 1$, listed in increasing order of $j$; absent slots contribute
no literal.

articles.title: Binary-index translation of a dense formula
articles.statement:
The translation of a dense CNF formula
$\varphi$ replaces each clause $c$ of $\varphi$, keeping their order, by its binary-index
translation with offset $0$: if $c$ has length $L$, each slot $j$ of $c$ holding a literal of
polarity $b$ becomes the literal of polarity $b$ on variable $2^{L - 1 - j} - 1$, and absent slots
are dropped.

articles.title: The dense-to-binary translation on bit strings
articles.statement:
The translation of a bit string $w$ is the
backwards dense-to-binary translation applied to the reversal of $w$, started with no clause open,
with its literal, slot and clause counters all equal to $0$, and with empty output.

articles.title: Configurations of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
A configuration of the verifier is a
configuration of the multi-stack Turing machine model with the verifier's labels, states and
stack alphabets. It consists of an optional current label (absent once the machine has halted),
a state, which is either a symbol of the work alphabet $G$ or nothing, and for each stack the
list of symbols on it: Booleans on the output stack and symbols of $G$ on each of the four work
stacks.

articles.title: Dense CNF-SAT certificate check
articles.statement:
For bit strings $w$ (the encoded formula) and $y$ (the
certificate), the check of $y$ against $w$ is the Boolean result of the verifier's left-to-right
scan of the formula bits $w$, started with $y$ as the assignment bits not yet used by the current
clause, no used bits, and the current clause not yet satisfied.

articles.title: Satisfaction of a dense clause
articles.statement:
A finite bit sequence $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ satisfies
a clause $c$ when there are an index $j$ and a Boolean $b$ such that slot $j$ of $c$ holds the
literal $x_j = b$, $j < n$, and $a_j = b$. Variables $x_j$ with $j \ge n$ are unassigned and
satisfy no literal.

articles.title: Dense clause
articles.statement:
A clause is a finite list of slots, where slot $j$ records how the variable
$x_j$ occurs: the slot is either empty (the variable is absent) or holds a Boolean $b$, meaning
the literal $x_j = b$; so $b$ true gives $x_j$ and $b$ false gives $\lnot x_j$.

articles.title: The binary-index translation preserves satisfiability when all clauses have equal length
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a dense CNF formula all of whose clauses have the same length $V$. Then the
binary-index translation of $\varphi$ is satisfiable (some assignment of truth values to the
variables satisfies every clause) if and only if some finite list of truth values satisfies
$\varphi$.

articles.title: Truncating a satisfying assignment
articles.statement:
Let $w$ be a bit string and $\varphi$ the CNF formula
decoded from $w$. If a finite bit sequence $a$ satisfies $\varphi$, then so does the prefix of $a$
of length $|w|$ (all of $a$ when $a$ has at most $|w|$ bits).

articles.title: Satisfaction of a dense CNF formula
articles.statement:
A finite bit sequence $a$ satisfies a CNF formula
$\varphi$ when $a$ satisfies every clause of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Dense CNF formula
articles.statement:
A CNF formula is a finite list of dense clauses, read as the conjunction
of its clauses.

articles.title: The dense-to-binary translation on raw bits is polynomial-time
articles.statement:
There is a finite
multi-stack Turing machine whose input and output alphabets are the bits such that, for every bit
string $w$ of length $L$, the machine started on input $w$ halts within $2L^2 + 10L + 11$ steps with
the dense-to-binary translation of $w$ on its output stack and all other stacks empty.

articles.title: The translation on a whole clause
articles.statement:
Write $\mathrm{conv}(w, \iota, n, k, m, o)$ for the
reversed-string translation run on the bit string $w$ with open-clause flag $\iota$, literal count
$n$, slot count $k$, clause count $m$ and output $o$; juxtaposition of bit strings is
concatenation, $w^R$ is the reversal of $w$, $1^n$ is $n$ ones and $|x|$ is the length of a list
$x$. Let $c$ be a dense clause, $r$ and $o$ bit strings, $\iota$ a truth value and
$n, k, m \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $E(c)$ be the dense encoding of $c$ (its slot codes followed by the
terminator $00$), $c'$ the binary-index translation of $c$ with offset $0$, and $e$ the
concatenation of the binary codes of the literals of $c'$. Put $o' = 1^n 0\, o$ if $\iota$ is true
and $o' = o$ otherwise. Then
$\mathrm{conv}(E(c)^R r, \iota, n, k, m, o) =
\mathrm{conv}(r, \mathrm{true}, |c'|, |c|, m + 1, e\, o')$.

articles.title: The translation on the remaining clauses
articles.statement:
Write $\mathrm{conv}(w, \iota, n, k, m, o)$ for
the reversed-string translation run on the bit string $w$ with open-clause flag $\iota$, literal
count $n$, slot count $k$, clause count $m$ and output $o$; juxtaposition of bit strings is
concatenation, $w^R$ is the reversal of $w$, $1^n$ is $n$ ones and $|x|$ is the length of a list
$x$. For a dense clause $c$, let $E(c)$ be its dense encoding, $c'$ its binary-index translation
with offset $0$, $e(c)$ the concatenation of the binary codes of the literals of $c'$, and $B(c)$
the binary code of the clause $c'$. Let $p, k, m \in \mathbb{N}$, let $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_p$ be
dense clauses and let $D$ be a bit string. Then
$\mathrm{conv}(E(c_1)^R \cdots E(c_p)^R, \mathrm{true}, |c_0'|, k, m, e(c_0)\, D) =
1^{m + p} 0\, B(c_p) \cdots B(c_1) B(c_0) D$.

articles.title: The translation computes the binary encoding
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a dense CNF formula. Run the
reversed-string translation on the reversal of the dense encoding of $\varphi$, starting with no
clause open, literal count $0$, slot count $0$, clause count $0$ and empty output. The result is
the binary encoding of the binary-index translation of $\varphi$.

articles.title: The translation on the slots of a clause
articles.statement:
Write $\mathrm{conv}(w, \iota, n, k, m, o)$ for
the reversed-string translation run on the bit string $w$ with open-clause flag $\iota$, literal
count $n$, slot count $k$, clause count $m$ and output $o$; juxtaposition of bit strings is
concatenation, $w^R$ is the reversal of $w$ and $|x|$ is the length of a list $x$. Let $c$ be a
dense clause, $r$ and $o$ bit strings and $n, k, m \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $s(c)$ be the
concatenation of the two-bit codes of the slots of $c$, let $c'$ be the binary-index translation
of $c$ with offset $k$, and let $e$ be the concatenation of the binary codes of the literals of
$c'$. Then
$\mathrm{conv}(s(c)^R r, \mathrm{true}, n, k, m, o) =
\mathrm{conv}(r, \mathrm{true}, n + |c'|, k + |c|, m, e\, o)$.

articles.title: Step bound for the main loop
articles.statement:
For every bit string $l$, whether or not a clause is open, and
all natural numbers $n, k, m, Q$ with $|l| + n + k + m \le Q$, the exact step count of the main loop
on stash $l$ with literal, slot and clause counters $n, k, m$ is at most
$(|l| + 1)(2Q + 6) + Q + 4$.

articles.title: Step count of the main loop
The dense-to-binary translation on the reversed bit string
articles.statement:
The function
$\mathrm{conv}(w, \iota, n, k, m, o)$ consumes the bit string $w$ two bits at a time and prepends
to the output bit string $o$. The truth value $\iota$ records whether a clause is open, $n$ counts
the literals of the open clause, $k$ counts slots and $m$ counts clauses. Juxtaposition of bit
strings is concatenation, $1^n$ is $n$ ones, $(11)^k$ is $k$ copies of $11$, $\bar s$ is the
negation of a bit $s$, and $C$ is $1^n 0\, o$ if $\iota$ is true and $o$ otherwise. For every bit
$s$ and bit string $r$:

* $\mathrm{conv}(00\, r, \iota, n, k, m, o) = \mathrm{conv}(r, \mathrm{true}, 0, 0, m + 1, C)$;
* $\mathrm{conv}(10\, r, \iota, n, k, m, o) = \mathrm{conv}(r, \iota, n, k + 1, m, o)$;
* $\mathrm{conv}(s1\, r, \iota, n, k, m, o)$ is
  $\mathrm{conv}(r, \mathrm{true}, n + 1, k + 1, m, (11)^k 0 \bar s\, o)$ if $\iota$ is true and
  $\mathrm{conv}(r, \mathrm{false}, n, k, m, o)$ otherwise;
* if $w$ has fewer than two bits, $\mathrm{conv}(w, \iota, n, k, m, o) = 1^m 0\, C$.

On the reversed dense encoding a slot $s_1 s_2$ is read as $s_2 s_1$: $00$ is a terminator, which
closes the open clause and opens the next, $10$ is an absent slot, and $s1$ is a present slot,
whose literal $(2^k - 1, \bar s)$ is emitted (its binary code is $(11)^k 0 \bar s$) inside a
clause and skipped outside one. At the end the open clause is closed and the unary clause count
is emitted.

articles.title: Dense decoding with an accumulator
articles.statement:
Given a bit string $w$ and the list $c$ of slots read so
far for the current clause, stored in reverse order, the result is the CNF formula obtained by
reading $w$ two bits at a time: $00$ outputs the current clause in reading order and continues
with no slots read; $01$ adds an empty slot to the current clause; and $1s$, for a bit $s$, adds a
slot holding the Boolean $\lnot s$, so $10$ adds a positive and $11$ a negative literal. When
fewer than two bits remain, decoding stops and outputs no further clauses, so a trailing
unterminated clause and a dangling odd bit are ignored and decoding is total.

articles.title: Decoding inverts the dense encoding
articles.statement:
For every CNF formula $\varphi$, decoding the bit
string that encodes $\varphi$ gives back $\varphi$. In particular, every CNF formula is the
decoding of some bit string.

articles.title: Dense decoding of CNF formulas
articles.statement:
The CNF formula decoded from a bit string $w$ is the
result of the accumulator decoding of $w$ started with no slots read for the current clause:
$w$ is read two bits at a time, $00$ ends a clause, $01$ is an empty slot, $10$ a positive and
$11$ a negative literal, and a trailing unterminated clause and a dangling odd bit are ignored.

articles.title: Self-delimiting code of a block of ones
articles.statement:
For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the self-delimiting
form of the bit string of $k$ ones is $k$ copies of $11$ followed by a single $0$.

articles.title: Dense CNF-SAT is in NP
articles.statement: **Dense CNF-SAT is in NP.**

articles.title: Dense CNF-SAT as a decision problem
articles.statement:
The decision problem of dense CNF-SAT accepts a bit
string $w$ exactly when $w$ belongs to dense CNF-SAT, that is, when the formula decoded from $w$
in the dense clause encoding has a satisfying assignment.

articles.title: Draining the work stacks of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
Let $\mathit{ans}$ be a Boolean, let
$i$, $a$, $b$ be lists of symbols of the work alphabet $G$, and let $v$ be any state. Start the
verifier's program at the label $\mathrm{drainI}(\mathit{ans})$ in state $v$, with the input
stack holding $i$, the formula stash empty, the assignment stacks $A$ and $B$ holding $a$ and
$b$, and the output stack empty. It then runs for exactly $|i| + |a| + |b| + 3$ steps and reaches
the label $\mathrm{finish}(\mathit{ans})$ with no symbol in its state, all four work stacks empty
and the output stack still empty.

articles.title: Right-tagged encoding of a certificate
articles.statement:
For a list $y$ of bits, its right-tagged encoding
is the list of symbols of the work alphabet $G$ obtained by replacing each bit $b$ of $y$ with
the right symbol $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\ b)$. This is how the certificate appears after the
separator in the pair encoding of a formula and a certificate.

articles.title: Left-tagged encoding of a bit list
articles.statement:
For a list $l$ of bits, its encoding on a work stack
of the dense-SAT verifier is the list of symbols of the work alphabet $G$ obtained by replacing
each bit $b$ of $l$ with the left symbol $\mathrm{inl}(b)$.

articles.title: Dense encoding of a clause
articles.statement:
The bit string encoding a clause is the concatenation of the
two-bit codes of its slots, in order (empty slot $01$, positive literal $10$, negative literal
$11$), followed by the terminator $00$.

articles.title: Dense encoding of a CNF formula
articles.statement:
The dense encoding of a CNF formula $\varphi$ is the bit
string obtained by concatenating, in order, the encodings of the clauses of $\varphi$, where a
clause is encoded as the two-bit codes of its slots followed by the terminator $00$.

articles.title: Binary codes of literals on variables one less than a power of two
articles.statement:
For every
$k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every truth value $b$, the binary code of the literal of polarity $b$ on
variable $2^k - 1$ is $k$ copies of $11$, followed by $0$, followed by the bit $b$.

articles.title: The binary code of $2^k - 1$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k$, the binary code of
$2^k - 1$ (Mathlib's encoding of natural numbers as bit lists, least significant bit first) is
the list of $k$ ones.

articles.title: Two-bit code of a slot
articles.statement:
Slot $j$ of a dense clause is empty (variable $x_j$ is absent),
holds the positive literal $x_j$, or holds the negative literal $\neg x_j$. Its code is $01$ when
empty, $10$ for the positive literal and $11$ for the negative literal.

articles.title: Closing a clause in the translated output
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$ and a bit string
$o$, closing a clause with $n$ literals in front of $o$ gives the bit string consisting of $n$
ones, then a zero, then $o$; that is, the unary count of $n$ is prepended to $o$.

In the translation, $o$ starts with the codes of the clause's $n$ literals, already emitted.

articles.title: Single-pass evaluation of a dense CNF encoding
articles.statement:
The scan $E(r, u, v, f)$ takes the formula
bits $r$ still to be read, the assignment bits $u$ not yet used by the current clause, the bits
$v$ already used by it (most recent first) and a boolean $f$ recording whether the current clause
is already satisfied; write $x u'$ for the list with first bit $x$ followed by the list $u'$. It
reads $r$ two bits at a time; let $r'$ be the bits after the pair read. On $00$ (end of clause)
the result is $f \wedge E(r', \overline{v}\,u, [\,], \mathrm{false})$, where $\overline{v}\,u$ is
the reversal of $v$ followed by $u$. On $01$ (an empty slot) the result is $E(r', u', x v, f)$
when $u = x u'$, and $E(r', [\,], v, f)$ when $u$ is empty. On $1s$ (a literal with sign bit $s$)
the result is $E(r', u', x v, f \vee (x = \neg s))$ when $u = x u'$, and $E(r', [\,], v, f)$
when $u$ is empty. When fewer than two bits remain, the result is true.

The scan mirrors the verifier machine step by step.

articles.title: Indexed evaluation of a dense CNF encoding
articles.statement:
The scan $I(r, a, j, f)$ takes the formula
bits $r$ still to be read, an assignment $a$ (a list of booleans), the position $j$ of the next
slot in the current clause and a boolean $f$ recording whether the current clause is already
satisfied. It reads $r$ two bits at a time; let $r'$ be the bits after the pair read. On $00$
(end of clause) the result is $f \wedge I(r', a, 0, \mathrm{false})$. On $01$ (an empty slot) the
result is $I(r', a, j + 1, f)$. On $1s$ (a literal with sign bit $s$) the result is
$I(r', a, j + 1, f')$, where $f'$ is true when $f$ is true, or when $j < |a|$ and the entry $a_j$
of $a$ (counting from $0$) equals $\neg s$.
When fewer than two bits remain, the result is true.

articles.title: The converter's final phase
articles.statement:
Write $0$ for false, $1$ for true and $1^j$ for $j$ copies
of $1$. Let $o$ be a bit string, $\iota$ a flag saying whether a clause is open, and $n, k, m$
natural numbers with $n = 0$ if no clause is open; let $c = n + 1$ if a clause is open and $c = 0$
otherwise. Started at the label that clears the slot counter at the end, for the flag $\iota$, with
empty internal state, empty input and stash, output $o$, literal, slot and clause counter stacks
holding $n$, $k$ and $m$ ones respectively, and an empty scratch stack, the converter reaches in
exactly $(k + 1) + c + (m + 1)$ steps the halting configuration with empty internal state, every
stack but the output empty, and output $1^m 0 1^n 0 o$ if a clause is open and $1^m 0 o$ otherwise
(listed from the top of the stack).

articles.title: Formula filter of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
The partial map on the work alphabet $G$ that
sends each left symbol $\mathrm{inl}(b)$ to itself and is undefined on every right symbol
$\mathrm{inr}(o)$, including the separator $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{none})$, written $\#$.

The verifier's first copying loop uses it, so on the pair encoding of a formula and a
certificate it stops at the separator $\#$.

articles.title: Certificate filter of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
The partial map on the work alphabet $G$
that sends each right symbol $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\ b)$ to the left symbol
$\mathrm{inl}(b)$ and is undefined on every other symbol, that is on the left symbols and on the
separator $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{none})$.

articles.title: Work alphabet of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
The work alphabet $G$ is the disjoint union of
the Booleans and the optional Booleans. Its elements are the left symbols $\mathrm{inl}(b)$ and
the right symbols $\mathrm{inr}(o)$, where $b$ is a Boolean and $o$ is either
$\mathrm{some}\ b$ or $\mathrm{none}$. This is the alphabet of the pair encoding, in which
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{none})$ is the separator $\#$.

Formula and assignment bits are stored on the work stacks as left symbols $\mathrm{inl}(b)$.

articles.title: The dense certificate check runs in polynomial time
articles.statement:
The map sending a pair $(w, y)$ of bit
strings to the result of the certificate check on formula bits $w$ and assignment bits $y$ is
polynomial-time computable, where pairs of bit strings carry their canonical bitstring encoding.

articles.title: Labels of the dense-to-binary converter
articles.statement:
The labels of the dense-to-binary converter
program are the moving label $\mathrm{mv}$; the reading label $\mathrm{rd}(\iota)$ for a Boolean
$\iota$; the second-read label $\mathrm{rd2}(\iota, s)$ for Booleans $\iota$ and $s$; the two
literal labels $\mathrm{litA}$ and $\mathrm{litB}$; the two closing labels $\mathrm{eN}$ and
$\mathrm{eK}$; the clearing label $\mathrm{fK}(\iota)$ for a Boolean $\iota$; the literal-count
label $\mathrm{fN}$; and the clause-count label $\mathrm{fM}$. Equality of labels is decidable.

Here $\iota$ records whether a clause is open, and $s$ is the first bit read of a slot.

articles.title: Labels of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
The labels of the verifier's program are
$\mathrm{read1}$, $\mathrm{read2}$, $\mathrm{back1}$ and $\mathrm{back2}$; $\mathrm{c0}(f)$ and
$\mathrm{c1}(f, b)$ for Booleans $f$ and $b$; $\mathrm{adv}(f, o)$ for a Boolean $f$ and an
optional Boolean $o$; $\mathrm{restore}(f)$ for a Boolean $f$; and $\mathrm{drainI}(a)$,
$\mathrm{drainA}(a)$, $\mathrm{drainB}(a)$ and $\mathrm{finish}(a)$ for a Boolean $a$. There are
finitely many labels, and equality of labels is decidable.

The labels $\mathrm{c0}(f)$ and $\mathrm{c1}(f, b)$ read the two bits of a token, with $f$
recording whether the current clause is already satisfied. $\mathrm{adv}(f, o)$ moves one
assignment bit from stack $B$ to stack $A$ ($o = \mathrm{some}\ s$ for the literal token $1s$),
and $\mathrm{restore}(f)$ moves the used assignment bits back from $A$ to $B$.

articles.title: Decoded clauses are no longer than the input
articles.statement:
For every bit string $r$ and every clause
$c_0$, every clause produced by the auxiliary decoder run on $r$ with accumulated partial clause
$c_0$ has length at most $|c_0| + |r|$.

articles.title: Running the generic copy loop of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
Let $s$ be a work stack, $g$ a
partial map on the work alphabet $G$, $t$ an optional target work stack other than $s$, and
$\ell$, $\ell'$ labels such that the verifier's program at $\ell$ is the generic loop with source
$s$, map $g$, target $t$, own label $\ell$ and exit $\ell'$. Let $o$ be a list of output bits.
Let $x = x_1 \dots x_n$, $y = y_1 \dots y_n$ and $r$ be lists of symbols of $G$ with
$g(x_j) = y_j$ defined for every $j$, and with $r$ empty or $g$ undefined at the first symbol of
$r$. Let $V$ be work-stack contents with $V(s) = x r$, and let $v$ be any state. Started at
$\ell$ in state $v$ with work stacks $V$ and output stack $o$, the program runs for exactly
$n + 1$ steps and reaches the label $\ell'$. Its state is then the first symbol of $r$ (nothing
if $r$ is empty) and its output stack is still $o$. Its work stacks are obtained from $V$ by
replacing stack $s$ with $r$ minus its first symbol (empty if $r$ is empty) and then, if $t$ is
a stack, pushing $y_1, \dots, y_n$ onto $t$ one at a time.

articles.title: Generic copy loop of the dense-SAT verifier
articles.statement:
For a work stack $s$, a partial map $g$ on
the work alphabet $G$, an optional target work stack $t$, and labels $\ell$ (the loop's own
label) and $\ell'$ (its exit), the generic loop is the program statement that does the following.
It pops the top of $s$ and stores the popped symbol $x$ as the machine state (nothing if $s$ is
empty). If $x$ exists and $g(x) = y$ is defined, it pushes $y$ onto $t$ (or pushes nothing when
there is no target stack) and jumps to $\ell$. Otherwise, when $s$ was empty or $g$ is undefined
at $x$, it jumps to $\ell'$.

articles.title: Work stacks from four lists
articles.statement:
Given four lists $i$, $f$, $a$, $b$ of work symbols in $G$,
the contents of the verifier's work stacks in which the input stack holds $i$, the formula stash
$F$ holds $f$, and the assignment stacks $A$ and $B$ hold $a$ and $b$.

articles.title: Moving the input onto the stash
articles.statement:
Let $l$, $a$, $o$ be bit strings and $v$ an optional
bit, and list stacks top first. Started at the moving label with internal state $v$, input stack
$l$, stash $a$, output stack $o$, empty counter stacks $N$, $K$, $M$ and empty scratch stack $T$,
the dense-to-binary converter reaches, in exactly $|l| + 1$ steps, the label for reading with no
clause open, with no internal state, an empty input stack, the reversal of $l$ followed by $a$ on
the stash, output stack $o$, and $N$, $K$, $M$, $T$ still empty.

articles.title: Pair encoding $w \# y$
articles.statement:
For bit strings $w$ and $y$, the word over the pair alphabet
$G = \mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\,\mathrm{Bool}$ consisting of the bits $b$ of $w$ in
order, each tagged on the left as $\mathrm{inl}\,b$, then the separator
$\# = \mathrm{inr}\,\mathrm{none}$, then the bits $b$ of $y$ in order, each tagged on the right as
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\,b)$. This is the input of the dense CNF-SAT verifier.

articles.title: Splitting the verifier input
articles.statement:
For all bit strings $w$ and $y$, the verifier program
leads in exactly $(|w| + 1) + (|y| + 1) + (|w| + 1) + (|y| + 1)$ steps from the configuration at
label $\mathsf{read1}$ with empty machine state, the input stack holding (from the top) the bits
$b$ of $w$ as $\mathrm{inl}\,b$, the separator $\mathrm{inr}\,\mathrm{none}$ and the bits $b$ of
$y$ as $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\,b)$, and all other stacks empty, to the configuration at label
$\mathsf{c0}(\mathrm{false})$ with empty machine state, the input stack holding the bits $b$ of
$w$ as $\mathrm{inl}\,b$, the stack $B$ holding the bits $b$ of $y$ as $\mathrm{inl}\,b$ (both from
the top in order), and the stacks $F$, $A$ and the output stack empty.

The four phases stash $w$ on $F$ and $y$ on $A$, then move them back onto the input stack and
$B$.

articles.title: The dense-to-binary converter program
articles.statement:
The program uses an input stack, a stash, an
output stack, unary counter stacks $N$, $K$, $M$ and a scratch stack $T$; each label first pops
one stack and keeps the popped bit (or nothing, if the stack was empty) as its internal state.
Below, $\iota$ says whether a clause is open, $0$ is false and $1$ is true.

Moving: pop the input; if a bit $b$ was popped, push $b$ onto the stash and repeat, otherwise go to
reading with $\iota$ false.

Reading with $\iota$: pop the stash; if a bit $s$ was popped, go to the second read with $\iota$
and $s$, otherwise go to clearing with $\iota$.

Second read with $\iota$ and $s$: pop the stash. If it was empty, go to clearing with $\iota$. If
it gave $0$: when $s = 1$, push $1$ onto $K$ and go to reading with $\iota$; when $s = 0$ and
$\iota$ is true, push $0$ onto the output and go to the first closing label; when $s = 0$ and
$\iota$ is false, go to the second closing label. If it gave $1$: when $\iota$ is true, push
$\lnot s$ and then $0$ onto the output and go to the first literal label; otherwise go to reading
with $\iota$ false.

First literal label: pop $K$; if a bit was popped, push $1$ twice onto the output and $1$ onto $T$
and repeat, otherwise go to the second literal label.

Second literal label: pop $T$; if a bit was popped, push $1$ onto $K$ and repeat, otherwise push
$1$ onto $N$, then $1$ onto $K$, and go to reading with $\iota$ true.

First closing label: pop $N$; if a bit was popped, push $1$ onto the output and repeat, otherwise
go to the second closing label.

Second closing label: pop $K$; if a bit was popped, repeat, otherwise push $1$ onto $M$ and go to
reading with $\iota$ true.

Clearing with $\iota$: pop $K$; if a bit was popped, repeat, otherwise push $0$ onto the output and
go to the literal-count label if $\iota$ is true and to the clause-count label otherwise.

Literal-count label: pop $N$; if a bit was popped, push $1$ onto the output and repeat, otherwise
push $0$ onto the output and go to the clause-count label.

Clause-count label: pop $M$; if a bit was popped, push $1$ onto the output and repeat, otherwise
halt.

articles.title: The dense CNF-SAT verifier program
articles.statement:
The program assigns a statement to each label. Every
pop stores the popped symbol, or nothing if the stack was empty, as the machine state.

* $\mathsf{read1}$: pop the input stack; while the popped symbol is some $\mathrm{inl}\,b$, push
  $\mathrm{inl}\,b$ onto $F$ and pop again; otherwise go to $\mathsf{read2}$.
* $\mathsf{read2}$: pop the input stack; while the popped symbol is some
  $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{some}\,b)$, push $\mathrm{inl}\,b$ onto $A$ and pop again; otherwise go
  to $\mathsf{back1}$.
* $\mathsf{back1}$: pop $F$ and push each popped symbol onto the input stack until $F$ is empty,
  then go to $\mathsf{back2}$.
* $\mathsf{back2}$: pop $A$ and push each popped symbol onto $B$ until $A$ is empty, then go to
  $\mathsf{c0}(\mathrm{false})$.
* $\mathsf{c0}(fl)$: pop the input stack; if the popped symbol is $\mathrm{inl}\,b$, go to
  $\mathsf{c1}(fl, b)$, otherwise go to $\mathsf{drainI}(\mathrm{true})$.
* $\mathsf{c1}(fl, \mathrm{false})$: pop the input stack; on $\mathrm{inl}\,\mathrm{false}$ go to
  $\mathsf{restore}(fl)$, on $\mathrm{inl}\,\mathrm{true}$ go to
  $\mathsf{adv}(fl, \mathrm{none})$, otherwise go to $\mathsf{drainI}(\mathrm{true})$.
* $\mathsf{c1}(fl, \mathrm{true})$: pop the input stack; on $\mathrm{inl}\,s$ go to
  $\mathsf{adv}(fl, \mathrm{some}\,s)$, otherwise go to $\mathsf{drainI}(\mathrm{true})$.
* $\mathsf{adv}(fl, o)$: pop $B$; if a symbol $x$ was popped, push $x$ onto $A$ and go to
  $\mathsf{c0}(fl')$, where $fl'$ is true when $fl$ is true, or when $o = \mathrm{some}\,s$ for a
  bit $s$ with $x = \mathrm{inl}(\lnot s)$; if $B$ was empty, go to $\mathsf{c0}(fl)$.
* $\mathsf{restore}(fl)$: pop $A$ and push each popped symbol onto $B$ until $A$ is empty, then
  go to $\mathsf{c0}(\mathrm{false})$ if $fl$ is true and to $\mathsf{drainI}(\mathrm{false})$
  otherwise.
* $\mathsf{drainI}(ans)$, $\mathsf{drainA}(ans)$, $\mathsf{drainB}(ans)$: pop and discard the
  input stack, $A$, $B$ respectively until it is empty, then go to $\mathsf{drainA}(ans)$,
  $\mathsf{drainB}(ans)$, $\mathsf{finish}(ans)$ respectively.
* $\mathsf{finish}(ans)$: push $ans$ onto the output stack, clear the machine state and halt.
