symbol $H$ control symbols. Consider the relation in which a word $w$ with exactly one control
symbol rewrites to $w'$ by one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$. This relation is
confluent: if $w$ rewrites in zero or more such steps to both $w_1$ and $w_2$, then $w_1$ and
$w_2$ both rewrite in zero or more such steps to a common word.

articles.title: Rewriting preserves the number of control symbols
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing
machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and call the states and the halting symbol
$H$ control symbols. If a word $w$ rewrites to $w'$ in one step of the rewriting system simulating
$M$, then $w$ and $w'$ contain the same number of control symbols.

articles.title: Number of control symbols
articles.statement:
The number of control symbols of a word $w$ over the symbols of
the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine is the number of letters of $w$ that are
states or the halting symbol $H$.

articles.title: Rewrites from words with one control symbol
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with
finitely many states and tape symbols, and call the states and the halting symbol $H$ control
symbols. A word $w$ rewrites to $w'$ by a controlled step when $w$ contains exactly one control
symbol and $w$ rewrites to $w'$ in one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$.

articles.title: The halting symbol erases the tape
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely
many states and tape symbols, and let $\vdash$, $\dashv$ be the end markers and $H$ the halting
symbol of the rewriting system simulating $M$. For all words $X$ and $Y$ of tape symbols, the word
$\vdash X\,H\,Y \dashv$ rewrites in zero or more steps of this rewriting system to the halting
word $\vdash H \dashv$.

articles.title: A halted configuration rewrites to the halting word
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing
machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and let $\vdash$, $\dashv$ be the end markers
and $H$ the halting symbol of the rewriting system simulating $M$. Let $c$ be a configuration of
$M$ at which $M$ has no next step, and let $w$ be a word that spells $c$: for some state $q$, tape
symbol $h$ and lists $L$, $R$ of tape symbols, $c$ is in state $q$ with $h$ under the head, the
tape left of the head reads $L$ from left to right and the tape right of the head reads $R$, up to
blanks at the far ends, and $w = \vdash L\,q\,h\,R \dashv$. Then $w$ rewrites in zero or more steps
of this rewriting system to the halting word $\vdash H \dashv$.

articles.title: Domino (Post correspondence problem)
articles.statement:
A domino over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a pair
$(t, b)$ of words over $\alpha$: its top word $t$ and its bottom word $b$.

articles.title: End domino of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction
articles.statement:
Over the alphabet $\alpha$ extended with the
star $\star$ and the end marker $\diamond$, the end domino is $(\star\diamond, \diamond)$: its top
word is $\star$ followed by $\diamond$, and its bottom word is $\diamond$.

articles.title: End marker
articles.statement:
The end marker $\diamond$ is the symbol of the extended alphabet of the
MPCP-to-PCP reduction that is neither a letter of $\alpha$ nor the star $\star$.

articles.title: Unique splitting at a marked letter
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a property of the elements of a type
$\alpha$, let $A$ and $B$ be lists over $\alpha$ none of whose elements satisfy $P$, and let
$y \in \alpha$. If $C$ and $D$ are lists over $\alpha$ and $x \in \alpha$ satisfies $P$ with
$C\,x\,D = A\,y\,B$ (concatenation), then $C = A$, $x = y$ and $D = B$.

articles.title: Thue equivalence from a word with one control symbol uses only controlled steps
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be
a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and call the states and
the halting symbol $H$ control symbols. Suppose $w$ contains exactly one control symbol, and $w$
and $w'$ are equivalent under the equivalence relation generated by one-step rewriting in the
rewriting system simulating $M$. Then $w$ and $w'$ are equivalent under the equivalence relation
generated by the one-step rewrites from words with exactly one control symbol.

articles.title: Erasing rules
articles.statement:
For a finite tape alphabet $\Gamma$, let $H$ be the halting symbol of the
rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine with tape alphabet $\Gamma$. The erasing rules
are the rewriting rules $c\,H \to H$ and $H\,c \to H$ for every tape symbol $c \in \Gamma$: the
halting symbol deletes the tape symbol on either side of it.

articles.title: Some finite Thue system has an undecidable word problem
articles.statement:
(Post, Markov) There are a
finite alphabet $\alpha$, with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers,
and a finite list $R$ of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ such that no multi-stack Turing machine
decides, for words $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, whether $x$ and $y$ are equivalent under the
reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure of one-step rewriting by $R$.

articles.title: MPCP is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet $\alpha$, with a primitive recursive
coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no multi-stack Turing machine decides, for
a finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, whether every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top and
a nonempty bottom and $P$ has a solution of the modified Post correspondence problem, that is,
a nonempty sequence of dominoes of $P$, repetitions allowed, that starts with the first domino
of $P$ and whose tops and bottoms concatenate to the same word.

articles.title: The Post correspondence problem is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet $\alpha$, with
a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no multi-stack Turing
machine decides whether a finite list of dominoes over $\alpha$ has a solution, that is, a
nonempty sequence of dominoes of the list, repetitions allowed, whose tops and bottoms
concatenate to the same word.

articles.title: Reachability for string rewriting is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet $\alpha$,
with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no multi-stack
Turing machine decides, for a finite list $R$ of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ and words $x$ and
$y$ over $\alpha$, whether every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side
and $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$.

articles.title: The uniform word problem for Thue systems is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet
$\alpha$, with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no
multi-stack Turing machine decides, for a finite list $R$ of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ and
words $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, whether $x$ and $y$ are equivalent under the reflexive,
symmetric and transitive closure of one-step rewriting by $R$.

articles.title: A word with one control symbol splits at it
articles.statement:
If a word $w$ over the symbols of the
rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine contains exactly one control symbol (a state
symbol or the halting symbol), then $w = p\,x\,s$ for a control symbol $x$ and words $p$ and
$s$ that contain no control symbol.

articles.title: One machine step is one rewrite
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely
many tape symbols and states. If the word $w$ spells the configuration $c$ and $M$ steps from
$c$ to $c'$, then $w$ rewrites in one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$ to a word
$w'$ that spells $c'$.

articles.title: The halting word
articles.statement:
The halting word is the word $\vdash H \dashv$ made of the left end
marker, the halting symbol and the right end marker. It is the target word of the rewriting
simulation of a single-tape machine.

articles.title: The start word
articles.statement:
For an input $l$ of tape symbols, the start word is
$\vdash q_0\, h\, R \dashv$, where $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are the left and right end markers,
$q_0$ is the default state, $h$ is the first symbol of $l$ (the default tape symbol if $l$ is
empty) and $R$ is the rest of $l$. It spells the configuration in state $q_0$ with head symbol
$h$, empty left part and right part $R$.

articles.title: Invariant of the rewriting simulation of a single-tape machine
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape
machine with finitely many tape symbols and states, and $l$ an input. A word $w$ satisfies the
invariant for $l$ when either $w$ spells a configuration that $M$ reaches from its initial
configuration on $l$, or $M$ halts on $l$ and $w = \vdash X\, H\, Y \dashv$ for some words $X$
and $Y$ of tape symbols, where $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are the left and right end markers and $H$
is the halting symbol. It serves as the invariant of the words reachable from the start word
of $l$.

articles.title: Boolean test for control symbols
articles.statement:
The Boolean function on the symbols of the rewriting
system simulating a single-tape Turing machine that is true on every state symbol and on the
halting symbol $H$, and false on every tape symbol and on the end markers $\vdash$ and $\dashv$.

articles.title: Control symbols
articles.statement:
A symbol of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape Turing machine
is a control symbol if it is a state symbol or the halting symbol $H$; tape symbols and the end
markers $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are not control symbols.

articles.title: Boolean check for PCP solutions
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive
coding and decidable equality, and let $P$ and $s$ be lists of dominoes over $\alpha$. The Boolean
solution check of $s$ for $P$ is true exactly when $s$ is nonempty, every domino of $s$ occurs in
$P$, and the top word of $s$ equals the bottom word of $s$, and it is false otherwise.

articles.title: PCP solution
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite list of dominoes. A solution of $P$ is a nonempty
sequence $d_1, \dots, d_k$ of dominoes, each occurring in $P$ (repetitions allowed), such that the
concatenation of the top words of $d_1, \dots, d_k$ equals the concatenation of their bottom
words.

articles.title: Total length of dominoes that are at least as long on top
articles.statement:
Write $|w|$ for the length of a
word $w$. Let $s$ be a finite sequence of dominoes over an alphabet. If every domino $(t, b)$ in
$s$ satisfies $|b| \le |t|$, then the concatenation of the bottom words of $s$ is no longer than
the concatenation of the top words of $s$.

articles.title: Total length of dominoes that are strictly longer on top
articles.statement:
Write $|w|$ for the length of a
word $w$. Let $s$ be a nonempty finite sequence of dominoes over an alphabet. If every domino
$(t, b)$ in $s$ satisfies $|b| < |t|$, then the concatenation of the bottom words of $s$ is strictly
shorter than the concatenation of the top words of $s$.

articles.title: The alphabet inside the extended alphabet
articles.statement:
Each letter $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha$ is
regarded as a symbol of the extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction, which consists of the
letters of $\alpha$, the star $\star$ and the end marker $\diamond$.

articles.title: Erasing stars and end markers
articles.statement:
For a word $w$ over the extended alphabet of the
MPCP-to-PCP reduction, this is the word over $\alpha$ obtained from $w$ by deleting every star
$\star$ and every end marker $\diamond$, keeping the letters of $\alpha$ in their order.

articles.title: MPCP many-one reduces to PCP
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive
coding, and let $\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ extended with two new symbols, the star and the end marker.
There is a computable function $f$ from finite lists of dominoes over $\alpha$ to finite lists of
dominoes over $\alpha'$ such that, for every list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, $f(P)$ has a PCP
solution if and only if both every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top word and a nonempty bottom
word, and $P$ has an MPCP solution.

articles.title: PCP over a finite alphabet many-one reduces to PCP over the binary alphabet
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$
be a finite alphabet with a primitive recursive encoding of its letters as natural numbers. Then
the Post correspondence problem over $\alpha$ is many-one reducible to the Post correspondence
problem over the two-letter alphabet of Booleans $\mathrm{true}$ and $\mathrm{false}$: there is a
computable map $f$ sending each finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$ to a finite list $f(P)$
of dominoes over the Booleans such that $P$ has a PCP solution if and only if $f(P)$ has a PCP
solution.

articles.title: Single-tape halting many-one reduces to the word problem of a fixed Thue system
articles.statement:
Let $M$
be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and let $R_M$ be the
rewriting system simulating $M$. Then the set of inputs on which $M$ halts is many-one reducible
to the set of pairs $(x, y)$ of words over the symbols of $R_M$ that are equivalent under the
reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure of one-step rewriting by $R_M$.

articles.title: Single-tape halting many-one reduces to string rewriting reachability
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a
single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols. Then the set of inputs on
which $M$ halts is many-one reducible to the set of instances $(R, x, y)$, where $R$ is a list of
rules and $x$, $y$ are words over the symbols of the rewriting system simulating $M$, such that
every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side and $x$ rewrites to $y$ in
zero or more steps of $R$.

articles.title: Starred image of a domino
articles.statement:
For a word $u$ over $\alpha$, write $\star u$ for the word over
the extended alphabet obtained by putting a star $\star$ before every letter of $u$, and $u\star$
for the word obtained by putting a star after every letter. A domino $(t, b)$ over $\alpha$ is sent
to the domino $(\star t, b\star)$ over the extended alphabet.

articles.title: Image of a PCP instance under a word map
articles.statement:
Given a map $f$ from words over $\alpha$
to words over $\beta$ and a list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the image of $P$ under $f$ is the
list of dominoes over $\beta$ obtained by replacing each domino $(u, v)$ of $P$ by $(f(u), f(v))$,
in the same order.

articles.title: MPCP reduces to PCP on instances with nonempty words
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a list of dominoes over
an alphabet $\alpha$ in which every domino has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom. Then $P$ has
an MPCP solution if and only if the image of $P$ under the reduction from MPCP to PCP, an
instance over $\alpha$ extended with a star and an end marker, has a PCP solution.

articles.title: On instances with nonempty words, a PCP solution of the reduced instance gives an MPCP solution
articles.statement:
**On instances with nonempty words, a PCP solution of the reduced instance gives an MPCP
solution.** Let $P$ be a list of dominoes in which every domino has a nonempty top and a nonempty
bottom. If the image of $P$ under the reduction from MPCP to PCP has a PCP solution, then $P$ has
an MPCP solution.

articles.title: The modified Post correspondence problem
articles.statement:
A list $P$ of dominoes has an MPCP solution
when $P$ is nonempty and some PCP solution of $P$ starts with the first domino of $P$.

articles.title: Rewriting at a state symbol
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many
states and tape symbols, and let $\sqcup$ be its blank symbol. For words $u$, $v$ and a state $q$,
the successor of $u\,q\,v$ is defined as follows. If $v$ does not begin with a tape symbol, there
is none. If $v = a\,v'$ for a tape symbol $a$: when $M$ has no transition from $q$ reading $a$,
it is $u\,H\,v'$, where $H$ is the halting symbol; when $M$ writes $b$ and enters $q'$, it is
$u\,q'\,b\,v'$; when $M$ moves right and enters $q'$, it is $u\,a\,q'\,\sqcup \dashv v''$ if
$v' = {\dashv}\,v''$ for the right end marker $\dashv$, it is $u\,a\,q'\,c\,v''$ if
$v' = c\,v''$ for a tape symbol $c$, and there is none otherwise; when $M$ moves left and enters
$q'$, it is $u' \vdash q'\,\sqcup\,a\,v'$ if $u = u' \vdash$ for the left end marker $\vdash$, it
is $u'\,q'\,c\,a\,v'$ if $u = u'\,c$ for a tape symbol $c$, and there is none otherwise.

articles.title: Boolean test for nonempty words
articles.statement:
For a list $P$ of dominoes, this Boolean test returns
true exactly when every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom.

articles.title: Instances with nonempty words
articles.statement:
A list $P$ of dominoes has nonempty words when every
domino of $P$ has a nonempty top word and a nonempty bottom word.

articles.title: The halting word is irreducible
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely
many states and tape symbols. There is no word $w$ such that the halting word $\vdash H \dashv$
rewrites to $w$ in one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$.

articles.title: The Post correspondence problem is undecidable over the binary alphabet
articles.statement:
The Post
correspondence problem over the two-letter alphabet of Booleans $\mathrm{true}$ and
$\mathrm{false}$, that is, the property of a finite list $P$ of dominoes over the Booleans of
having a PCP solution, is not decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine: no multi-stack machine
computes a total function $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that, for every such $P$ with
natural-number encoding $n_P$, $g(n_P) = 1$ exactly when $P$ has a PCP solution.

articles.title: The unary PCP criterion
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with at most one letter, and write
$|w|$ for the length of a word $w$. A finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$ has a PCP solution
if and only if either some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$ has $|t| = |b|$, or some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$
has $|t| < |b|$ and some domino $(t', b')$ in $P$ has $|b'| < |t'|$.

articles.title: An injective word homomorphism preserves and reflects PCP solvability
articles.statement:
Let $h$ map each
letter of $\alpha$ to a word over $\beta$, and extend it to words by
$h(a_1 \cdots a_n) = h(a_1) \cdots h(a_n)$. If this extension is injective on words over $\alpha$,
then for every list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the list obtained from $P$ by replacing each
domino $(u, v)$ by $(h(u), h(v))$ has a PCP solution if and only if $P$ has a PCP solution.

articles.title: An MPCP solution gives a PCP solution of the reduced instance
articles.statement:
If a list $P$ of dominoes
has an MPCP solution, then the image of $P$ under the reduction from MPCP to PCP has a PCP
solution.

articles.title: The Post correspondence problem
articles.statement:
A list $P$ of dominoes is a solvable instance of the
Post correspondence problem when it has a PCP solution: a nonempty sequence of dominoes from $P$,
repetitions allowed, whose top words and bottom words concatenate to the same word.

articles.title: The nonempty-words test is primitive recursive
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $\alpha$ with a
primitive recursive coding, the Boolean test of whether every domino of a list over $\alpha$ has
a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom is a primitive recursive function of the list.

articles.title: PCP is recursively enumerable
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive
coding, the set of lists of dominoes over $\alpha$ that have a PCP solution is recursively
enumerable.

The proof searches all candidate sequences.

articles.title: The total reduction from MPCP to PCP
articles.statement:
For a list $P$ of dominoes, the total reduction
sends $P$ to its image under the reduction from MPCP to PCP when every domino of $P$ has a
nonempty top and a nonempty bottom, and to the empty instance, which has no PCP solution,
otherwise.

articles.title: The rules for one transition
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many
states and tape symbols, let $\sqcup$ be its blank symbol, and write $\vdash$, $\dashv$ for the end
markers and $H$ for the halting symbol. The rules for a state $q$ reading a tape symbol $a$ are:
the rule $q\,a \to H$ if $M$ has no transition from $q$ reading $a$; the rule
$q\,a \to q'\,b$ if $M$ writes $b$ and enters $q'$; the rules
$q\,a \dashv \to a\,q'\,\sqcup \dashv$ and, for every tape symbol $c$, $q\,a\,c \to a\,q'\,c$ if
$M$ moves right and enters $q'$; and the rules ${\vdash}\,q\,a \to {\vdash}\,q'\,\sqcup\,a$ and,
for every tape symbol $c$, $c\,q\,a \to q'\,c\,a$ if $M$ moves left and enters $q'$.

articles.title: The rewriting system simulating a Turing machine
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing
machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and write $H$ for the halting symbol. The
rewriting system simulating $M$ is the finite list of rules consisting of the rules for every
state $q$ reading every tape symbol $a$, followed by the erasing rules $c\,H \to H$ and
$H\,c \to H$ for every tape symbol $c$.

articles.title: The word of a configuration
articles.statement:
For a state $q$, a tape symbol $h$ and words $L$, $R$ of
tape symbols, the word of the configuration in state $q$ with head symbol $h$, left part $L$
(in reading order, from left to right) and right part $R$ is $\vdash L\,q\,h\,R \dashv$, where
$\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are the end markers.

articles.title: Words spelling a configuration
articles.statement:
A word $w$ spells a configuration $c$ of a single-tape
Turing machine if there are a state $q$, a tape symbol $h$ and words $L$, $R$ of tape symbols
such that $c$ is in state $q$, its head reads $h$, its tape reads $L$ immediately to the left of
the head and $R$ immediately to the right of it, with blanks beyond, and
$w = \vdash L\,q\,h\,R \dashv$.

articles.title: Splitting a rewrite site at its control symbol
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $u$, $v$, $p$, $s$ be words
over the symbols of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine, and let $x$ and $y$ be
symbols. If no symbol of $A$ or of $B$ is a control symbol (a state symbol or the halting symbol),
$x$ is a control symbol, and $u\,p\,x\,s\,v = A\,y\,B$, then $u\,p = A$, $x = y$ and $s\,v = B$.

articles.title: A star after every letter
articles.statement:
Let $\star$ be the star of the extended alphabet. For a word
$u = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$, the word $u\star$ over the extended alphabet is
$a_1 \star a_2 \star \cdots a_n \star$, obtained by putting a star after every letter of $u$; the
empty word gives the empty word.

articles.title: A star before every letter
articles.statement:
Let $\star$ be the star of the extended alphabet. For a word
$u = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$, the word $\star u$ over the extended alphabet is
$\star a_1 \star a_2 \cdots \star a_n$, obtained by putting a star before every letter of $u$; the
empty word gives the empty word.

articles.title: The star symbol
articles.statement:
The star $\star$ is the new symbol of the extended alphabet that is
neither a letter of $\alpha$ nor the end marker $\diamond$.

articles.title: The start domino of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction
articles.statement:
For a domino $(t, b)$ over an alphabet
$\alpha$, its start domino is the domino $(\star t, \star b \star)$ over the extended alphabet,
where $\star t$ puts the star $\star$ before every letter of $t$ and $b \star$ puts a star after
every letter of $b$, so that the bottom word gets one extra star in front.

articles.title: Local confluence on words with one control symbol
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape machine with
finite tape alphabet and finite set of states, and let $w$ be a word over the symbols of its
rewriting system that contains exactly one control symbol (a state symbol or the halting symbol).
If $w$ rewrites in one step to $w_1$ and in one step to $w_2$ under the rules of $M$, then there is
a word $d$ such that $w_1$ rewrites to $d$ in at most one step and $w_2$ rewrites to $d$ in zero or
more steps.

Rewriting at a state symbol is deterministic, and the two erasures at the halting symbol commute.

articles.title: A rewrite at the control symbol
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape machine with finite tape
alphabet and finite set of states. Let $x$ be a control symbol (a state symbol or the halting
symbol $H$) and let $u$ and $v$ be words that contain no control symbol. If $u\,x\,v$ rewrites in
one step to $w'$ under the rules of $M$, then either $x$ is a state symbol $q$ and the successor of
$u\,q\,v$ under the rules for $q$ is defined and equals $w'$, or $x = H$ and either $u = u'\,c$ for
a word $u'$ and a tape symbol $c$ with $w' = u'\,H\,v$, or $v = c\,v'$ for a tape symbol $c$ and a
word $v'$ with $w' = u\,H\,v'$.

articles.title: Every rewrite preserves the invariant of reachable words
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a single-tape machine
with finite tape alphabet and finite set of states, and let $l$ be an input word. Write $\vdash$
and $\dashv$ for the left and right end markers and $H$ for the halting symbol. A word $w$
satisfies the invariant for $M$ and $l$ when either $w$ spells a configuration that $M$ reaches from
its initial configuration on $l$ (the configuration with state $q$, head symbol $h$, left part $L$
and right part $R$, finite words of tape symbols read from left to right beyond which the tape is
blank, is spelled ${\vdash}\,L\,q\,h\,R\,{\dashv}$), or $M$ halts on $l$ and
$w = {\vdash}\,X\,H\,Y\,{\dashv}$ for words $X$ and $Y$ of tape symbols. If $w$ satisfies the
invariant and rewrites in one step to $w'$ under the rules of $M$, then $w'$ satisfies the
invariant.

articles.title: Swapping top and bottom
articles.statement:
For a finite sequence $s$ of dominoes, the swapped sequence is
obtained from $s$ by exchanging the top and bottom word of every domino: each $(t, b)$ becomes
$(b, t)$, and the order of the dominoes is unchanged.

articles.title: The extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $\alpha$, the extended
alphabet consists of the letters of $\alpha$ together with two new symbols: the star $\star$ and
the end marker $\diamond$.

It is represented so that it has a primitive recursive encoding whenever $\alpha$ has one.

articles.title: A single-tape machine halts iff its start word rewrites to the halting word
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a
single-tape machine with finite tape alphabet and finite set of states, and write $\vdash$ and
$\dashv$ for the left and right end markers and $H$ for the halting symbol. For every input word
$l$, $M$ halts on $l$ if and only if the start word ${\vdash}\,q_0\,h\,R\,{\dashv}$ of $l$
rewrites to the halting word ${\vdash}\,H\,{\dashv}$ in zero or more steps under the rules of $M$,
where $q_0$ is the default state, $h$ is the first letter of $l$ (the blank if $l$ is empty) and
$R$ is the rest of $l$.

articles.title: A single-tape machine halts iff its start word is Thue equivalent to the halting word
articles.statement:
Let
$M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, write $\vdash$ and
$\dashv$ for the left and right end markers and $H$ for the halting symbol, and let $l$ be an input
word of tape symbols. Then $M$ halts on $l$ if and only if the start word of $l$ and the halting
word ${\vdash}\,H\,{\dashv}$ are equivalent under the reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure
of one-step rewriting by the rewriting system simulating $M$.

articles.title: Unary PCP is decidable by a multi-stack machine
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with at most
one letter whose elements have a computable encoding. Then the Post correspondence problem over
$\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine: some multi-stack Turing machine decides, for every
finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, whether $P$ has a PCP solution.

articles.title: PCP is Turing-recognizable
articles.statement:
For every alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive
encoding, there is a multi-stack Turing machine that, started on the binary encoding of a list
$P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, halts exactly when $P$ has a PCP solution.

articles.title: Symbols of the rewriting system of a single-tape machine
articles.statement:
For a tape alphabet $\Gamma$ and
a set of states $\Lambda$, the symbols of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine are
a tape symbol $a$ for each $a \in \Gamma$, a state symbol $q$ for each $q \in \Lambda$, the left end
marker $\vdash$, the right end marker $\dashv$ and the halting symbol $H$.

articles.title: The reduction from MPCP to PCP
articles.statement:
Write $\star$ for the star and $\diamond$ for the end
marker of the extended alphabet; for a word $u$ over $\alpha$, $\star u$ puts a star before every
letter of $u$ and $u \star$ puts a star after every letter of $u$. The empty list of dominoes is
sent to the empty list. A list $P = [d_0, d_1, \ldots, d_n]$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, with
$d_0 = (t_0, b_0)$, is sent to the following list of dominoes over the extended alphabet: first
the start domino $(\star t_0, \star b_0 \star)$, then the domino $(\star t, b \star)$ for each
domino $(t, b)$ of $P$ in order (including $d_0$), and last the end domino
$(\star \diamond, \diamond)$, whose top word is a star followed by the end marker.

articles.title: Top word of a sequence of dominoes
articles.statement:
For a sequence of dominoes
$(t_1, b_1), \ldots, (t_n, b_n)$, its top word is the concatenation $t_1 t_2 \cdots t_n$ of their
top words; the empty sequence has the empty top word.

articles.title: Unary code of a letter
articles.statement:
Given an indexing $e$ assigning a natural number to each letter of
$\alpha$, the unary code of a letter $a$ is the Boolean word consisting of $e(a)$ copies of
$\mathrm{true}$ followed by one $\mathrm{false}$; writing $1$ for true and $0$ for false, it is
$1^{e(a)} 0$.

articles.title: The unary code of an injective indexing is uniquely decodable
articles.statement:
Let $e$ be an injective map
from $\alpha$ to the natural numbers, and let $c(a)$ be the unary code of a letter $a$: $e(a)$
copies of $\mathrm{true}$ followed by one $\mathrm{false}$. Then the map sending a word
$a_1 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$ to the Boolean word $c(a_1) \cdots c(a_n)$ is injective.

articles.title: The unary PCP test
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with at most one letter, and write $|w|$
for the length of a word $w$. For a finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the unary test of
$P$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$ has $|t| = |b|$, or
some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$ has $|t| < |b|$ and some domino $(t', b')$ in $P$ has $|b'| < |t'|$.

articles.title: Erasing the markers from a domino
articles.statement:
For a domino $(t, b)$ over the extended alphabet, its
unmapping is the domino over $\alpha$ obtained by deleting every star $\star$ and every end marker
$\diamond$ from both $t$ and $b$, keeping the letters of $\alpha$ in order.

It reads a domino of the reduced PCP instance back as a domino over $\alpha$.

articles.title: Single-bit words
articles.statement:
Over the alphabet consisting of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$
and two bits $0$ and $1$, the single-bit words form the language $\{0, 1\}$ whose only words are
the one-letter words $0$ and $1$.

articles.title: Bit words
articles.statement:
Over the alphabet consisting of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two
bits $0$ and $1$, the bit words form the language $\{0, 1\}^*$ of all finite words, including
the empty word, all of whose letters are bits.

articles.title: Bits as letters
articles.statement:
Each boolean $b$ (with false read as $0$ and true as $1$) is sent to the
corresponding bit letter of the alphabet consisting of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and
two bits $0$ and $1$.

articles.title: Unique decomposition at the separator
articles.statement:
Over the alphabet consisting of the letters of
$T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, let $u, u'$ be words over $T$ and $v, v'$ words
over the bits. If $u \# v = u' \# v'$, then $u = u'$ and $v = v'$.

articles.title: Regularity of context-free languages is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet $T$,
with a primitive recursive encoding and decidable equality, such that no multi-stack Turing
machine decides, for an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$, whether the language of $g$
is regular.

articles.title: The auxiliary productions of the regularity grammar
articles.statement:
For a natural number $s$, these are
the following productions over the nonterminals $\mathbb{N}$ and the alphabet consisting of the
letters of the finite alphabet $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, where $A_n$
denotes nonterminal $n$: $A_0 \to A_{s+4} \# A_1$, $A_0 \to A_2 \# A_3$, $A_1 \to \varepsilon$,
$A_1 \to 0 A_1$, $A_1 \to 1 A_1$, $A_2 \to \varepsilon$, $A_3 \to \varepsilon$,
$A_3 \to 0 A_3 1$, and $A_2 \to t A_2$ for each letter $t$ of $T$.

In the regularity grammar of a grammar $g$, $s$ is the start nonterminal of $g$, and these
productions are added to those of $g$ with every nonterminal $n$ renamed $n + 4$.

articles.title: Regularity of the reduction language characterises universality
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite
alphabet and $L$ a language over $T$. Over the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$
and $1$, the language $L \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, of the words $u \# v$
with $u$ a word over $T$, $v$ a word over the bits, and $u \in L$ or $v = 0^n 1^n$ for some $n$,
is regular if and only if $L$ contains every word over $T$.

articles.title: The reduction language of a universal language is regular
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite alphabet
and $L$ a language over $T$ that contains every word over $T$. Over the letters of $T$, a
separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, the language
$L \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, which here equals $T^* \# \{0,1\}^*$, is
regular.

articles.title: Every production of the regularity grammar is sound for its intended languages
articles.statement:
Let $g$
be an encoded context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, and let
$G$ be the regularity grammar of $g$, over the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$
and $1$; words over $T$ are read as words over this alphabet. Assign to the nonterminals of $G$
the languages $V(0) = L(g) \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, where $L(g)$ is the
language of $g$, $V(1) = \{0,1\}^*$, $V(2) = T^*$, $V(3) = \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, and for each
$n$, $V(n + 4)$ the set of words that $g$ generates from its nonterminal $n$. Then $V$ is a
valuation of $G$: for every production $A \to \alpha$ of $G$, the language obtained from $\alpha$
by replacing each nonterminal $B$ by $V(B)$ and each letter $a$ by $\{a\}$, and concatenating, is
contained in $V(A)$.

articles.title: The language of the regularity grammar
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar over a
finite alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, with language $L(g)$. Over the letters of $T$, a
separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, the regularity grammar of $g$ generates exactly
$L(g) \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, the set of words $u \# v$ with $u$ a word
over $T$, $v$ a word over the bits, and $u \in L(g)$ or $v = 0^n 1^n$ for some $n$.

articles.title: One-letter words over $T$
articles.statement:
This is the language over the alphabet $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$
of the reduction from universality to regularity consisting of the one-letter words $t$ with
$t \in T$.

articles.title: Words over $T$ in the reduction alphabet
articles.statement:
This is the language $T^*$ over the alphabet
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ of the reduction from universality to regularity: the words, including the
empty word, all of whose letters lie in $T$.

articles.title: Alphabet of the reduction from universality to regularity
articles.statement:
For a type $T$, the alphabet
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ consists of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$,
all distinct.

articles.title: Universality many-one reduces to regularity of context-free languages
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a
finite alphabet with decidable equality and a primitive recursive coding, and let
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ extend $T$ by a separator $\#$ and two bits. There is a computable map $f$
from encoded context-free grammars over $T$ to encoded context-free grammars over
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ such that a grammar $g$ generates every word over $T$ if and only if the
language generated by $f(g)$ is regular.

articles.title: Shifted right-hand sides generate the images of words
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an encoded context-free
grammar over a finite alphabet $T$, let $G$ be the grammar over $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ that the
reduction from universality to regularity builds from $g$, and let $L_G(m)$ be the language $G$
generates from nonterminal $m$. For a word $u$ over $T$ write $\bar u$ for the same word over
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$. Let $W$ assign to each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ a language $W(n)$ over $T$ with
$\bar u \in L_G(n + 4)$ for every $u \in W(n)$. Let $\alpha$ be a right-hand side over nonterminals
in $\mathbb{N}$ and terminals in $T$, and let $\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ with each nonterminal $n$
replaced by $n + 4$ and each terminal read in $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$. If $u$ lies in the language
that $\alpha$ denotes when each nonterminal $n$ is read as $W(n)$, then $\bar u$ lies in the
language that $\alpha'$ denotes when each nonterminal $m$ is read as $L_G(m)$.

articles.title: Shifted right-hand sides denote images of words of $g$
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an encoded context-free
grammar over $T$, let $L_g(n)$ be the language $g$ generates from nonterminal $n$ and $L(g)$ its
language. For a word $u$ over $T$ write $\bar u$ for the same word over $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$.
Let $V$ assign to each $m \in \mathbb{N}$ the language $V(m)$ over $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ given by
$V(0) = L(g)\,\#\,\{0,1\}^* \cup T^*\,\#\,\{0^k1^k : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$, $V(1) = \{0,1\}^*$,
$V(2) = T^*$, $V(3) = \{0^k1^k : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$ and $V(n + 4) = \{\bar u : u \in L_g(n)\}$.
Let $\alpha$ be a right-hand side over nonterminals in $\mathbb{N}$ and terminals in $T$, and let
$\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ with each nonterminal $n$ replaced by $n + 4$ and each terminal read in
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$. If $w$ lies in the language that $\alpha'$ denotes when each nonterminal
$m$ is read as $V(m)$, then $w = \bar u$ for some $u$ in the language that $\alpha$ denotes when
each nonterminal $n$ is read as $L_g(n)$.

articles.title: Productions of the regularity grammar preserve generated languages
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an
encoded context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, let $G$ be the
regularity grammar of $g$, over the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$,
and for a nonterminal $B$ let $L_G(B)$ be the language that the grammar denoted by $G$ generates
from $B$. If $(A, \alpha)$ is an encoded production of $G$ and $w$ is a word in the language that
the decoded right-hand side $\alpha$ denotes when each nonterminal $B$ is read as $L_G(B)$, each
letter $a$ as $\{a\}$, and these languages are concatenated in order, then $w \in L_G(A)$.

articles.title: Non-universality makes the reduction language non-regular
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a language over an
alphabet $T$, let $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ extend $T$ by a separator $\#$ and two bits, and let
$R(L) = L\,\#\,\{0,1\}^* \cup T^*\,\#\,\{0^n1^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ over this alphabet. If some
word $u$ over $T$ is not in $L$, then $R(L)$ is not regular.

The words $v$ over the bits with $u\,\#\,v \in R(L)$ are exactly the words $0^n1^n$.

articles.title: `{0ⁿ1ⁿ}` is not regular
articles.statement:
The words `0ⁱ` are pairwise inequivalent for the Nerode
congruence.

articles.title: Grammar of the reduction from universality to regularity
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an encoded
context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$ with start nonterminal $s$, and write $N_k$ for
nonterminal $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon$ for the empty word. The reduction grammar of $g$
is the encoded grammar over $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ (the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two
bits $0$ and $1$) with start nonterminal $N_0$ and the productions $N_0 \to N_{s+4}\,\#\,N_1$,
$N_0 \to N_2\,\#\,N_3$, $N_1 \to \varepsilon$, $N_1 \to 0\,N_1$, $N_1 \to 1\,N_1$,
$N_2 \to \varepsilon$, $N_2 \to t\,N_2$ for each $t \in T$, $N_3 \to \varepsilon$ and
$N_3 \to 0\,N_3\,1$, together with the production $N_{n+4} \to \alpha'$ for each production
$N_n \to \alpha$ of $g$, where $\alpha'$ is $\alpha$ with each nonterminal $N_k$ replaced by
$N_{k+4}$ and each letter of $T$ kept.

Its language is $L(g)\,\#\,\{0,1\}^* \cup T^*\,\#\,\{0^n1^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$, where $L(g)$
is the language of $g$.

articles.title: The target language of the regularity reduction
articles.statement:
For a language $L$ over an alphabet
$T$, this is the language over the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and the two bits $0, 1$
consisting of the words $u \# v$ with $u \in T^*$ and $v \in \{0,1\}^*$ such that $u \in L$ or
$v = 0^n 1^n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$; that is,
$L \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$.

articles.title: Languages assigned to the nonterminals of the regularity grammar
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an encoded
context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, let $L(g)$ be its
language and $L_g(n)$ the language $g$ generates from nonterminal $n$. Over the alphabet
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ (the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$), write
$\bar u$ for a word $u$ over $T$ read in this alphabet. This assigns to each $m \in \mathbb{N}$
the language $V(m)$ over $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ given by
$V(0) = L(g)\,\#\,\{0,1\}^* \cup T^*\,\#\,\{0^k1^k : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$, $V(1) = \{0,1\}^*$,
$V(2) = T^*$, $V(3) = \{0^k1^k : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$ and $V(n + 4) = \{\bar u : u \in L_g(n)\}$.

These are the intended languages of the nonterminals of the regularity grammar of $g$.

articles.title: The separator letter
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $T$, among the letters of the reduction (the letters
of $T$, a separator and two bits), this is the separator, written $\#$.

articles.title: Shifted derivations in the regularity grammar
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar
over a finite alphabet $T$, and let $n$ be a nonterminal of $g$. If $g$ derives a word $u$ over
$T$ from $n$, then the regularity grammar of $g$ derives from its nonterminal $n + 4$ the word $u$
read over the extended alphabet, each letter $t$ of $T$ replaced by the corresponding letter.

articles.title: Shifting a production into the regularity grammar
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite alphabet with
decidable equality, and consider the alphabet $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ of the letters of $T$, a
separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$. An encoded production $(n, \alpha)$ over $T$, with
left-hand side the nonterminal $n$ and right-hand side $\alpha$, is sent to the encoded production
$(n + 4, \alpha')$ over $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$, where $\alpha'$ is $\alpha$ with each nonterminal
$k$ replaced by the nonterminal $k + 4$ and each letter of $T$ read as the same letter of
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$.

articles.title: Shifting a symbol into the regularity grammar
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite alphabet with decidable
equality, and consider the alphabet $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ of the letters of $T$, a separator
$\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$. A symbol of an encoded grammar over $T$, that is, a nonterminal
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ or a letter $t \in T$, is sent to a symbol of an encoded grammar over
$T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$: the nonterminal $n$ goes to the nonterminal $n + 4$, and the letter $t$
goes to the letter $t$ of $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$.

articles.title: Alphabet letters in the extended alphabet
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $T$, each letter $t \in T$ is
sent to the corresponding letter among the letters of the reduction (the letters of $T$, a
separator and two bits).

articles.title: A grammar is universal iff its regularity grammar generates a regular language
articles.statement:
Let $g$
be an encoded context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$. Then $g$ generates every word over
$T$ if and only if the regularity grammar of $g$ generates a regular language.

articles.title: The language $\{0^n 1^n\}$
articles.statement:
The language over the two bits $0$ and $1$ (the Booleans
false and true) consisting of the words $0^n 1^n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, that is, $n$ zeros
followed by $n$ ones.

articles.title: Copy domino
articles.statement:
For a letter $a$ of $\alpha$, the copy domino of $a$ is the domino over the
extended alphabet whose top and bottom are both the one-letter word $a$.

articles.title: The backward direction of the MPCP reduction
articles.statement:
Let $(R, x, y)$ be a reachability instance
and read words over $\alpha$ as words of letters. Let $A$ be a sequence of dominoes of the MPCP
instance of $(R, x, y)$. For all words $v, s, t$ over $\alpha$, if $s$ rewrites to $t$ under $R$
in zero or more steps and the top of $A$ equals $v \star t$ followed by the bottom of $A$, where
$\star$ is the row separator, then $s v$ rewrites to $y$ under $R$ in zero or more steps.

Reading the dominoes left to right, $s$ is the part of the current row already matched, with
bottoms $t$, and $v$ is the rest of the row still to be matched on top.

articles.title: Derivations in a string rewriting system
articles.statement:
For a list of rules $R$, a word $x$ derives a
word $y$ when $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$, that is, when $(x, y)$ lies in
the reflexive-transitive closure of the one-step rewriting relation of $R$.

articles.title: The forward direction of the MPCP reduction
articles.statement:
Let $(R, x, y)$ be a reachability instance
and read words over $\alpha$ as words of letters. If a word $w$ over $\alpha$ rewrites to $y$
under $R$ in zero or more steps and every letter of $w$ occurs in a rule of $R$, in $x$ or in
$y$, then there is a sequence $A$ of dominoes of the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$ whose top is
$w \star$ followed by the bottom of $A$, where $\star$ is the row separator.

articles.title: Comparing words of letters before a separator
articles.statement:
Let $u, v$ be words over $\alpha$, read as
words of letters, and let $X, Y$ be words over the extended alphabet of $\alpha$. If
$u X = v \star Y$, where $\star$ is the row separator, then there is a word $w$ over $\alpha$
with $v = u w$ and $X = w \star Y$.

articles.title: Final domino
articles.statement:
For a word $y$ over $\alpha$, the final domino of $y$ is the domino over the
extended alphabet with top $y \star \diamond$ and bottom $\diamond$, where $y$ is read as a word
of letters, $\star$ is the row separator and $\diamond$ is the end marker.

articles.title: Letters differ from the star
articles.statement:
For every letter $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha$, the symbol
$a$ of the extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction is different from the star $\star$.

articles.title: Lifting a word to the extended alphabet
articles.statement:
A word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$ is sent to
the word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over the extended alphabet of $\alpha$ in which each $a_i$ is read as a
letter.

articles.title: Reachability with nonempty sides many-one reduces to MPCP with nonempty words
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive coding, and let $\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ extended
with two new symbols, the star and the end marker. There is a computable function $f$ from
instances $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem over $\alpha$, where $R$ is a list of rewriting
rules over $\alpha$ and $x$ and $y$ are words over $\alpha$, to finite lists of dominoes over
$\alpha'$ such that, for every such instance, the following are equivalent: every rule of $R$ has
a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side and $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of
$R$; and every domino of $f(R, x, y)$ has a nonempty top word and a nonempty bottom word and
$f(R, x, y)$ has an MPCP solution.

articles.title: Reachability for rules with nonempty sides many-one reduces to PCP
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an
alphabet with a primitive recursive coding, let $\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ extended with two new
symbols, the star and the end marker, and let $\alpha''$ be $\alpha'$ extended in the same way by
two further new symbols. There is a computable function $f$ from instances $(R, x, y)$ of the
reachability problem over $\alpha$, where $R$ is a list of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ and $x$
and $y$ are words over $\alpha$, to finite lists of dominoes over $\alpha''$ such that, for every
such instance, $f(R, x, y)$ has a PCP solution if and only if every rule of $R$ has a nonempty
left side and a nonempty right side and $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$.

articles.title: Rewriting steps keep the letters of the instance
articles.statement:
Let $(R, x, y)$ be an instance of the
reachability problem over an alphabet $\alpha$. If a word $w$ rewrites to a word $w'$ in one
step of $R$ and every letter of $w$ is among the letters of the instance, then every letter of
$w'$ is among the letters of the instance.

articles.title: Rewriting systems with nonempty sides
articles.statement:
A string rewriting system $R$, given as a list of
rules $(l, r)$, has nonempty sides when every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side $l$ and a
nonempty right side $r$.

articles.title: The total reduction of reachability with nonempty sides to MPCP
articles.statement:
On an instance
$(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem, the reduction returns the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$
when every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side, and otherwise the empty
list of dominoes, which has no solution.

articles.title: The domino of a rewriting rule
articles.statement:
For a rule $(l, r)$ over an alphabet $\alpha$, the domino
of the rule has top $l$ and bottom $r$, read as words over the extended alphabet, that is, $\alpha$
together with a star and an end marker.

articles.title: Rewriting rules
articles.statement:
A rewriting rule over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a pair $(l, r)$ of words
over $\alpha$; applying it replaces an occurrence of $l$ by $r$.

articles.title: The separator domino
articles.statement:
Over the extended alphabet, that is, an alphabet $\alpha$ together
with a star $\star$ and an end marker $\diamond$, the separator domino has top and bottom both
equal to the one-letter word $\star$; the star separates the rows of a derivation.

articles.title: Reachability reduces to MPCP
articles.statement:
For an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem,
$x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$ if and only if the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$
has an MPCP solution, that is, a solution that starts with its first domino.

articles.title: The reachability problem for string rewriting
articles.statement:
An instance $(R, x, y)$ consists of a string
rewriting system $R$, given as a list of rules, and two words $x$ and $y$; it is a yes-instance of
the reachability problem when $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$.

articles.title: The start domino of the reduction from reachability to MPCP
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be a word over an
alphabet $\alpha$, and extend $\alpha$ by a star $\star$ and an end marker $\diamond$. The start
domino of $x$ has top the one-letter word $\diamond$ and bottom the word $\diamond x \star$, with
the letters of $x$ read as letters of the extended alphabet.

articles.title: One-step rewriting
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a string rewriting system, given as a list of rules. A word
$w$ rewrites to a word $w'$ in one step of $R$ when there are a rule $(l, r)$ of $R$ and words
$u$ and $v$ with $w = u l v$ and $w' = u r v$.

articles.title: Letters of a rewriting instance
articles.statement:
For an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem,
where $R = [(l_1, r_1), \dots, (l_k, r_k)]$ is a list of rewriting rules and $x$, $y$ are words,
the letters of the instance form the word $l_1 r_1 l_2 r_2 \cdots l_k r_k \, x \, y$, a list in
which a letter may occur several times.

articles.title: The word problem of a Thue system
articles.statement:
On an instance $(R, x, y)$, where $R$ is a list of
rewriting rules and $x$, $y$ are words, the word problem asks whether $x$ and $y$ are related by
the equivalence relation generated by the one-step rewriting relation of $R$, that is, by its
reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure.

articles.title: The MPCP instance of a reachability instance
articles.statement:
Let $(R, x, y)$ be an instance of the
reachability problem over an alphabet $\alpha$, where $R = [(l_1, r_1), \dots, (l_k, r_k)]$, and
write $\#$ for the separator and $\diamond$ for the end marker of the extended alphabet
$\mathrm{Sym}(\alpha)$, in which letters of $\alpha$ are read as letters. Let $a_1 \cdots a_m$ be
the word $l_1 r_1 l_2 r_2 \cdots l_k r_k \, x \, y$, the letters of the instance. The MPCP
instance of $(R, x, y)$ is the list of dominoes (top word, bottom word)
$(\diamond, \diamond x \#), (y \# \diamond, \diamond), (\#, \#), (l_1, r_1), \dots, (l_k, r_k),
(a_1, a_1), \dots, (a_m, a_m)$, in this order. Its first domino is $(\diamond, \diamond x \#)$.

articles.title: Grammar of all words
articles.statement:
For a finite alphabet $T$, the encoded context-free grammar over $T$
whose start nonterminal is $S = 0$ and whose productions are $S \to \varepsilon$ and $S \to a S$
for every letter $a \in T$.

It generates every word over $T$.

articles.title: Membership in the first grammar of a pair is computable
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be an alphabet with a
primcodable encoding and decidable equality. The predicate that holds of a pair
$((g_1, g_2), w)$, where $g_1, g_2$ are encoded context-free grammars over $T$ and $w$ is a word
over $T$, exactly when $w$ lies in the language of $g_1$, is a computable predicate.

articles.title: Whether two context-free languages are disjoint is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is an alphabet $T$,
with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no
multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of
encoded context-free grammars over $T$, whether no word lies in both $L(G_1)$ and $L(G_2)$,
where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$.

$T$ is not required to be finite.

articles.title: Whether a context-free grammar is ambiguous is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is an alphabet $T$,
with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no
multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for an encoded context-free
grammar $G$ over $T$, whether $G$ is ambiguous, that is, whether some word has two different
leftmost derivations from the start nonterminal of $G$.

$T$ is not required to be finite. This is Sipser's problem $\mathit{AMBIG}_{\mathit{CFG}}$.

articles.title: Equivalence of context-free grammars is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet $T$, with
decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack
machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of encoded
context-free grammars over $T$, whether $L(G_1) = L(G_2)$, where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$.

This is Sipser's problem $\mathit{EQ}_{\mathit{CFG}}$.

articles.title: Inclusion of context-free languages is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet $T$, with
decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack
machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of encoded
context-free grammars over $T$, whether $L(G_1) \subseteq L(G_2)$, where $L(G)$ is the language
of $G$.

articles.title: Whether two context-free languages intersect is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is an alphabet $T$,
with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no
multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of
encoded context-free grammars over $T$, whether some word lies in both $L(G_1)$ and $L(G_2)$,
where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$.

$T$ is not required to be finite. This is Sipser's problem $\mathit{OVERLAP}_{\mathit{CFG}}$.

articles.title: Whether a context-free grammar generates every word is undecidable
articles.statement:
There is a finite
alphabet $T$, with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such
that no multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for an encoded
context-free grammar $G$ over $T$, whether every word over $T$ lies in the language of $G$.

This is Sipser's problem $\mathit{ALL}_{\mathit{CFG}}$.

articles.title: Disjointness of context-free languages is not recognizable
articles.statement:
There is an alphabet $T$,
with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of
encoded context-free grammars over $T$ whose languages are disjoint (no word lies in both) is not
recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

articles.title: Equivalence of context-free grammars is not recognizable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet
$T$, with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$
of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ whose languages are equal is not recognizable by a
multi-stack Turing machine.

articles.title: Inclusion of context-free languages is not recognizable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet $T$,
with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of
encoded context-free grammars over $T$ for which the language of $g_1$ is contained in the
language of $g_2$ is not recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

articles.title: The complement of PCP is not recognizable
articles.statement: **The complement of PCP is not recognizable**, over some finite alphabet.

articles.title: Universality of context-free grammars is not recognizable
articles.statement:
There is a finite alphabet
$T$, with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of encoded
context-free grammars over $T$ whose language contains every word over $T$ is not recognizable by
a multi-stack Turing machine.

The complement of the Post correspondence problem reduces to this problem.

articles.title: Post's theorem, contrapositive
articles.statement:
A recognizable undecidable predicate has an
unrecognizable complement.

articles.title: Equivalence of context-free grammars is co-recognizable
articles.statement:
For every alphabet $T$ with a
primcodable encoding and decidable equality, the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of encoded
context-free grammars over $T$ whose languages are equal is co-recognizable by a multi-stack
Turing machine.

A recognizer for the complement searches for a word in exactly one of the two languages.

articles.title: Inclusion of context-free languages is co-recognizable
articles.statement:
For every alphabet $T$ with a
primcodable encoding and decidable equality, the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of encoded
context-free grammars over $T$ for which the language of $g_1$ is contained in the language of
$g_2$ is co-recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

articles.title: Universality of context-free grammars is co-recognizable
articles.statement:
For every alphabet $T$ with a
primcodable encoding and decidable equality, the set of encoded context-free grammars over $T$
whose language contains every word over $T$ is co-recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

A recognizer for the complement searches for a word outside the language.

articles.title: The overlap problem for context-free grammars is recognizable
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be an alphabet
with a primitive recursive coding into the natural numbers and decidable equality. For an
encoded context-free grammar $G$ over $T$, write $L(G)$ for the language it generates. The
problem $\mathrm{OVERLAP}_{\mathrm{CFG}}$, the set of pairs $(G, H)$ of encoded context-free
grammars over $T$ such that some word $w$ over $T$ lies in both $L(G)$ and $L(H)$, is
recognizable by a multi-stack machine.

The proof searches for a common word, using that membership in a context-free language is
decidable.

articles.title: List of all letters
articles.statement:
For a finite alphabet $\alpha$, the list of all letters of $\alpha$,
each appearing exactly once, in some fixed but unspecified order.

articles.title: No right symbol directly precedes a left symbol in a left-then-right word
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$
and $\beta$ be types and consider words over the disjoint union $\alpha \sqcup \beta$. For all
words $u, v$ over $\alpha \sqcup \beta$, all $b \in \beta$ and $a \in \alpha$, all words $X$ over
$\alpha$ and all words $Y$ over $\beta$, we have $u\,b\,a\,v \ne X\,Y$: a word over $\alpha$
followed by a word over $\beta$ never has a symbol of $\beta$ immediately followed by a symbol of
$\alpha$.

articles.title: Domino-independent productions of the universality grammar
articles.statement:
For a finite alphabet
$\alpha$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is a list of productions whose nonterminals $N_0, N_1, \dots$
are encoded as natural numbers and whose terminals are the letters $a \in \alpha$ and the two bits
$\mathbf{t}$ (true) and $\mathbf{f}$ (false). Writing $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ for the
unary code of an index $i$, the list consists of the productions $N_3 \to \varepsilon$,
$N_5 \to \varepsilon$, $N_6 \to \varepsilon$, $N_7 \to \varepsilon$; $N_5 \to \mathbf{t}\,N_5$,
$N_5 \to \mathbf{f}\,N_5$, $N_6 \to \mathbf{t}\,N_6$, $N_6 \to \mathbf{f}\,N_6$;
$N_0 \to N_3$, $N_0 \to N_3\,\mathbf{f}\,N_5$, $N_0 \to N_6\,c(k)\,N_6$, $N_0 \to N_1$,
$N_0 \to N_2$; for each letter $a \in \alpha$, the productions $N_3 \to a\,N_3$,
$N_4 \to a\,N_3$, $N_6 \to a\,N_6$, $N_0 \to N_6\,\mathbf{t}\,a\,N_6$ and
$N_0 \to N_6\,\mathbf{f}\,a\,N_6$; and for each $i < k$, the production $N_7 \to c(i)\,N_7$.

The nonterminal $N_0$ is the start symbol. The intended languages are: for $N_3$ the words of
letters, for $N_4$ the nonempty words of letters, for $N_5$ the words of bits, for $N_6$ all
words, and for $N_7$ the concatenated codes of indices below $k$. The start productions (those
with left side $N_0$) generate the malformed words and the two mismatch nonterminals $N_1$ and
$N_2$.

articles.title: Unary code of an index
articles.statement:
The code of an index $i \in \mathbb{N}$ is the bit word
$\mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ of length $i + 1$: the bit $\mathbf{t}$ (true) followed by $i$ copies
of the bit $\mathbf{f}$ (false); with $|$ for true and $1$ for false, it is the word $|\,1^i$.

articles.title: Concatenated index codes are uniquely decodable
articles.statement:
For a finite sequence
$I = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of natural numbers write $c(I) = c(i_1) \cdots c(i_n)$, where
$c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ is the unary code of $i$. If $I$ and $J$ are finite sequences of
natural numbers with $c(I) = c(J)$, then $I = J$.

articles.title: Codes of indices below $k$ contain no code of $k$
articles.statement:
Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let
$J = (j_1, \dots, j_n)$ be a finite sequence of natural numbers with $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$. Write
$c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ for the unary code of $i$ and $c(J) = c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$. Then
there are no bit words $Y$ and $Z$ with $c(J) = Y\,c(k)\,Z$.

articles.title: Concatenated code of an index sequence
articles.statement:
For a finite sequence $I = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$
of natural numbers, its code is the bit word $c(i_1)\,c(i_2) \cdots c(i_n)$, the concatenation of
the unary codes $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ of its entries; the empty sequence has the
empty code.

articles.title: Words of bits
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language over the disjoint union of $\alpha$
and the bits $\{\mathbf{t}, \mathbf{f}\}$ consisting of the words in which every symbol is a bit,
including the empty word.

articles.title: Codes of index sequences below $k$
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $\alpha$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the
language over the disjoint union of $\alpha$ and the bits $\{\mathbf{t}, \mathbf{f}\}$ consisting of
the bit words $c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$ with $n \ge 0$ and $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$, where
$c(j) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^j$ is the unary code of $j$. In particular it contains the empty
word.

articles.title: A word that does not start with $w$ leaves $w$ at some position
articles.statement:
Let $w$ and $x$ be words over an alphabet $\alpha$ such that $w$ is not a prefix of $x$. Then
there is a position $m < |w|$ with the following property: writing $w = u\,c\,r$ with $|u| = m$
and $c \in \alpha$, either $x = u$, or $x = u\,a\,y$ for some letter $a \ne c$ and some word $y$.

articles.title: A bit inside a word of letters followed by bits starts a suffix of the bits
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$
and $\beta$ be types, call the elements of $\alpha$ letters and those of $\beta$ bits, and regard
words over $\alpha$ and over $\beta$ as words over the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$. If
$u\,b\,z = X\,Y$ for words $u, z$ over $\alpha \oplus \beta$, a bit $b$, a word $X$ of letters and a
word $Y$ of bits, then there are words $Y_1, Y_2$ of bits with $Y = Y_1 Y_2$ and $b\,z = Y_2$.

articles.title: The universality grammar generates every word exactly when PCP has no solution
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and let $P$ be a list of dominoes over
$\alpha$. The universality grammar of $P$ generates every word over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$
if and only if the Post correspondence problem $P$ has no solution.

articles.title: The intended languages form a valuation of the universality grammar
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a
finite alphabet with decidable equality and let $P$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$. The
assignment of intended languages to the nonterminals of the universality grammar of $P$ is a
valuation of that grammar: for every production $A \to \gamma$, the language that $\gamma$ denotes
under the assignment is contained in the language assigned to $A$.

articles.title: The language of the universality grammar
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable
equality, let $P$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$ of length $m$, and for $i < m$ let $t_i$ and
$b_i$ be the top and bottom words of the domino of $P$ at position $i$, counting from $0$. Read the
bit $\mathrm{true}$ as the separator $|$ and the bit $\mathrm{false}$ as $1$, and let $c(i)$ be the
unary code of $i$: the bit $|$ followed by $i$ bits $1$. The language of the universality grammar
of $P$ equals the intended language of its start nonterminal $0$: a word over
$\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ belongs to it exactly when at least one of the following holds: it
consists of letters from $\alpha$ only (possibly none); it is a word of letters followed by a
nonempty word of bits whose first bit is $1$; some bit is immediately followed by a letter; it
contains $c(m)$ as a contiguous factor; or it equals $x\, c(i_n) \cdots c(i_1)$ for a word $x$
over $\alpha$ and indices $i_1, \dots, i_n < m$ with $n \ge 1$ such that
$x \ne t_{i_1} \cdots t_{i_n}$ or $x \ne b_{i_1} \cdots b_{i_n}$.

articles.title: Nonempty words of letters
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language of nonempty words of
letters is the set of all nonempty words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ whose symbols all lie
in $\alpha$, that is, the nonempty words over $\alpha$ viewed as words over
$\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$.

articles.title: Words of letters
articles.statement:
For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language of words of letters is the set of
all words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ whose symbols all lie in $\alpha$, that is, the words
over $\alpha$ (including the empty word) viewed as words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$.

articles.title: List language of a PCP instance
articles.statement:
Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{m-1})$ be a list of dominoes
over $\alpha$, let $s$ be a function sending each domino to a word over $\alpha$ (for instance its
top word), and write $w_i = s(d_i)$. The list language of $s$ and $P$ is the language over
$\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ of all words $w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}\, c(i_n) \cdots c(i_1)$ with
$n \ge 1$ and $i_1, \dots, i_n < m$, where $c(i)$ is the unary code of $i$: the bit
$\mathrm{true}$ followed by $i$ bits $\mathrm{false}$.

articles.title: List word of an index sequence
articles.statement:
Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{m-1})$ be a list of dominoes over
$\alpha$, let $s$ be a function sending each domino to a word over $\alpha$, and set
$w_i = s(d_i)$ for $i < m$ and $w_i = s(\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ for $i \ge m$, where
$(\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ is the domino with empty top and bottom. The list word of an index
sequence $i_1, \dots, i_n$ is the word $w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}\, c(i_n) \cdots c(i_1)$ over
$\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$, where $c(i)$ is the unary code of $i$: the bit $\mathrm{true}$
followed by $i$ bits $\mathrm{false}$.

articles.title: Malformed words
articles.statement:
Consider words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$, whose symbols are
letters from $\alpha$ and bits, and read the bit $\mathrm{true}$ as the separator $|$ and the bit
$\mathrm{false}$ as $1$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a word is malformed with bound $k$ when at least
one of the following holds: it consists of letters only (possibly none); it is a word of letters
followed by a nonempty word of bits whose first bit is $1$; some bit is immediately followed by a
letter; or it contains the block $|\,1^k$ (the bit $|$ followed by $k$ bits $1$) as a contiguous
factor.

articles.title: Every word is malformed or well formed
articles.statement:
Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $w$ be a word over
$\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$. Then $w$ is malformed with bound $k$, or
$w = x\, c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$ for a word $x$ over $\alpha$ and a nonempty sequence of indices
$j_1, \dots, j_n < k$, where $c(j)$ is the unary code of $j$: the bit $\mathrm{true}$ followed by
$j$ bits $\mathrm{false}$.

articles.title: The complement of PCP many-one reduces to universality of context-free grammars
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding. There
is a computable map sending each PCP instance $P$ (a list of dominoes over $\alpha$) to an
encoded context-free grammar $G_P$ over the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ (the letters
of $\alpha$ together with two bits) such that $P$ has no PCP solution if and only if $G_P$
generates every word over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$.

articles.title: Evaluating a form with one nonterminal
articles.statement:
Let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each
nonterminal. For terminal words $u$ and $v$, a nonterminal $A$ and a word $w$, the word $w$ lies
in the language that $V$ assigns to the sentential form $u\,A\,v$ if and only if $w = u z v$ for
some $z \in V(A)$.

articles.title: Evaluating a form with two nonterminals
articles.statement:
Let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each
nonterminal. For terminal words $u$, $v$ and $x$, nonterminals $A$ and $B$ and a word $w$, the
word $w$ lies in the language that $V$ assigns to the sentential form $u\,A\,v\,B\,x$ if and
only if $w = u z_1 v z_2 x$ for some $z_1 \in V(A)$ and $z_2 \in V(B)$.

articles.title: Membership in the mismatch productions
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a list of dominoes over a finite
alphabet with decidable equality, $A$ a nonterminal, $s$ a map from dominoes to words (in use, the
top or the bottom), $i < |P|$ an index, $w = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$, and
$\mathrm{code}(i)$ the unary code of $i$ as bits. Write letters and bits as terminals and $N_3$,
$N_4$, $N_7$ for the nonterminals $3$, $4$ and $7$. Each of the following encoded productions
belongs to the mismatch productions of $A$ for $s$ and $P$: $A \to w\,A\,\mathrm{code}(i)$;
$A \to w\,N_4\,\mathrm{code}(i)$; for each $m < |w|$, with $u$ the prefix of $w$ of length $m$,
$A \to u\,N_7\,\mathrm{code}(i)$; and, for each such $m$ and each letter $a$ different from the
letter of $w$ following $u$, $A \to u\,a\,N_3\,N_7\,\mathrm{code}(i)$.

articles.title: The mismatch language
articles.statement:
**The mismatch language** of one side of a list $P$ of dominoes. Let $s$ be a map from dominoes
to words (in use, the top or the bottom), write $w_i = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$
and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ for the unary code of $i$ as bits. The language, over letters and bits,
consists of the words $x\,\mathrm{code}(i_n) \cdots \mathrm{code}(i_1)$ where $x$ is a word of
letters and $i_1, \dots, i_n$ with $n \ge 1$ are indices below $|P|$ such that
$x \ne w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}$.

articles.title: Every mismatched word is derivable from the mismatch nonterminal
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a list of
dominoes over a finite alphabet, $s$ a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom),
$w_i = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$, and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ the unary code of $i$ as
bits. Let $A$ be a nonterminal such that every mismatch production of $A$ for $s$ and $P$ is a
production of the universality grammar of $P$. Then for every nonempty sequence
$i_1, \dots, i_n$ of indices below $|P|$ and every word $x$ of letters with
$x \ne w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}$, the word $x\,\mathrm{code}(i_n) \cdots \mathrm{code}(i_1)$ is
derivable from $A$ in the universality grammar of $P$.

articles.title: The mismatch productions
articles.statement:
**The mismatch productions** of a nonterminal $A$ for one side of a list $P$ of dominoes over a
finite alphabet. Let $s$ be a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). For each
index $i < |P|$ write $w = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$ and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ for
the unary code of $i$ as bits. With letters and bits as terminals and $N_3$, $N_4$, $N_7$ the
nonterminals $3$, $4$, $7$ (meant to generate words of letters, nonempty words of letters and
codes of indices), the productions are $A \to w\,A\,\mathrm{code}(i)$ and
$A \to w\,N_4\,\mathrm{code}(i)$, which peel $w$ off, and, for each proper prefix $u$ of $w$,
$A \to u\,N_7\,\mathrm{code}(i)$ and $A \to u\,a\,N_3\,N_7\,\mathrm{code}(i)$ for every letter $a$
other than the letter of $w$ following $u$, which stop matching.

articles.title: Malformed words are in no list language
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a list of dominoes and $s$ a map from
dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). Write the code of an index $i$ as the bits
$|\,1^i$, where $|$ stands for the bit true and $1$ for the bit false. A word over letters and
bits that is malformed with respect to $|P|$ (it has no bits, its first bit is a $1$, a bit is
followed by a letter, or it contains the factor $|\,1^{|P|}$) does not belong to the list
language of $s$ for $P$.

articles.title: Mismatched words are not in the list language
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a list of dominoes and $s$ a map
from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). No word of the mismatch language of $s$
for $P$ belongs to the list language of $s$ for $P$.

articles.title: The letters other than a given letter
articles.statement:
For a letter $a$ of a finite alphabet with decidable
equality, the list of all letters $b$ of the alphabet with $b \ne a$, in the order of a fixed
enumeration of the alphabet.

articles.title: A PCP instance is solvable exactly when its top and bottom list languages meet
articles.statement:
A list $P$
of dominoes has a PCP solution if and only if some word belongs both to the list language of the
top words of $P$ and to the list language of the bottom words of $P$.

articles.title: Encoded bit terminal
articles.statement:
For a type $\alpha$ and a bit $b$, the terminal $b$ of the alphabet
$\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar, that is, the element
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{inr}\, b)$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.

articles.title: Encoded letter terminal
articles.statement:
For a letter $a \in \alpha$, the terminal $a$ of the alphabet
$\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar, that is, the element
$\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{inl}\, a)$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.

articles.title: Encoded nonterminal
articles.statement:
For a type $\alpha$ and a natural number $A$, the nonterminal $A$ as a
symbol of an encoded grammar over the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$, that is, the element
$\mathrm{inl}\, A$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.

articles.title: The universality grammar
articles.statement:
For a finite alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a list
$P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the encoded context-free grammar over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$
with start nonterminal $0$ whose productions are the base productions for $k = |P|$, followed by
the mismatch productions of the top words of $P$ with nonterminal $1$, followed by the mismatch
productions of the bottom words of $P$ with nonterminal $2$.

Its language is the union of the complements of the top and bottom list languages of $P$.

articles.title: Intended languages of the nonterminals of the universality grammar
articles.statement:
For a list $P$ of
dominoes over $\alpha$, the assignment of a language over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ to each
natural number that sends $0$ to the union of the malformed language for $k = |P|$ and the
mismatch languages of the top words and of the bottom words of $P$; $1$ to the mismatch language
of the top words of $P$; $2$ to the mismatch language of the bottom words of $P$; $3$ to the words
of letters; $4$ to the nonempty words of letters; $5$ to the words of bits; $6$ to the set of all
words; $7$ to the codes of index sequences with all indices below $|P|$; and every other number
to the empty language.
